meaning: As the unwise act out of attachment to their work, Arjuna, so should the wise act, but without attachment, wishing for the welfare of the world.
lifeNote: Work as hard as anyone, but for a bigger reason than yourself.
actions: Give your full effort today and dedicate it to others' good.
Work beside someone and match their energy, minus the stress.
Choose one task today because it helps many people.

iast: na buddhibhedaṁ janayedajñānāṁ karmasaṅginām · joṣayetsarvakarmāṇi vidvān yuktaḥ samācaran
meaning: The wise should not unsettle the minds of the unwise who are attached to action. Working steadily themselves, they should encourage others in all their duties.
lifeNote: Do not shake someone's effort by looking down on it. Encourage people where they are.
actions: Encourage someone's effort today instead of correcting their method.
Avoid criticising someone who is trying their best.
Lead by working alongside someone rather than lecturing.

iast: prakṛteḥ kriyamāṇāni guṇaiḥ karmāṇi sarvaśaḥ · ahaṅkāravimūḍhātmā kartā'hamiti manyate
meaning: All actions are carried out by the qualities of nature. But one deluded by ego thinks, "I am the doer."
lifeNote: Many forces shape every result. Taking all the credit, or all the blame, misses the bigger picture.
actions: Share credit for one success today.
When something goes wrong, list the other factors involved before blaming yourself.
Notice one time today when ego says "I did this".

sanskrit: गुणा गुणेषु वर्तन्त इति मत्वा न सज्जते ॥
iast: tattvavittu mahābāho guṇakarmavibhāgayoḥ · guṇā guṇeṣu vartanta iti matvā na sajjate
meaning: But one who knows the truth about the qualities and their actions, mighty-armed one, sees that it is only qualities moving among qualities, and does not become attached.
lifeNote: Seeing life as a play of forces lets you act without taking everything personally.
words: of the divisions of qualities and actions
actions: When someone is rude today, see it as their mood, not a judgement of you.
Observe your own moods today as passing weather.
Let one irritation go by not taking it personally.

iast: prakṛterguṇasammūḍhāḥ sajjante guṇakarmasu · tānakṛtsnavido mandānkṛtsnavinna vicālayet
meaning: Those deluded by the qualities of nature become attached to their actions. One who knows the whole truth should not unsettle those whose understanding is partial.
lifeNote: Be patient with people who see less than you do. Understanding grows at its own pace.
words: to the actions of the qualities
actions: Be patient with someone who is still learning something you know.
Explain one thing gently instead of correcting harshly.
Remember a time you did not understand something you now know.

iast: mayi sarvāṇi karmāṇi saṁnyasyādhyātmacetasā · nirāśīrnirmamo bhūtvā yudhyasva vigatajvaraḥ
meaning: Surrendering all your actions to me, with your mind on the Self, free from expectation and possessiveness, fight without the fever of anxiety.
lifeNote: Handing over the results lets you work without the fever of worry.
words: with a mind on the Self
actions: Before a stressful task today, mentally hand over the outcome.
Work for one hour without checking for results.
When worry rises, say: I will do my part and let go of the rest.

iast: ye me matamidaṁ nityamanutiṣṭhanti mānavāḥ · śraddhāvanto'nasūyanto mucyante te'pi karmabhiḥ
meaning: Those who always follow this teaching of mine with faith and without finding fault are freed from the bondage of action.
lifeNote: Faith plus practice, without cynicism, is how teachings change lives.
actions: Practise one teaching from the Gita today without second-guessing it.
Drop one cynical thought about something good.
Keep going on a practice even if you do not see results yet.

iast: ye tvetadabhyasūyanto nānutiṣṭhanti me matam · sarvajñānavimūḍhāṁstānviddhi naṣṭānacetasaḥ
meaning: But those who find fault with this teaching and do not follow it are confused about all knowledge. Know them to be lost and without understanding.
lifeNote: Constant fault-finding closes the door to learning. Approach new ideas with openness first.
actions: Listen to one idea today without looking for flaws first.
Notice when you criticise something before understanding it.
Try a suggestion once before rejecting it.

sanskrit: प्रकृतिं यान्ति भूतानि निग्रहः किं करिष्यति ॥
iast: sadṛśaṁ ceṣṭate svasyāḥ prakṛterjñānavānapi · prakṛtiṁ yānti bhūtāni nigrahaḥ kiṁ kariṣyati
meaning: Even the wise act according to their own nature. All beings follow their nature; what can suppression achieve?
lifeNote: Fighting your nature exhausts you. Work with it, and guide it gently.
actions: Notice one strength of your nature and use it today.
Stop forcing yourself to be like someone else in one area.
Plan your hardest task for the time of day when you naturally work best.

iast: indriyasyendriyasyārthe rāgadveṣau vyavasthitau · tayorna vaśamāgacchettau hyasya paripanthinau
meaning: Attraction and aversion are rooted in every sense and its object. Do not fall under their control; they are obstacles on the path.
lifeNote: Likes and dislikes are natural, but they should not run your life.
actions: Do one thing you dislike today without complaining.
Skip one thing you crave today.
Notice how often likes and dislikes make your choices today.

iast: śreyānsvadharmo viguṇaḥ paradharmātsvanuṣṭhitāt · svadharme nidhanaṁ śreyaḥ paradharmo bhayāvahaḥ
meaning: It is better to do your own duty imperfectly than to do another's duty well. Even death in your own duty is better; another's path is full of danger.
lifeNote: Your path, done imperfectly, beats someone else's done perfectly. Stop comparing.
actions: Stop comparing your path with someone else's for one day.
Do your own work today, even imperfectly.
Write down what makes your path yours.

sanskrit: अथ केन प्रयुक्तोऽयं पापं चरति पूरुषः ।
iast: atha kena prayukto'yaṁ pāpaṁ carati pūruṣaḥ · anicchannapi vārṣṇeya balādiva niyojitaḥ
meaning: Arjuna said: Then what drives a person to do wrong, Krishna, even against their will, as if pushed by force?
lifeNote: Arjuna asks the question everyone asks: why do I do what I know I should not?
actions: Notice one habit you repeat even though you do not want to.
Write down what usually happens just before you do something you regret.
Be curious, not harsh, about one of your weaknesses today.

iast: kāma eṣa krodha eṣa rajoguṇasamudbhavaḥ · mahāśano mahāpāpmā viddhyenamiha vairiṇam
meaning: The Lord said: It is desire, it is anger, born of the quality of passion. It is all-devouring and the cause of great wrong. Know it as the enemy here.
lifeNote: Desire that is blocked turns into anger. Knowing this helps you catch both early.
words: born of the quality of passion
actions: When you feel angry today, ask: what did I want that I did not get?
Pause for ten breaths before acting on a strong desire.
Write down one recent anger and the desire behind it.

iast: dhūmenāvriyate vahniryathā''darśo malena ca · yatholbenāvṛto garbhastathā tenedamāvṛtam
meaning: As fire is covered by smoke, a mirror by dust, and an embryo by the womb, so is this knowledge covered by desire.
lifeNote: Your wisdom is still there under the dust. Clear it away gently and it shines again.
actions: Clean one physical space today as a sign of clearing your mind.
Spend five minutes in silence to let the dust settle.
Write down one thing that is clouding your judgement right now.

iast: āvṛtaṁ jñānametena jñānino nityavairiṇā · kāmarūpeṇa kaunteya duṣpūreṇānalena ca
meaning: The knowledge of even the wise is covered by this constant enemy in the form of desire, Arjuna, which is never satisfied and burns like fire.
lifeNote: Feeding a craving rarely satisfies it; it only grows. Notice when more is never enough.
actions: Notice one thing you keep wanting more of.
Choose "enough" once today.
Delay one craving by a day and see if it fades.

iast: indriyāṇi mano buddhirasyādhiṣṭhānamucyate · etairvimohayatyeṣa jñānamāvṛtya dehinam
meaning: The senses, the mind and the intellect are said to be its dwelling place. Through them, desire covers knowledge and deludes the embodied soul.
lifeNote: Desire works through your senses, thoughts and reasoning. Watch all three.
actions: Notice what you see, think and decide when a craving appears.
Change one environment cue that triggers a bad habit.
Question one excuse your mind makes for a craving.

iast: tasmāttvamindriyāṇyādau niyamya bharatarṣabha · pāpmānaṁ prajahi hyenaṁ jñānavijñānanāśanam
meaning: So first control your senses, best of the Bharatas, and destroy this sinful thing that ruins both knowledge and wisdom.
lifeNote: Start with what you can manage: what you see, eat and listen to. Big change begins with small control.
actions: Choose one sense habit to manage today: screens, food or noise.
Remove one temptation from your environment.
Keep one small promise to yourself today.

sanskrit: मनसस्तु परा बुद्धिर्यो बुद्धेः परतस्तु सः ॥
iast: indriyāṇi parāṇyāhurindriyebhyaḥ paraṁ manaḥ · manasastu parā buddhiryo buddheḥ paratastu saḥ
meaning: The senses are said to be higher than the body; the mind is higher than the senses; the intellect is higher than the mind; and higher than the intellect is the Self.
lifeNote: You are more than your senses, moods and thoughts. Lead from the highest part of you.
actions: When a mood takes over today, step back and let your wiser self decide.
Sit quietly and notice the one who is aware of your thoughts.
Make one decision today from your values, not your feelings.

iast: evaṁ buddheḥ paraṁ buddhvā saṁstabhyātmānamātmanā · jahi śatruṁ mahābāho kāmarūpaṁ durāsadam
meaning: Knowing the Self to be higher than the intellect, steady yourself by the Self, mighty-armed one, and conquer this enemy in the form of desire, so hard to overcome.
lifeNote: Chapter 3 ends with a call to master yourself. It is hard, and it is possible.
actions: Pick one habit you want to master and take the first step today.
Reflect on one teaching from Chapter 3 and live it this week.
Celebrate one small victory over yourself today.

iast: imaṁ vivasvate yogaṁ proktavānahamavyayam · vivasvān manave prāha manurikṣvākave'bravīt
meaning: Krishna said: I taught this imperishable yoga to Vivasvan, the sun. Vivasvan passed it to Manu, and Manu passed it to Ikshvaku.
lifeNote: Wisdom that lasts is handed from person to person. Someone took the trouble to teach you what you know.
actions: Thank one person who taught you something that still helps you.
Pass on one useful thing you know to someone younger.
Write down a lesson you would want to hand on.

sanskrit: स कालेनेह महता योगो नष्टः परन्तप ॥
iast: evaṁ paramparāprāptamimaṁ rājarṣayo viduḥ · sa kāleneha mahatā yogo naṣṭaḥ parantapa
meaning: Received this way, one teacher to the next, the saintly kings knew it. But over a long time this yoga was lost to the world.
lifeNote: Even good knowledge fades if nobody practises it. What is not lived is soon forgotten.
actions: Pick one good habit you have let slip and restart it today.
Practise something you learnt instead of only remembering it.
Notice which family values are fading and keep one alive.

sanskrit: स एवायं मया तेऽद्य योगः प्रोक्तः पुरातनः ।
भक्तोऽसि मे सखा चेति रहस्यं ह्येतदुत्तमम् ॥
iast: sa evāyaṁ mayā te'dya yogaḥ proktaḥ purātanaḥ · bhakto'si me sakhā ceti rahasyaṁ hyetaduttamam
meaning: That same ancient yoga I am teaching you today, because you are my devotee and my friend. It is a supreme secret.
lifeNote: The deepest lessons are shared in trust. Openness and friendship make you ready to learn.
actions: Ask a mentor you trust about something you truly struggle with.
Listen to advice from a friend without defending yourself.
Be the kind of friend someone can confide in.

sanskrit: अपरं भवतो जन्म परं जन्म विवस्वतः ।
iast: aparaṁ bhavato janma paraṁ janma vivasvataḥ · kathametadvijānīyāṁ tvamādau proktavāniti
meaning: Arjuna said: Your birth came later, and Vivasvan's long before. How am I to understand that you taught it in the beginning?
lifeNote: Arjuna asks honestly when something does not make sense. Questions are part of learning, not a lack of faith.
actions: Ask the question you have been too shy to ask.
Write down one thing you do not understand yet.
Welcome questions from others instead of brushing them off.

sanskrit: बहूनि मे व्यतीतानि जन्मानि तव चार्जुन ।
तान्यहं वेद सर्वाणि न त्वं वेत्थ परन्तप ॥
iast: bahūni me vyatītāni janmāni tava cārjuna · tānyahaṁ veda sarvāṇi na tvaṁ vettha parantapa
meaning: Krishna said: Many births of mine have passed, and of yours too, Arjuna. I know them all; you do not.
lifeNote: You are part of a much longer story than this moment. Today's trouble is one page, not the whole book.
actions: When something feels huge, ask how it will look in five years.
Remember one hard season that has already passed.
Take one slow breath before reacting to a setback today.

iast: ajo'pi sannavyayātmā bhūtānāmīśvaro'pi san · prakṛtiṁ svāmadhiṣṭhāya saṁbhavāmyātmamāyayā
meaning: Though I am unborn and unchanging, and the lord of all beings, I take charge of my own nature and appear by my own power.
lifeNote: Krishna chooses to show up in the world. Love is often shown by choosing to be present.
actions: Be fully present with one person today, phone away.
Show up for something you said you would attend.
Notice where you can step in to help instead of watching.

sanskrit: यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत ।
iast: yadā yadā hi dharmasya glānir bhavati bhārata · abhyutthānam adharmasya tadātmānaṁ sṛjāmy aham
meaning: Whenever goodness declines and wrong rises, Arjuna, I come forth.
lifeNote: When things go wrong around you, be the one who stands up for what is right.
actions: Stand up for someone who is being treated unfairly today.
Do one right thing today even if it is inconvenient.
Tell a child the story of a time someone helped you.

iast: paritrāṇāya sādhūnāṁ vināśāya ca duṣkṛtām · dharmasaṁsthāpanārthāya saṁbhavāmi yuge yuge
meaning: To protect the good, to end the work of wrongdoers and to re-establish dharma, I appear age after age.
lifeNote: Goodness is never left without help for long. You can be part of that help where you are.
actions: Stand up for one person who is being treated unfairly.
Do one small act that makes your home or team fairer.
Refuse to join in when people mock someone.

sanskrit: जन्म कर्म च मे दिव्यमेवं यो वेत्ति तत्त्वतः ।
त्यक्त्वा देहं पुनर्जन्म नैति मामेति सोऽर्जुन ॥
iast: janma karma ca me divyamevaṁ yo vetti tattvataḥ · tyaktvā dehaṁ punarjanma naiti māmeti so'rjuna
meaning: One who truly understands my divine birth and work is not born again after leaving the body. That person comes to me, Arjuna.
lifeNote: Understanding changes where you end up. What you truly grasp shapes the path you walk.
actions: Spend ten quiet minutes reflecting on what matters most to you.
Read one verse slowly and think about it through the day.
Ask yourself what you are really moving towards.

iast: vītarāgabhayakrodhā manmayā māmupāśritāḥ · bahavo jñānatapasā pūtā madbhāvamāgatāḥ
meaning: Free from attachment, fear and anger, absorbed in me and taking refuge in me, many people purified by knowledge have reached my nature.
lifeNote: Fear and anger lose their grip when you lean on something larger than yourself.
words: free from attachment, fear and anger
actions: When fear rises, name it and take three slow breaths.
Let go of one grudge you keep replaying.
Start your day with a short prayer or quiet intention.

sanskrit: ये यथा मां प्रपद्यन्ते तांस्तथैव भजाम्यहम् ।
iast: ye yathā māṁ prapadyante tāṁstathaiva bhajāmyaham · mama vartmānuvartante manuṣyāḥ pārtha sarvaśaḥ
meaning: However people approach me, so I receive them. In every way, Arjuna, people are following my path.
lifeNote: There are many honest ways towards the good. Respect the paths other people walk.
actions: Learn how a friend of another faith or view finds meaning.
Avoid mocking someone else's way of praying.
Notice what you get back mirrors what you put in.

sanskrit: काङ्क्षन्तः कर्मणां सिद्धिं यजन्त इह देवताः ।
क्षिप्रं हि मानुषे लोके सिद्धिर्भवति कर्मजा ॥
iast: kāṅkṣantaḥ karmaṇāṁ siddhiṁ yajanta iha devatāḥ · kṣipraṁ hi mānuṣe loke siddhirbhavati karmajā
meaning: Wanting success in their work, people here worship the gods, for in the human world success from action comes quickly.
lifeNote: Quick results are tempting. Ask whether you are chasing outcomes or growing as a person.
actions: Notice one goal you chase only for quick reward.
Add one long-term goal alongside your short-term ones.
Celebrate effort today, not only results.

iast: cāturvarṇyaṁ mayā sṛṣṭaṁ guṇakarmavibhāgaśaḥ · tasya kartāramapi māṁ viddhyakartāramavyayam
meaning: The four kinds of work were created by me according to people's qualities and actions. Though I made this order, know me as the unchanging non-doer.
lifeNote: Your nature and actions, not your birth, point to the work that fits you.
actions: List three things you are naturally good at.
Notice which work leaves you energised rather than drained.
Judge people by how they act, not where they come from.

sanskrit: न मां कर्माणि लिम्पन्ति न मे कर्मफले स्पृहा ।
इति मां योऽभिजानाति कर्मभिर्न स बध्यते ॥
iast: na māṁ karmāṇi limpanti na me karmaphale spṛhā · iti māṁ yo'bhijānāti karmabhirna sa badhyate
meaning: Actions do not stain me, and I have no craving for their fruit. Whoever knows me this way is not bound by actions.
lifeNote: Work without craving does not weigh you down. It is the clinging that ties you up.
actions: Finish one task today without checking how it was received.
Notice where craving for praise makes work heavier.
Do one kind thing anonymously.

sanskrit: एवं ज्ञात्वा कृतं कर्म पूर्वैरपि मुमुक्षुभिः ।
कुरु कर्मैव तस्मात्त्वं पूर्वैः पूर्वतरं कृतम् ॥
iast: evaṁ jñātvā kṛtaṁ karma pūrvairapi mumukṣubhiḥ · kuru karmaiva tasmāttvaṁ pūrvaiḥ pūrvataraṁ kṛtam
meaning: Knowing this, seekers of freedom in earlier times did their work. So you too should act, as the ancients did long ago.
lifeNote: Those you admire did not run from work; they changed how they worked.
actions: Learn how someone you admire handles daily duties.
Do today's main task in the spirit of a role model.
Stop waiting for perfect conditions to start.

iast: kiṁ karma kimakarmeti kavayo'pyatra mohitāḥ · tatte karma pravakṣyāmi yajjñātvā mokṣyase'śubhāt
meaning: What is action and what is inaction? Even the wise are confused here. I will explain action to you; knowing it, you will be freed from harm.
lifeNote: If even wise people find a question hard, it is fine that you do too. Stay curious.
actions: Think about one recent choice where doing nothing was itself a choice.
Ask an experienced person how they decide when to act.
Accept that some questions take time to understand.

sanskrit: कर्मणो ह्यपि बोद्धव्यं बोद्धव्यं च विकर्मणः ।
iast: karmaṇo hyapi boddhavyaṁ boddhavyaṁ ca vikarmaṇaḥ · akarmaṇaśca boddhavyaṁ gahanā karmaṇo gatiḥ
meaning: One must understand action, wrong action and inaction. The way of action is deep and hard to grasp.
lifeNote: Doing, not doing and doing wrong all have consequences. Think before you rush or stall.
actions: Before a big decision, ask what happens if you do nothing.
Name one action you regret and what it taught you.
Pause for one minute before replying when upset.

sanskrit: कर्मण्यकर्म यः पश्येदकर्मणि च कर्म यः ।
स बुद्धिमान् मनुष्येषु स युक्तः कृत्स्नकर्मकृत् ॥
iast: karmaṇyakarma yaḥ paśyedakarmaṇi ca karma yaḥ · sa buddhimān manuṣyeṣu sa yuktaḥ kṛtsnakarmakṛt
meaning: One who sees inaction in action and action in inaction is wise among people. Such a person is a yogi, even while doing all kinds of work.
lifeNote: A calm mind can work hard and stay still inside. And avoiding work is still an action with results.
actions: Do a busy task while keeping your breathing slow.
Notice where avoiding something is quietly shaping your life.
Find stillness for five minutes in the middle of a busy day.

iast: yasya sarve samārambhāḥ kāmasaṅkalpavarjitāḥ · jñānāgnidagdhakarmāṇaṁ tamāhuḥ paṇḍitaṁ budhāḥ
meaning: One whose every undertaking is free of selfish desire, whose actions are burnt in the fire of knowledge, is called wise by the learned.
lifeNote: When the 'what's in it for me' fades, action becomes clean and light.
words: free from selfish desire and plans
whose actions are burnt by the fire of knowledge
actions: Start one task today asking how it helps others.
Notice a selfish motive and set it aside for one action.
Help someone without mentioning it later.

iast: tyaktvā karmaphalāsaṅgaṁ nityatṛpto nirāśrayaḥ · karmaṇyabhipravṛtto'pi naiva kiñcitkaroti saḥ
meaning: Giving up attachment to results, always content and depending on nothing, such a person does nothing at all even while fully engaged in work.
lifeNote: Contentment lets you work hard without feeling crushed by it.
actions: Write three things you already have that you are grateful for.
Work hard on one task without checking for approval.
Notice when you depend on praise to feel okay.

iast: nirāśīryatacittātmā tyaktasarvaparigrahaḥ · śārīraṁ kevalaṁ karma kurvannāpnoti kilbiṣam
meaning: Without craving, with mind and self controlled, giving up possessiveness and acting only to keep the body going, one incurs no fault.
lifeNote: Owning less and wanting less leaves more room for peace.
actions: Give away one thing you no longer use.
Skip one unnecessary purchase this week.
Notice what you cling to and loosen your grip a little.

sanskrit: समः सिद्धावसिद्धौ च कृत्वापि न निबध्यते ॥
iast: yadṛcchālābhasantuṣṭo dvandvātīto vimatsaraḥ · samaḥ siddhāvasiddhau ca kṛtvāpi na nibadhyate
meaning: Content with whatever comes, beyond pairs of opposites, free from envy and even in success and failure, such a person is not bound even while acting.
lifeNote: Envy steals joy. Contentment gives it back.
actions: Congratulate someone sincerely on their success.
Notice envy and turn it into one practical goal.
Treat today's result, good or bad, with the same calm.

iast: gatasaṅgasya muktasya jñānāvasthitacetasaḥ · yajñāyācarataḥ karma samagraṁ pravilīyate
meaning: For one who is unattached and free, whose mind rests in knowledge and who acts as an offering, all action dissolves completely.
lifeNote: Work done as an offering leaves no heavy residue behind.
words: whose mind is set in knowledge
actions: Dedicate today's work to someone you love.
Finish one task, then let it go without replaying it.
Treat a chore as a gift to your family.

iast: brahmārpaṇaṁ brahmahavirbrahmāgnau brahmaṇā hutam · brahmaiva tena gantavyaṁ brahmakarmasamādhinā
meaning: The offering is Brahman, the oblation is Brahman, offered by Brahman into the fire of Brahman. One absorbed in Brahman in all action reaches Brahman alone.
lifeNote: Seeing the sacred in everyday acts, even eating, turns ordinary life into worship.
actions: Say this verse or a short thanks before a meal.
Eat one meal slowly, without screens.
See one routine task today as an offering.

iast: daivamevāpare yajñaṁ yoginaḥ paryupāsate · brahmāgnāvapare yajñaṁ yajñenaivopajuhvati
meaning: Some yogis offer sacrifice to the gods. Others offer the self as sacrifice into the fire of Brahman.
lifeNote: People worship and serve in different ways. Each sincere way counts.
actions: Learn about one form of worship different from yours.
Choose one way you will serve this week.
Respect how your elders practise their faith.

iast: śrotrādīnīndriyāṇyanye saṁyamāgniṣu juhvati · śabdādīnviṣayānanya indriyāgniṣu juhvati
meaning: Some offer hearing and the other senses into the fires of restraint. Others offer sound and other sense objects into the fires of the senses.
lifeNote: Restraint can be a gift you give yourself, not a punishment.
words: in the fires of the senses
actions: Take one hour today without music or videos.
Notice one craving and let it pass without acting.
Choose what you listen to today with care.

iast: sarvāṇīndriyakarmāṇi prāṇakarmāṇi cāpare · ātmasaṁyamayogāgnau juhvati jñānadīpite
meaning: Others offer all the actions of the senses and of the breath into the fire of self-control, lit by knowledge.
lifeNote: Self-control grows when you understand why it matters.
actions: Write one reason why a habit you want to build matters.
Practise five minutes of quiet breathing.
Catch yourself before one automatic reaction.

iast: dravyayajñāstapoyajñā yogayajñāstathāpare · svādhyāyajñānayajñāśca yatayaḥ saṁśitavratāḥ
meaning: Some offer wealth, some austerity, some the practice of yoga. Others, firm in their vows, offer study and knowledge.
lifeNote: Money, effort, practice and study can all be offered. Give what you have.
actions: Donate a small amount to a cause you trust.
Study for twenty focused minutes as an offering.
Keep one small promise you made to yourself.

iast: apāne juhvati prāṇa prāṇe'pānaṁ tathā'pare · prāṇāpānagatī ruddhvā prāṇāyāmaparāyaṇāḥ
meaning: Some offer the incoming breath into the outgoing, and the outgoing into the incoming. Restraining the flow of breath, they devote themselves to breath control.
lifeNote: Your breath is always with you, a simple tool to steady the mind.
actions: Breathe in for four counts and out for six, five times.
Take three slow breaths before an exam or meeting.
Notice your breathing when you feel anxious.

iast: apare niyatāhārāḥ prāṇānprāṇeṣu juhvati · sarve'pyete yajñavido yajñakṣapitakalmaṣāḥ
meaning: Others, regulating their food, offer the life breaths into the life breaths. All of these know sacrifice and are cleansed of faults through it.
lifeNote: Even eating with moderation can be a spiritual practice.
actions: Stop eating when you are comfortably full today.
Choose one healthy swap in your meals this week.
Eat at regular times for three days.

iast: yajñaśiṣṭāmṛtabhujo yānti brahma sanātanam · nāyaṁ loko'styayajñasya kuto'nyaḥ kurusattama
meaning: Those who eat the nectar left after sacrifice reach the eternal Brahman. Without sacrifice, even this world is not yours, let alone the next.
lifeNote: Life works through giving. Someone who only takes ends up with less, not more.
words: eating the nectar left from sacrifice
for one who does not sacrifice
actions: Share some of your food or time with someone today.
Cook or serve others before serving yourself once.
Notice one way you only take and change it.

sanskrit: एवं बहुविधा यज्ञा वितता ब्रह्मणो मुखे ।
iast: evaṁ bahuvidhā yajñā vitatā brahmaṇo mukhe · karmajānviddhi tānsarvānevaṁ jñātvā vimokṣyase
meaning: Many kinds of sacrifice are spread before Brahman. Know that they are all born of action; knowing this you will be freed.
lifeNote: Every form of giving still asks you to act. Faith shows up in deeds.
actions: Turn one good intention into an action today.
Pick one form of service that suits you and start.
Notice that kindness is something you do, not only feel.

iast: śreyāndravyamayādyajñājjñānayajñaḥ parantapa · sarvaṁ karmākhilaṁ pārtha jñāne parisamāpyate
meaning: The sacrifice of knowledge is better than any material sacrifice. All action, without exception, finds its completion in knowledge.
lifeNote: Understanding is the deepest gift. Learning why you act completes the action.
actions: Learn the meaning behind one ritual you follow.
Teach someone a concept you understand well.
Spend time on understanding, not only memorising.

iast: tadviddhi praṇipātena paripraśnena sevayā · upadekṣyanti te jñānaṁ jñāninastattvadarśinaḥ
meaning: Learn this by approaching the wise with humility, asking sincere questions and serving them. Those who have seen the truth will teach you.
lifeNote: Humility, curiosity and service open the door to real teachers.
actions: Ask a teacher one thoughtful question this week.
Help a mentor with something before asking for help.
Listen fully before you disagree.

iast: yajjñātvā na punarmohamevaṁ yāsyasi pāṇḍava · yena bhūtānyaśeṣeṇa drakṣyasyātmanyatho mayi
meaning: Knowing this, Arjuna, you will not fall into confusion again. By it you will see all beings in yourself, and in me.
lifeNote: When you see others as part of yourself, kindness becomes natural.
actions: Treat a stranger today as you would a family member.
Notice what you share with someone you dislike.
Write down one moment you felt connected to everyone.

iast: api cedasi pāpebhyaḥ sarvebhyaḥ pāpakṛttamaḥ · sarvaṁ jñānaplavenaiva vṛjinaṁ santariṣyasi
meaning: Even if you were the worst of all wrongdoers, you would cross over all wrongdoing in the boat of knowledge.
lifeNote: No past is too heavy to begin again. Understanding can carry you across.
actions: Forgive yourself for one past mistake and write what you learnt.
Make one small amends you have been avoiding.
Remind yourself that change starts today.

iast: yathaidhāṁsi samiddho'gnirbhasmasātkurute'rjuna · jñānāgniḥ sarvakarmāṇi bhasmasātkurute tathā
meaning: As a blazing fire turns firewood to ashes, Arjuna, so the fire of knowledge turns all actions to ashes.
lifeNote: Real understanding burns away old patterns that once bound you.
actions: Identify one old habit and learn what triggers it.
Write down a lesson that ended a past mistake.
Replace one unhelpful pattern with a new action today.

sanskrit: न हि ज्ञानेन सदृशं पवित्रमिह विद्यते ।
iast: na hi jñānena sadṛśaṁ pavitramiha vidyate · tatsvayaṁ yogasaṁsiddhaḥ kālenātmani vindati
meaning: Nothing here purifies like knowledge. One perfected in yoga finds it in oneself, in time.
lifeNote: Wisdom grows inside you with patient practice; give it time.
actions: Practise one skill daily for a week without judging progress.
Be patient with yourself while learning something hard.
Reflect for five minutes on what you learnt today.

iast: śraddhāvām̐llabhate jñānaṁ tatparaḥ saṁyatendriyaḥ · jñānaṁ labdhvā parāṁ śāntimacireṇādhigacchati
meaning: One with faith, devoted and with senses controlled, gains knowledge. Having gained it, that person soon reaches supreme peace.
lifeNote: Trust, focus and self-discipline together lead to learning, and learning leads to peace.
actions: Study one subject with full focus and phone away.
Trust your preparation on the day of a test.
Keep one small daily discipline for a week.

sanskrit: नायं लोकोऽस्ति न परो न सुखं संशयात्मनः ॥
iast: ajñaścāśraddadhānaśca saṁśayātmā vinaśyati · nāyaṁ loko'sti na paro na sukhaṁ saṁśayātmanaḥ
meaning: One who is ignorant, without faith and full of doubt is lost. For the doubter there is neither this world, nor the next, nor happiness.
lifeNote: Constant doubt freezes you. At some point you must trust and move.
actions: Make one decision today you have been doubting for long.
Set a time limit for weighing options, then choose.
Ask one trusted person and then act on their advice.

iast: yogasaṁnyastakarmāṇaṁ jñānasaṁchinnasaṁśayam · ātmavantaṁ na karmāṇi nibadhnanti dhanañjaya
meaning: One who has offered all action through yoga, whose doubts are cut by knowledge and who is self-possessed, is not bound by actions, Arjuna.
lifeNote: Clear understanding and a steady self free you to act without fear.
words: who has renounced action through yoga
whose doubts are cut by knowledge
actions: Write down a doubt and the facts that answer it.
Act on one decision with full commitment today.
Notice how much lighter work feels without second-guessing.

iast: tasmādajñānasaṁbhūtaṁ hṛtsthaṁ jñānāsinā''tmanaḥ · chittvainaṁ saṁśayaṁ yogamātiṣṭhottiṣṭha bhārata
meaning: So, with the sword of knowledge, cut away this doubt in your heart that is born of ignorance. Take up yoga and stand up, Arjuna.
lifeNote: After understanding comes action. Cut the doubt, then stand up and do your part.
actions: Stand up and start the task you have been doubting.
Say out loud: I am ready, and begin.
Cut one excuse from your vocabulary this week.

sanskrit: संन्यासं कर्मणां कृष्ण पुनर्योगं च शंससि ।
iast: saṁnyāsaṁ karmaṇāṁ kṛṣṇa punaryogaṁ ca śaṁsasi · yacchreya etayorekaṁ tanme brūhi suniścitam
meaning: Arjuna said: Krishna, you praise giving up action, and then again you praise the yoga of action. Tell me for certain which one of the two is better.
lifeNote: When advice seems to point two ways, ask for a clear answer instead of guessing.
actions: Write down two options you are torn between and ask someone you trust.
Ask for one clear next step when advice feels mixed.
Pick one option today rather than staying stuck.

iast: saṁnyāsaḥ karmayogaśca niḥśreyasakarāvubhau · tayostu karmasaṁnyāsātkarmayogo viśiṣyate
meaning: Krishna said: Renunciation and the yoga of action both lead to the highest good. But of the two, the yoga of action is better than giving up action.
lifeNote: Running away from duty is not the same as being free. Doing your work with a free mind is the better road.
actions: Stay with a hard task instead of quitting it today.
Change your attitude to one chore instead of avoiding it.
Notice where quitting would only be escape.

sanskrit: ज्ञेयः स नित्यसंन्यासी यो न द्वेष्टि न काङ्क्षति ।
iast: jñeyaḥ sa nityasaṁnyāsī yo na dveṣṭi na kāṅkṣati · nirdvandvo hi mahābāho sukhaṁ bandhātpramucyate
meaning: Know that one who neither hates nor craves is always a renunciate. Free from the pull of opposites, that person is easily freed from bondage.
lifeNote: Freedom is less about where you live and more about what you hate and crave.
actions: Notice one dislike that controls your mood and soften it.
Let one craving pass today without feeding it.
Practise calm towards someone who annoys you.

iast: sāṁkhyayogau pṛthagbālāḥ pravadanti na paṇḍitāḥ · ekamapyāsthitaḥ samyagubhayorvindate phalam
meaning: Only the immature say the path of knowledge and the path of action are different, not the wise. Practise either one properly and you gain the fruit of both.
lifeNote: Thinkers and doers are not rivals. Done fully, either path leads home.
actions: Respect a friend whose strengths differ from yours.
Go deep in one path instead of switching constantly.
Stop arguing over which way is 'right' and practise yours.

sanskrit: एकं सांख्यं च योगं च यः पश्यति स पश्यति ॥
iast: yatsāṁkhyaiḥ prāpyate sthānaṁ tadyogairapi gamyate · ekaṁ sāṁkhyaṁ ca yogaṁ ca yaḥ paśyati sa paśyati
meaning: The state reached by the path of knowledge is reached by the path of action too. One who sees knowledge and action as one truly sees.
lifeNote: Different roads can lead to the same summit. Seeing that is real understanding.
actions: Find what you share with someone who works differently.
Combine study and practice in one skill today.
Avoid looking down on paths you have not chosen.

iast: saṁnyāsastu mahābāho duḥkhamāptumayogataḥ · yogayukto munirbrahma nacireṇādhigacchati
meaning: Renunciation is hard to reach without the yoga of action. The sage who practises it soon reaches Brahman.
lifeNote: Letting go is learnt by doing, not by deciding to stop doing.
actions: Practise letting go in small daily tasks.
Do your duty fully before thinking of stepping back.
Learn detachment through one real responsibility.

iast: yogayukto viśuddhātmā vijitātmā jitendriyaḥ · sarvabhūtātmabhūtātmā kurvannapi na lipyate
meaning: Engaged in yoga, pure in heart, master of self and senses, seeing his own self in all beings, such a person is not tainted even while acting.
lifeNote: When you feel others as yourself, your actions stay clean.
words: seeing his self in all beings
actions: Before acting, ask how it would feel if done to you.
Treat a colleague's problem as if it were your own.
Keep one sense habit in check today.

iast: naiva kiṁcitkaromīti yukto manyeta tattvavit · paśyan śṛṇvanspṛśañjighrannaśnangacchansvapan śvasan
meaning: One steady in yoga who knows the truth thinks, 'I do nothing at all,' while seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, eating, walking, sleeping and breathing.
lifeNote: Much of life simply happens through you. Holding it lightly eases the ego.
actions: Notice how your breath happens without effort.
Drop 'I did it all' thinking for one success today.
Take a walk and simply observe.

iast: pralapanvisṛjangṛhṇannunmiṣannimiṣannapi · indriyāṇīndriyārtheṣu vartanta iti dhārayan
meaning: Speaking, letting go, taking, opening and closing the eyes, such a person understands that it is only the senses moving among their objects.
lifeNote: You are more than your senses. Watching them work gives you a little space to choose.
actions: When angry, notice the sensations before reacting.
Close your eyes for one minute and just notice.
Say less and listen more in one conversation.

sanskrit: ब्रह्मण्याधाय कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा करोति यः ।
iast: brahmaṇyādhāya karmāṇi saṅgaṁ tyaktvā karoti yaḥ · lipyate na sa pāpena padmapatramivāmbhasā
meaning: One who acts, offering all actions to Brahman and giving up attachment, is not touched by wrong, as a lotus leaf is not wet by water.
lifeNote: Like a lotus leaf, you can live in the world without being soaked by it.
actions: Do your work fully, then let the result roll off.
Do not take one criticism personally today.
Picture a lotus leaf when gossip comes your way.

iast: kāyena manasā buddhyā kevalairindriyairapi · yoginaḥ karma kurvanti saṅgaṁ tyaktvā''tmaśuddhaye
meaning: With body, mind, intellect and senses alone, yogis act without attachment, for the purification of the self.
lifeNote: Work can clean the heart when done without clinging.
actions: Do one physical task mindfully as self-practice.
Use your work today to grow patience.
Notice how serving others makes you feel lighter.

iast: yuktaḥ karmaphalaṁ tyaktvā śāntimāpnoti naiṣṭhikīm · ayuktaḥ kāmakāreṇa phale sakto nibadhyate
meaning: The steady person gives up the fruit of action and gains lasting peace. The unsteady, driven by desire and attached to results, is bound.
lifeNote: Peace comes from how you relate to results, not from getting them.
actions: After an exam or project, let the result go for the evening.
Notice when worry about results is spoiling your work.
Write one sentence of peace before sleeping.

sanskrit: नवद्वारे पुरे देही नैव कुर्वन्न कारयन् ॥
iast: sarvakarmāṇi manasā saṁnyasyāste sukhaṁ vaśī · navadvāre pure dehī naiva kurvanna kārayan
meaning: Renouncing all actions with the mind, the self-controlled person rests happily in the city of nine gates, the body, neither acting nor causing action.
lifeNote: The body is a home you live in, not the whole of who you are.
actions: Sit quietly for five minutes and feel at home in your body.
Treat your body with care today: water, rest, movement.
Let one worry go while sitting still.

sanskrit: न कर्तृत्वं न कर्माणि लोकस्य सृजति प्रभुः ।
iast: na kartṛtvaṁ na karmāṇi lokasya sṛjati prabhuḥ · na karmaphalasaṁyogaṁ svabhāvastu pravartate
meaning: The Lord does not create doership or actions for people, nor the link between action and result. It is nature that is at work.
lifeNote: Do not blame God for your choices; nature and habit drive much of what you do.
actions: Take responsibility for one choice you have been blaming on fate.
Notice one habit that runs on autopilot.
Change one small routine that leads you astray.

sanskrit: नादत्ते कस्यचित्पापं न चैव सुकृतं विभुः ।
iast: nādatte kasyacitpāpaṁ na caiva sukṛtaṁ vibhuḥ · ajñānenāvṛtaṁ jñānaṁ tena muhyanti jantavaḥ
meaning: The all-pervading one takes on no one's wrongdoing or good deeds. Knowledge is covered by ignorance, and so beings are deluded.
lifeNote: Confusion comes from a covered understanding, not from being bad.
actions: When confused, look for what you may not know yet.
Be kind to people who act from ignorance.
Read something that clears up a confusion.

iast: jñānena tu tadajñānaṁ yeṣāṁ nāśitamātmanaḥ · teṣāmādityavajjñānaṁ prakāśayati tatparam
meaning: But for those whose ignorance is destroyed by knowledge of the self, that knowledge shines like the sun and reveals the supreme.
lifeNote: Understanding works like sunrise: once it comes, the dark simply goes.
actions: Study the one topic you fear most for twenty minutes.
Explain a difficult idea in your own words.
Watch a sunrise and think about what you want to understand.

iast: tadbuddhayastadātmānastanniṣṭhāstatparāyaṇāḥ · gacchantyapunarāvṛttiṁ jñānanirdhūtakalmaṣāḥ
meaning: With intellect, self, devotion and goal fixed on that, their faults cleansed by knowledge, they go where there is no return.
lifeNote: When your thinking, heart and goals point the same way, you move with power.
actions: Write one goal and check that your habits support it.
Remove one distraction that pulls against your goal.
Spend ten minutes on what matters most first.

sanskrit: शुनि चैव श्वपाके च पण्डिताः समदर्शिनः ॥
iast: vidyāvinayasaṁpanne brāhmaṇe gavi hastini · śuni caiva śvapāke ca paṇḍitāḥ samadarśinaḥ
meaning: The wise see with an equal eye a learned and humble priest, a cow, an elephant, a dog and an outcaste.
lifeNote: Real wisdom sees the same life in everyone, without ranking people.
actions: Greet the cleaner or guard with the same respect as your boss.
Be gentle with an animal today.
Catch one moment where you judge someone by status.

sanskrit: इहैव तैर्जितः सर्गो येषां साम्ये स्थितं मनः ।
निर्दोषं हि समं ब्रह्म तस्माद्ब्रह्मणि ते स्थिताः ॥
iast: ihaiva tairjitaḥ sargo yeṣāṁ sāmye sthitaṁ manaḥ · nirdoṣaṁ hi samaṁ brahma tasmādbrahmaṇi te sthitāḥ
meaning: Those whose mind rests in equality have conquered the cycle of birth even here. Brahman is flawless and equal, so they abide in Brahman.
lifeNote: An equal mind is already free. You do not have to wait for some later reward.
actions: Treat praise and blame the same way today.
Speak to everyone in a meeting with equal respect.
Notice one bias and set it aside.

iast: na prahṛṣyetpriyaṁ prāpya nodvijetprāpya cāpriyam · sthirabuddhirasammūḍho brahmavidbrahmaṇi sthitaḥ
meaning: One who does not rejoice too much at the pleasant or become upset at the unpleasant, steady and clear, knows Brahman and rests in Brahman.
lifeNote: Do not ride every wave of good and bad news. A steady mind is a strong one.
actions: Respond to good news calmly today, without boasting.
Respond to bad news with one slow breath before reacting.
Keep a steady routine through a busy week.

iast: bāhyasparśeṣvasaktātmā vindatyātmani yatsukham · sa brahmayogayuktātmā sukhamakṣayamaśnute
meaning: Unattached to outer pleasures, one finds happiness within. United with Brahman in yoga, that person enjoys endless happiness.
lifeNote: The happiest joy does not depend on things outside you.
actions: Spend an evening without shopping or scrolling.
Find one joy today that costs nothing.
Sit with yourself quietly before sleeping.

sanskrit: ये हि संस्पर्शजा भोगा दुःखयोनय एव ते ।
आद्यन्तवन्तः कौन्तेय न तेषु रमते बुधः ॥
iast: ye hi saṁsparśajā bhogā duḥkhayonaya eva te · ādyantavantaḥ kaunteya na teṣu ramate budhaḥ
meaning: Pleasures born of contact with sense objects are sources of pain; they have a beginning and an end. The wise do not delight in them.
lifeNote: Quick pleasures end, and often leave a hangover. Choose joys that last.
actions: Notice how you feel an hour after a quick pleasure.
Swap one cheap thrill for a meaningful activity.
Choose rest over binge-watching tonight.

sanskrit: कामक्रोधोद्भवं वेगं स युक्तः स सुखी नरः ॥
iast: śaknotīhaiva yaḥ soḍhuṁ prākśarīravimokṣaṇāt · kāmakrodhodbhavaṁ vegaṁ sa yuktaḥ sa sukhī naraḥ
meaning: One who can withstand the force of desire and anger here, before leaving the body, is a yogi and a happy person.
lifeNote: The urge to snap or grab passes if you can ride it out for a few breaths.
actions: Count to ten before replying when angry.
Wait ten minutes before acting on a strong craving.
Notice the urge rise and fall like a wave.

iast: yo'ntaḥsukho'ntarārāmastathāntarjyotireva yaḥ · sa yogī brahmanirvāṇaṁ brahmabhūto'dhigacchati
meaning: One who is happy within, rejoices within and is lit from within, that yogi becomes one with Brahman and attains liberation in Brahman.
lifeNote: Build a source of joy inside you that no one can take away.
actions: Do one thing purely because you love it.
Start your day with five quiet minutes.
Notice inner calm when nothing outside is going right.

iast: labhante brahmanirvāṇamṛṣayaḥ kṣīṇakalmaṣāḥ · chinnadvaidhā yatātmānaḥ sarvabhūtahite ratāḥ
meaning: Sages whose faults are gone, whose doubts are cut, who are self-controlled and devoted to the welfare of all beings attain liberation in Brahman.
lifeNote: Caring for the good of all is part of the path to inner freedom.
words: in the welfare of all beings
actions: Do one thing today for the good of your neighbourhood.
Support a cause that helps people you will never meet.
Ask how a decision affects everyone, not only you.

iast: kāmakrodhaviyuktānāṁ yatīnāṁ yatacetasām · abhito brahmanirvāṇaṁ vartate viditātmanām
meaning: For the disciplined who are free of desire and anger, whose minds are controlled and who know the self, liberation in Brahman is all around them.
lifeNote: Peace is closer than you think once desire and anger calm down.
words: of those free from desire and anger
of those who know the self
actions: Notice how peaceful you feel after letting go of anger.
Keep a calm mind through one irritating situation.
Write what anger costs you each week.

iast: sparśānkṛtvā bahirbāhyāṁścakṣuścaivāntare bhruvoḥ · prāṇāpānau samau kṛtvā nāsābhyantaracāriṇau
meaning: Shutting out external contacts, fixing the gaze between the eyebrows and making the in-breath and out-breath equal as they move within the nostrils...
lifeNote: Simple meditation starts by closing the doors to distraction and evening out the breath.
actions: Close your eyes and breathe evenly for three minutes.
Silence notifications while you meditate.
Breathe in and out for the same count five times.

sanskrit: विगतेच्छाभयक्रोधो यः सदा मुक्त एव सः ॥
iast: yatendriyamanobuddhirmunirmokṣaparāyaṇaḥ · vigatecchābhayakrodho yaḥ sadā mukta eva saḥ
meaning: ...the sage who controls senses, mind and intellect, intent on freedom, without desire, fear and anger, is truly free for ever.
lifeNote: Desire, fear and anger are the three locks. Loosen them and you are already free.
words: with senses, mind and intellect controlled
free from desire, fear and anger
actions: Name today's main fear and one step to face it.
Let one desire go unfulfilled with a smile.
End the day by releasing any anger you carried.

iast: bhoktāraṁ yajñatapasāṁ sarvalokamaheśvaram · suhṛdaṁ sarvabhūtānāṁ jñātvā māṁ śāntimṛcchati
meaning: Knowing me as the receiver of all sacrifice and austerity, great lord of all worlds and the friend of all beings, one attains peace.
lifeNote: Knowing that the highest power is also your friend brings deep peace.
actions: When anxious, remember you are not alone.
Offer your effort today with trust.
Be a friend to someone who feels alone.

sanskrit: अनाश्रितः कर्मफलं कार्यं कर्म करोति यः ।
स संन्यासी च योगी च न निरग्निर्न चाक्रियः ॥
iast: anāśritaḥ karmaphalaṁ kāryaṁ karma karoti yaḥ · sa saṁnyāsī ca yogī ca na niragnirna cākriyaḥ
meaning: Krishna said: One who does the work that should be done without depending on its fruit is a renunciate and a yogi, not one who merely gives up rituals or stops acting.
lifeNote: Real renunciation is in the attitude, not in dropping your responsibilities.
actions: Do your next duty without asking what you'll get.
Do not use 'detachment' as an excuse to skip work.
Finish one unglamorous task fully.

sanskrit: यं संन्यासमिति प्राहुर्योगं तं विद्धि पाण्डव ।
iast: yaṁ saṁnyāsamiti prāhuryogaṁ taṁ viddhi pāṇḍava · na hyasaṁnyastasaṅkalpo yogī bhavati kaścana
meaning: What they call renunciation, know that to be yoga, Arjuna. No one becomes a yogi without giving up selfish intentions.
lifeNote: Letting go of selfish plans is where real practice begins.
actions: Notice one plan driven only by ego and drop it.
Make one decision today for the good of the team.
Ask 'who does this serve?' before starting a task.

iast: ārurukṣormuneryogaṁ karma kāraṇamucyate · yogārūḍhasya tasyaiva śamaḥ kāraṇamucyate
meaning: For the sage who wants to climb to yoga, action is the means. For one who has reached it, calm is the means.
lifeNote: Beginners grow through doing; the experienced grow through stillness. Both have their season.
words: for one who wants to climb
actions: If you're starting out, focus on steady daily practice.
If you've practised long, add quiet reflection.
Respect where you are on the path right now.

iast: yadā hi nendriyārtheṣu na karmasvanuṣajjate · sarvasaṅkalpasaṁnyāsī yogārūḍhastadocyate
meaning: When one is not attached to sense objects or to actions, and has given up all selfish intent, then that person is said to be established in yoga.
lifeNote: Being settled means you're not pulled around by every want and plan.
actions: Go through one day without buying anything non-essential.
Let a plan change without getting upset.
Notice one attachment and loosen it.

iast: uddhared ātmanātmānaṁ nātmānam avasādayet · ātmaiva hy ātmano bandhur ātmaiva ripur ātmanaḥ
meaning: Lift yourself by your own mind; do not let yourself fall. The mind alone is your friend, and the mind alone is your enemy.
lifeNote: Speak to yourself today the way you would speak to a friend you believe in.
actions: Replace one harsh thought about yourself with a fair one today.
Do one small thing you have been putting off.
Write one sentence of encouragement to your future self.

iast: bandhurātmā''tmanastasya yenātmaivātmanā jitaḥ · anātmanastu śatrutve vartetātmaiva śatruvat
meaning: For one who has mastered the self, the self is a friend. For one who has not, the self behaves like an enemy.
lifeNote: Your own mind can be your best friend or your worst critic. Training it decides which.
actions: Speak to yourself today the way a good friend would.
Notice one self-sabotaging thought and challenge it.
Keep one promise to yourself.

iast: jitātmanaḥ praśāntasya paramātmā samāhitaḥ · śītoṣṇasukhaduḥkheṣu tathā mānāpamānayoḥ
meaning: For one who has mastered the self and is calm, the supreme self stays steady in cold and heat, pleasure and pain, honour and dishonour.
lifeNote: Self-mastery makes you steady through weather, moods and opinions.
words: of one who has mastered himself
in cold and heat, pleasure and pain
actions: Stay calm through one uncomfortable situation today.
Respond to praise and criticism with the same thanks.
Notice how temporary today's discomforts are.

iast: jñānavijñānatṛptātmā kūṭastho vijitendriyaḥ · yukta ityucyate yogī samaloṣṭāśmakāñcanaḥ
meaning: Content in knowledge and wisdom, unshaken, with senses conquered, the yogi who sees a lump of earth, a stone and gold as equal is called steady.
lifeNote: Money and status lose their spell when you value what you understand.
words: seeing clod, stone and gold as equal
actions: Value a friendship above a possession today.
Notice when price changes how you feel about something.
Spend time learning instead of buying.

iast: suhṛnmitrāryudāsīnamadhyasthadveṣyabandhuṣu · sādhuṣvapi ca pāpeṣu samabuddhirviśiṣyate
meaning: One who has an equal mind towards well-wishers, friends, enemies, the neutral, mediators, the hateful, relatives, the good and wrongdoers alike stands out.
lifeNote: Treating people fairly, even those who dislike you, is a mark of real strength.
actions: Be polite to someone you find difficult.
Avoid gossip about an 'enemy' today.
Give fair credit to someone you don't like.

iast: yogī yuñjīta satatamātmānaṁ rahasi sthitaḥ · ekākī yatacittātmā nirāśīraparigrahaḥ
meaning: The yogi should practise constantly, staying alone in a quiet place, with mind and body controlled, free from craving and possessiveness.
lifeNote: Quiet time alone is not lonely; it is where the mind gets trained.
actions: Find ten minutes alone and quiet today.
Leave your phone in another room while sitting.
Make a small quiet corner at home.

iast: śucau deśe pratiṣṭhāpya sthiramāsanamātmanaḥ · nātyucchritaṁ nātinīcaṁ cailājinakuśottaram
meaning: In a clean place, set up a firm seat for yourself, neither too high nor too low, covered with kusha grass, a deerskin and a cloth.
lifeNote: A clean, simple, steady space helps the mind settle.
words: covered with cloth, skin and kusha grass
actions: Tidy your study or prayer space today.
Use the same seat for daily practice.
Remove clutter from one corner of your room.

iast: tatraikāgraṁ manaḥ kṛtvā yatacittendriyakriyaḥ · upaviśyāsane yuñjyādyogamātmaviśuddhaye
meaning: Sitting there with the mind one-pointed and thoughts and senses controlled, one should practise yoga to purify the self.
lifeNote: One-pointed attention is a skill. Small daily sittings build it.
actions: Focus on one task for 25 minutes without switching.
Sit for five minutes watching your breath.
Turn off notifications during study.

iast: samaṁ kāyaśirogrīvaṁ dhārayannacalaṁ sthiraḥ · saṁprekṣya nāsikāgraṁ svaṁ diśaścānavalokayan
meaning: Holding the body, head and neck straight and still, steady, gazing at the tip of the nose and not looking around...
lifeNote: Posture matters: a straight spine and a still gaze help a wandering mind.
words: at the tip of the nose
actions: Sit up straight for one study session.
Keep your gaze on one point while breathing slowly.
Check your posture every hour today.

sanskrit: मनः संयम्य मच्चित्तो युक्त आसीत मत्परः ॥
iast: praśāntātmā vigatabhīrbrahmacārivrate sthitaḥ · manaḥ saṁyamya maccitto yukta āsīta matparaḥ
meaning: ...calm, fearless and firm in self-restraint, controlling the mind and thinking of me, one should sit steady, with me as the highest goal.
lifeNote: Fearlessness and focus grow when the heart is fixed on what is highest.
actions: Hold one image or word of the divine in mind for a minute.
Name a fear and sit calmly with it.
Keep one simple vow of restraint this week.

iast: yuñjannevaṁ sadā''tmānaṁ yogī niyatamānasaḥ · śāntiṁ nirvāṇaparamāṁ matsaṁsthāmadhigacchati
meaning: Practising this way always, the yogi with a disciplined mind attains peace, the supreme liberation that abides in me.
lifeNote: Consistency, not intensity, brings lasting peace.
actions: Meditate at the same time for seven days.
Track a daily practice on a calendar.
Do a short practice even on busy days.

iast: nātyaśnatastu yogo'sti na caikāntamanaśnataḥ · na cātisvapnaśīlasya jāgrato naiva cārjuna
meaning: Yoga is not for one who eats too much or not at all, nor for one who sleeps too much or stays awake too much, Arjuna.
lifeNote: Extremes wear you out. Balanced food and sleep are spiritual practice too.
words: for one who eats too much
for one who does not eat
for one who sleeps too much
for one who stays awake too much
actions: Go to bed at a regular time tonight.
Avoid skipping meals before an exam.
Stop eating before you feel stuffed.

iast: yuktāhāravihārasya yuktaceṣṭasya karmasu · yuktasvapnāvabodhasya yogo bhavati duḥkhahā
meaning: For one who is moderate in eating and recreation, balanced in work, and regular in sleep and waking, yoga becomes the destroyer of sorrow.
lifeNote: A balanced routine is one of the simplest cures for unhappiness.
actions: Plan tomorrow with time for work, rest and play.
Take a short walk between work sessions.
Keep the same wake-up time all week.

iast: yadā viniyataṁ cittamātmanyevāvatiṣṭhate · niḥspṛhaḥ sarvakāmebhyo yukta ityucyate tadā
meaning: When the disciplined mind rests in the self alone, free from longing for all desires, one is said to be steady in yoga.
lifeNote: When the mind can rest without needing something new, you have found steadiness.
actions: Sit five minutes without wanting anything.
Notice the pull to check your phone and pause.
Be content with what you have for one evening.

sanskrit: यथा दीपो निवातस्थो नेङ्गते सोपमा स्मृता ।
iast: yathā dīpo nivātastho neṅgate sopamā smṛtā · yogino yatacittasya yuñjato yogamātmanaḥ
meaning: As a lamp in a windless place does not flicker: that is the image used for the controlled mind of a yogi practising meditation.
lifeNote: A focused mind is like a steady flame: calm, bright and unshaken.
actions: Light a lamp or candle and watch the flame for two minutes.
Shut out one 'wind' (noise, app) during study.
Picture a steady flame when anxious.

iast: yatroparamate cittaṁ niruddhaṁ yogasevayā · yatra caivātmanā''tmānaṁ paśyannātmani tuṣyati
meaning: Where the mind, restrained by practice, comes to rest; where, seeing the self by the self, one is content in the self...
lifeNote: Deep contentment is found inside, when the mind stops chasing.
actions: Sit still until your thoughts slow down.
Notice contentment when you stop scrolling.
Write down what made you quietly content today.

sanskrit: वेत्ति यत्र न चैवायं स्थितश्चलति तत्त्वतः ॥
iast: sukhamātyantikaṁ yattadbuddhigrāhyamatīndriyam · vetti yatra na caivāyaṁ sthitaścalati tattvataḥ
meaning: ...where one knows boundless happiness that is grasped by the intellect and lies beyond the senses; established there, one never moves from the truth.
lifeNote: The deepest joy is understood, not consumed.
actions: Notice a joy that came from understanding something.
Spend time on a hobby that deepens your mind.
Reflect on a moment you felt deeply settled.

sanskrit: यं लब्ध्वा चापरं लाभं मन्यते नाधिकं ततः ।
iast: yaṁ labdhvā cāparaṁ lābhaṁ manyate nādhikaṁ tataḥ · yasminsthito na duḥkhena guruṇāpi vicālyate
meaning: Having gained it, one thinks no other gain is greater. Established in it, one is not shaken even by heavy sorrow.
lifeNote: Find something worth more than any loss, and loss loses its power over you.
actions: Name what you value most, beyond money or status.
Lean on your deepest value during a hard moment.
Comfort someone in grief by simply staying near.

iast: taṁ vidyād duḥkhasaṁyogaviyogaṁ yogasaṁjñitam · sa niścayena yoktavyo yogo'nirviṇṇacetasā
meaning: Know that this separation from contact with sorrow is called yoga. It should be practised with determination and without discouragement.
lifeNote: Do not give up when practice feels slow. Determination is part of the practice.
actions: Practise today even if yesterday felt useless.
Write 'keep going' where you will see it.
Celebrate showing up, not perfection.

iast: saṅkalpaprabhavānkāmāṁstyaktvā sarvānaśeṣataḥ · manasaivendriyagrāmaṁ viniyamya samantataḥ
meaning: Giving up completely all desires born of mental planning, and restraining the senses on all sides with the mind...
lifeNote: Most cravings begin as a thought. Catch the thought and the craving weakens.
actions: Notice the first thought behind a craving.
Let one daydream go without acting on it.
Close distracting tabs before working.

sanskrit: आत्मसंस्थं मनः कृत्वा न किञ्चिदपि चिन्तयेत् ॥
iast: śanaiḥ śanairuparamed buddhyā dhṛtigṛhītayā · ātmasaṁsthaṁ manaḥ kṛtvā na kiñcidapi cintayet
meaning: ...one should become still slowly and gradually, with a firm intellect. Settling the mind in the self, one should think of nothing else.
lifeNote: Calm comes step by step. Be patient with your mind as you would with a child.
actions: Increase meditation by one minute this week.
Be gentle when your mind wanders, and simply return.
Slow down one daily activity on purpose.

iast: yato yato niścarati manaścañcalamasthiram · tatastato niyamyaitadātmanyeva vaśaṁ nayet
meaning: Wherever the restless, unsteady mind wanders, one should bring it back from there and settle it under the control of the self.
lifeNote: Wandering is normal. The practice is simply to come back, again and again.
actions: Each time you get distracted, return without scolding yourself.
Keep a note of where your mind wanders most.
Use a timer to bring your mind back to study.

iast: praśāntamanasaṁ hyenaṁ yoginaṁ sukhamuttamam · upaiti śāntarajasaṁ brahmabhūtamakalmaṣam
meaning: The highest happiness comes to the yogi whose mind is tranquil, whose passions are calmed, who is free from fault and one with Brahman.
lifeNote: Calm passion is the doorway to the best kind of happiness.
actions: Calm your mind before an important talk.
Notice the quiet joy after a peaceful hour.
Avoid stirring arguments today.

iast: yuñjannevaṁ sadā''tmānaṁ yogī vigatakalmaṣaḥ · sukhena brahmasaṁsparśamatyantaṁ sukhamaśnute
meaning: Practising this way always, the yogi free from faults easily enjoys the infinite happiness of contact with Brahman.
lifeNote: Regular practice makes peace feel natural rather than forced.
actions: Keep your daily practice short but regular.
Notice when calm comes more easily than before.
Thank yourself for staying consistent.

iast: sarvabhūtasthamātmānaṁ sarvabhūtāni cātmani · īkṣate yogayuktātmā sarvatra samadarśanaḥ
meaning: One united in yoga sees the self in all beings and all beings in the self, seeing the same everywhere.
lifeNote: When you see yourself in others, cruelty becomes impossible and kindness easy.
actions: Imagine yourself in the shoes of someone you disagree with.
Do one kind thing for someone very different from you.
Look at a crowd and remember each person feels like you do.

sanskrit: यो मां पश्यति सर्वत्र सर्वं च मयि पश्यति ।
तस्याहं न प्रणश्यामि स च मे न प्रणश्यति ॥
iast: yo māṁ paśyati sarvatra sarvaṁ ca mayi paśyati · tasyāhaṁ na praṇaśyāmi sa ca me na praṇaśyati
meaning: One who sees me everywhere and sees everything in me, I am never lost to that person, nor is that person ever lost to me.
lifeNote: Seeing the sacred everywhere means you are never truly alone.
actions: Look for one sign of goodness in an ordinary moment.
When lonely, remember this verse.
Offer a short thanks when you see beauty.

sanskrit: सर्वथा वर्तमानोऽपि स योगी मयि वर्तते ॥
iast: sarvabhūtasthitaṁ yo māṁ bhajatyekatvamāsthitaḥ · sarvathā vartamāno'pi sa yogī mayi vartate
meaning: The yogi who, established in oneness, worships me as dwelling in all beings lives in me, however he lives.
lifeNote: Serving people is a way of worshipping the divine in them.
actions: Serve someone today as if serving God.
See your daily work as worship.
Volunteer for an hour this month.

sanskrit: सुखं वा यदि वा दुःखं सः योगी परमो मतः ॥
iast: ātmaupamyena sarvatra samaṁ paśyati yo'rjuna · sukhaṁ vā yadi vā duḥkhaṁ saḥ yogī paramo mataḥ
meaning: One who, by comparison with oneself, sees the pleasure and pain of all beings as one's own, Arjuna, is considered the highest yogi.
lifeNote: Feel others' joy and pain as your own; that is the highest practice.
actions: Celebrate a friend's success as if it were yours.
Comfort someone in pain as you would want to be comforted.
Ask a quiet friend how they are really doing.

sanskrit: एतस्याहं न पश्यामि चञ्चलत्वात् स्थितिं स्थिराम् ॥
iast: yo'yaṁ yogastvayā proktaḥ sāmyena madhusūdana · etasyāhaṁ na paśyāmi cañcalatvāt sthitiṁ sthirām
meaning: Arjuna said: Krishna, this yoga of evenness you have taught, I do not see how it can last, because the mind is so restless.
lifeNote: It's honest to admit your mind is restless. Saying so is the start of training it.
actions: Admit one way your mind is restless right now.
Ask for help with focus instead of hiding the struggle.
Note how often you switch tasks in an hour.

sanskrit: चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्दृढम् ।
iast: cañcalaṁ hi manaḥ kṛṣṇa pramāthi balavaddṛḍham · tasyāhaṁ nigrahaṁ manye vāyoriva suduṣkaram
meaning: The mind is restless, turbulent, strong and stubborn, Krishna. I think controlling it is as hard as controlling the wind.
lifeNote: Everyone struggles with the mind, even great warriors. You are not alone in this.
actions: Write down three things that disturb your mind most.
Share your struggle with focus with a friend.
Start with controlling one small habit.

sanskrit: अभ्यासेन तु कौन्तेय वैराग्येण च गृह्यते ॥
iast: asaṁśayaṁ mahābāho mano durnigrahaṁ calaṁ · abhyāsena tu kaunteya vairāgyeṇa ca gṛhyate
meaning: Krishna said: Undoubtedly the mind is restless and hard to control, Arjuna. But it can be controlled by practice and detachment.
lifeNote: Practice and letting go: two simple tools that work on any mind.
actions: Practise focus daily for ten minutes, no matter what.
Let go of one distraction you are attached to.
Track practice days on a calendar.

sanskrit: असंयतात्मना योगो दुष्प्राप इति मे मतिः ।
iast: asaṁyatātmanā yogo duṣprāpa iti me matiḥ · vaśyātmanā tu yatatā śakyo'vāptumupāyataḥ
meaning: Yoga is hard for one without self-control; that is my view. But one who is self-controlled and strives by the right means can attain it.
lifeNote: Effort plus the right method works. Find a good method and keep at it.
actions: Learn one study technique that suits you.
Ask someone skilled how they practise.
Improve one method rather than only working harder.

sanskrit: अप्राप्य योगसंसिद्धिं कां गतिं कृष्ण गच्छति ॥
iast: ayatiḥ śraddhayopeto yogāccalitamānasaḥ · aprāpya yogasaṁsiddhiṁ kāṁ gatiṁ kṛṣṇa gacchati
meaning: Arjuna said: Krishna, what happens to someone who has faith but does not strive enough, whose mind wanders from yoga before reaching perfection?
lifeNote: Arjuna worries about failing halfway. Many of us share that fear.
actions: Name a goal you fear failing at and take one step anyway.
Remember that partial progress still counts.
Talk about a fear of failure with someone you trust.

iast: kaccinnobhayavibhraṣṭaśchinnābhramiva naśyati · apratiṣṭho mahābāho vimūḍho brahmaṇaḥ pathi
meaning: Fallen from both worldly and spiritual success, does he perish like a broken cloud, without support, confused on the path to Brahman?
lifeNote: The fear of 'losing both' can keep you from trying. Krishna's answer comes next.
actions: Notice where fear of losing stops you from trying.
Try something new with a small, safe first step.
Write what you would do if failure did not scare you.

iast: etanme saṁśayaṁ kṛṣṇa chettumarhasyaśeṣataḥ · tvadanyaḥ saṁśayasyāsya chettā na hyupapadyate
meaning: Krishna, please remove this doubt of mine completely. No one but you can remove it.
lifeNote: Take your deepest doubts to someone you truly trust.
actions: Bring one nagging doubt to a mentor this week.
Write your doubt clearly before asking.
Pray or reflect on a question that troubles you.

iast: pārtha naiveha nāmutra vināśastasya vidyate · nahi kalyāṇakṛtkaściddurgatiṁ tāta gacchati
meaning: Krishna said: Arjuna, there is no loss for such a person, here or hereafter. No one who does good ever comes to a bad end, my friend.
lifeNote: Good effort is never wasted, even if you stumble. This is one of the Gita's kindest promises.
actions: Remind yourself that no sincere effort is wasted.
Restart a good habit you dropped.
Encourage a friend who feels they've failed.

iast: prāpya puṇyakṛtāṁ lokānuṣitvā śāśvatīḥ samāḥ · śucīnāṁ śrīmatāṁ gehe yogabhraṣṭo'bhijāyate
meaning: One who falls from yoga reaches the worlds of the righteous, lives there many years, and is then born into a pure and prosperous home.
lifeNote: Your efforts carry forward; nothing good you do disappears.
actions: Value the good start your family gave you.
Build a home where good habits are easy.
Keep going with a practice even after a slip.

iast: athavā yogināmeva kule bhavati dhīmatām · etaddhi durlabhataraṁ loke janma yadīdṛśam
meaning: Or else he is born into a family of wise yogis. Such a birth is very rare in this world.
lifeNote: Being around wise people is a gift. Seek them out and value them.
actions: Spend time with someone wise this week.
Thank an elder who taught you good values.
Join a group that practises what you value.

sanskrit: यतते च ततो भूयः संसिद्धौ कुरुनन्दन ॥
iast: tatra taṁ buddhisaṁyogaṁ labhate paurvadehikam · yatate ca tato bhūyaḥ saṁsiddhau kurunandana
meaning: There he regains the understanding of his former life and strives again for perfection, Arjuna.
lifeNote: You pick up where you left off. Past effort gives you a head start.
actions: Return to a skill you once practised.
Notice how fast old learning comes back.
Build on yesterday's work instead of restarting from zero.

iast: pūrvābhyāsena tenaiva hriyate hyavaśo'pi saḥ · jijñāsurapi yogasya śabdabrahmātivartate
meaning: By that former practice he is carried along, even without trying. Even one who only seeks to know yoga goes beyond mere ritual.
lifeNote: Good habits build momentum that carries you on hard days.
actions: Build one habit strong enough to run on bad days.
Notice where old good habits still help you.
Look beyond rituals to their meaning.

iast: prayatnādyatamānastu yogī saṁśuddhakilbiṣaḥ · anekajanmasaṁsiddhastato yāti parāṁ gatim
meaning: The yogi who strives with great effort, cleansed of faults and perfected over many lives, then reaches the supreme goal.
lifeNote: Great things take long, patient effort. Keep going.
actions: Commit to one long-term goal for a year.
Celebrate progress, however slow.
Keep going after a setback.

iast: tapasvibhyo'dhiko yogī jñānibhyo'pi mato'dhikaḥ · karmibhyaścādhiko yogī tasmādyogī bhavārjuna
meaning: The yogi is greater than ascetics, greater even than scholars and those who perform rituals. So be a yogi, Arjuna.
lifeNote: Union with the divine matters more than any single practice. Aim for that.
actions: Remember why you practise, not just how.
Bring heart into a routine you do mechanically.
Choose one practice and do it wholeheartedly.

sanskrit: श्रद्धावान्भजते यो मां स मे युक्ततमो मतः ॥
iast: yogināmapi sarveṣāṁ madgatenāntarātmanā · śraddhāvānbhajate yo māṁ sa me yuktatamo mataḥ
meaning: And of all yogis, the one who worships me with faith, his inner self absorbed in me, I consider the most united with me.
lifeNote: Love and faith are the heart of every practice.
actions: Practise with love today, not just discipline.
Spend a few minutes in heartfelt prayer.
Offer a task to the divine with devotion.

sanskrit: असंशयं समग्रं मां यथा ज्ञास्यसि तच्छृणु ॥
iast: mayyāsaktamanāḥ pārtha yogaṁ yuñjanmadāśrayaḥ · asaṁśayaṁ samagraṁ māṁ yathā jñāsyasi tacchṛṇu
meaning: Krishna said: Hear, Arjuna, how, with your mind attached to me, practising yoga and taking refuge in me, you will know me fully and without doubt.
lifeNote: Real knowledge grows from both love and practice. Keep your heart in what you learn.
actions: Study something you love with full attention today.
Begin your practice with a moment of devotion.
Listen fully when someone wise speaks.

iast: jñānaṁ te'haṁ savijñānamidaṁ vakṣyāmyaśeṣataḥ · yajjñātvā neha bhūyo'nyajjñātavyamavaśiṣyate
meaning: I will teach you this knowledge completely, along with its realisation. Knowing it, nothing else here remains to be known.
lifeNote: Information is not enough; it has to become lived understanding.
actions: Put one thing you learnt today into practice.
Explain a concept by using an example from your life.
Revise by applying, not only rereading.

iast: manuṣyāṇāṁ sahasreṣu kaścidyatati siddhaye · yatatāmapi siddhānāṁ kaścinmāṁ vetti tattvataḥ
meaning: Among thousands of people, hardly one strives for perfection. And among those who strive and succeed, hardly one knows me in truth.
lifeNote: Deep understanding is rare. Do not be discouraged if few walk the path with you.
actions: Keep going on a path even if your friends aren't on it.
Find one person who shares your deeper goal.
Value depth over popularity.

sanskrit: भूमिरापोऽनलो वायुः खं मनो बुद्धिरेव च ।
iast: bhūmirāpo'nalo vāyuḥ khaṁ mano buddhireva ca · ahaṅkāra itīyaṁ me bhinnā prakṛtiraṣṭadhā
meaning: Earth, water, fire, air, space, mind, intellect and ego: this is my nature, divided eight ways.
lifeNote: Even your mind and ego are part of nature. You can watch them rather than be ruled by them.
actions: Notice your ego reacting today and smile at it.
Spend time outdoors with earth, water and sky.
Separate 'my thought' from 'me' once today.

iast: apareyamitastvanyāṁ prakṛtiṁ viddhi me parām · jīvabhūtāṁ mahābāho yayedaṁ dhāryate jagat
meaning: This is my lower nature. But know my other, higher nature too, Arjuna: the life within beings, by which this world is sustained.
lifeNote: Beyond body and mind there is life itself, which holds everything together.
actions: Feel your heartbeat for a minute and appreciate being alive.
Treat all living things as sharing the same life.
Care for a plant or animal today.

iast: etadyonīni bhūtāni sarvāṇītyupadhāraya · ahaṁ kṛtsnasya jagataḥ prabhavaḥ pralayastathā
meaning: Understand that all beings come from these two natures. I am the origin of the whole world and also its dissolution.
lifeNote: Everything begins and ends in the same source. That gives perspective on gains and losses.
actions: When something ends, remember it returns to its source.
Appreciate beginnings without fearing endings.
Reflect on where your life comes from.

sanskrit: मयि सर्वमिदं प्रोतं सूत्रे मणिगणा इव ॥
iast: mattaḥ parataraṁ nānyatkiñcidasti dhanañjaya · mayi sarvamidaṁ protaṁ sūtre maṇigaṇā iva
meaning: There is nothing higher than me, Arjuna. All this is strung on me like pearls on a thread.
lifeNote: Like a hidden thread holding pearls, one reality connects everything.
actions: Notice how your day's people and events connect.
Look for the common thread in different religions.
Wear or keep something that reminds you of this verse.

sanskrit: प्रणवः सर्ववेदेषु शब्दः खे पौरुषं नृषु ॥
iast: raso'hamapsu kaunteya prabhāsmi śaśisūryayoḥ · praṇavaḥ sarvavedeṣu śabdaḥ khe pauruṣaṁ nṛṣu
meaning: I am the taste in water, Arjuna, the light of the moon and sun, Om in all the Vedas, sound in space and strength in people.
lifeNote: The divine is in simple things: a sip of water, moonlight, a person's courage.
actions: Drink a glass of water slowly and with thanks.
Look at the moon or sun and remember this verse.
Chant Om three times today.

sanskrit: पुण्यो गन्धः पृथिव्यां च तेजश्चास्मि विभावसौ ।
iast: puṇyo gandhaḥ pṛthivyāṁ ca tejaścāsmi vibhāvasau · jīvanaṁ sarvabhūteṣu tapaścāsmi tapasviṣu
meaning: I am the pure fragrance of the earth and the brilliance in fire. I am the life in all beings and the discipline in those who practise it.
lifeNote: Discipline is sacred too. Your effort carries something divine.
actions: Smell the earth after rain or a flower today.
Honour your discipline as sacred, not a burden.
Light a lamp and reflect for a minute.

sanskrit: बीजं मां सर्वभूतानां विद्धि पार्थ सनातनम् ।
iast: bījaṁ māṁ sarvabhūtānāṁ viddhi pārtha sanātanam · buddhirbuddhimatāmasmi tejastejasvināmaham
meaning: Know me as the eternal seed of all beings, Arjuna. I am the intelligence of the intelligent and the radiance of the radiant.
lifeNote: Your intelligence and talents are gifts. Use them well, and with gratitude.
actions: Thank the source of your abilities before studying.
Use your talent today to help someone.
Avoid arrogance about your gifts.

iast: balaṁ balavatāṁ cāhaṁ kāmarāgavivarjitam · dharmāviruddho bhūteṣu kāmo'smi bharatarṣabha
meaning: I am the strength of the strong, free from craving and attachment. In beings, I am desire that does not go against dharma.
lifeNote: Desire itself isn't bad. Desire in harmony with what's right is sacred.
actions: Check whether one current desire is in line with your values.
Use your strength to protect, not to dominate.
Pursue one goal in an honest way.

sanskrit: ये चैव सात्त्विका भावा राजसास्तामसाश्च ये ।
मत्त एवेति तान्विद्धि नत्वहं तेषु ते मयि ॥
iast: ye caiva sāttvikā bhāvā rājasāstāmasāśca ye · matta eveti tānviddhi natvahaṁ teṣu te mayi
meaning: Know that all states of goodness, passion and inertia come from me alone. But I am not in them; they are in me.
lifeNote: Moods come and go within something steadier. You are not your mood.
actions: Label your mood today: calm, restless or dull.
Do something that brings out your calm side.
Remember a bad mood passes.

iast: tribhirguṇamayairbhāvairebhiḥ sarvamidaṁ jagat · mohitaṁ nābhijānāti māmebhyaḥ paramavyayam
meaning: Deluded by these three states born of the qualities, the whole world does not recognise me, who am beyond them and imperishable.
lifeNote: Caught up in moods and drives, people miss what is lasting.
actions: Take a moment each day to look past your moods.
Notice when you are acting from habit, not choice.
Spend time on something lasting rather than passing.

sanskrit: दैवी ह्येषा गुणमयी मम माया दुरत्यया ।
मामेव ये प्रपद्यन्ते मायामेतां तरन्ति ते ॥
iast: daivī hyeṣā guṇamayī mama māyā duratyayā · māmeva ye prapadyante māyāmetāṁ taranti te
meaning: This divine illusion of mine, made of the qualities, is hard to cross. But those who surrender to me alone cross over it.
lifeNote: You cannot out-think every illusion alone. Surrender and trust help you cross.
actions: Hand one worry over in prayer tonight.
Ask for help instead of struggling alone.
Trust the process for one difficult situation.

sanskrit: न मां दुष्कृतिनो मूढाः प्रपद्यन्ते नराधमाः ।
iast: na māṁ duṣkṛtino mūḍhāḥ prapadyante narādhamāḥ · māyayāpahṛtajñānā āsuraṁ bhāvamāśritāḥ
meaning: Wrongdoers, the deluded and the lowest of people, robbed of knowledge by illusion and taking on a demonic nature, do not turn to me.
lifeNote: Cruelty and arrogance close the heart. Watch for them in yourself first.
actions: Check one harsh habit in your speech.
Choose humility in one argument today.
Notice what blinds you when you are angry.

iast: caturvidhā bhajante māṁ janāḥ sukṛtino'rjuna · ārto jijñāsurarthārthī jñānī ca bharatarṣabha
meaning: Four kinds of virtuous people worship me, Arjuna: the distressed, the seeker of knowledge, the seeker of wealth and the wise.
lifeNote: People turn to God for many reasons: pain, curiosity, need or wisdom. All are welcome.
actions: Notice why you pray, and accept it.
Don't judge others for praying only in trouble.
Add one prayer of thanks, not only of need.

sanskrit: प्रियो हि ज्ञानिनोऽत्यर्थमहं स च मम प्रियः ॥
iast: teṣāṁ jñānī nityayukta ekabhaktirviśiṣyate · priyo hi jñānino'tyarthamahaṁ sa ca mama priyaḥ
meaning: Of these, the wise one, always steady and single-minded in devotion, is the best. I am very dear to the wise, and they are dear to me.
lifeNote: Love grounded in understanding is the deepest kind.
actions: Learn more about what you believe in.
Combine study with devotion this week.
Tell someone dear why you love them.

sanskrit: उदाराः सर्व एवैते ज्ञानी त्वात्मैव मे मतम् ।
आस्थितः स हि युक्तात्मा मामेवानुत्तमां गतिम् ॥
iast: udārāḥ sarva evaite jñānī tvātmaiva me matam · āsthitaḥ sa hi yuktātmā māmevānuttamāṁ gatim
meaning: All these are noble, but the wise one I see as my very self. Steady in mind, that person is set on me as the highest goal.
lifeNote: Every sincere seeker is noble. Wisdom makes the bond intimate.
actions: Honour sincere seekers of every kind.
Make understanding part of your faith.
Set one clear highest goal for your life.

iast: bahūnāṁ janmanāmante jñānavānmāṁ prapadyate · vāsudevaḥ sarvamiti sa mahātmā sudurlabhaḥ
meaning: After many lives, the wise one surrenders to me, knowing 'Vasudeva is everything.' Such a great soul is very rare.
lifeNote: Seeing the divine in everything is the fruit of long growth. Be patient.
actions: Look for the divine in one ordinary person today.
Be patient with your spiritual growth.
Read about one great soul you admire.

sanskrit: तं तं नियममास्थाय प्रकृत्या नियताः स्वया ॥
iast: kāmaistaistairhṛtajñānāḥ prapadyante'nyadevatāḥ · taṁ taṁ niyamamāsthāya prakṛtyā niyatāḥ svayā
meaning: Those whose understanding is carried away by various desires turn to other gods, following various rules, led by their own nature.
lifeNote: Desire often decides where we look for help. Ask what you are really seeking.
actions: Notice what desire is behind your next prayer.
Ask whether you seek comfort or truth.
Write one thing you want, and why.

sanskrit: यो यो यां यां तनुं भक्तः श्रद्धयार्चितुमिच्छति ।
iast: yo yo yāṁ yāṁ tanuṁ bhaktaḥ śraddhayārcitumicchati · tasya tasyācalāṁ śraddhāṁ tāmeva vidadhāmyaham
meaning: Whatever form a devotee wishes to worship with faith, I make that person's faith in it steady.
lifeNote: Sincere faith, in any form, is strengthened, not mocked.
actions: Respect the faith of others, whatever form it takes.
Strengthen your own faith through daily practice.
Don't argue about whose form of worship is right.

sanskrit: लभते च ततः कामान्मयैव विहितान् हि तान् ॥
iast: sa tayā śraddhayā yuktastasyārādhanamīhate · labhate ca tataḥ kāmānmayaiva vihitān hi tān
