meaning: Endowed with that faith, he worships that form and gains his desires from it. But those desires are really granted by me alone.
lifeNote: Behind every good thing you receive is a deeper source. Remember it with gratitude.
actions: Thank the source behind one blessing today.
Notice gifts you take for granted.
Share one thing you received.

iast: antavattu phalaṁ teṣāṁ tadbhavatyalpamedhasām · devāndevayajo yānti madbhaktā yānti māmapi
meaning: But the fruit gained by those of limited understanding is perishable. Worshippers of the gods go to the gods; my devotees come to me.
lifeNote: What you aim at is where you arrive. Aim at what lasts.
actions: Check whether a current goal brings lasting good.
Set one goal that will matter in ten years.
Pray for wisdom, not only for wishes.

iast: avyaktaṁ vyaktimāpannaṁ manyante māmabuddhayaḥ · paraṁ bhāvamajānanto mamāvyayamanuttamam
meaning: The unwise think I, the unmanifest, have merely taken on a form. They do not know my highest, imperishable, supreme nature.
lifeNote: Do not judge the depth of something by its surface.
actions: Look past first impressions of one person.
Learn the deeper meaning of one ritual.
Ask what lies beneath an appearance.

iast: nāhaṁ prakāśaḥ sarvasya yogamāyāsamāvṛtaḥ · mūḍho'yaṁ nābhijānāti loko māmajamavyayam
meaning: I am not revealed to everyone, veiled by my own power. This deluded world does not recognise me, the unborn and imperishable.
lifeNote: Truth is often hidden in plain sight. Seek it with patience.
actions: Spend time in silence looking for what you miss.
Ask a deep question and live with it.
Notice something beautiful you usually ignore.

sanskrit: भविष्याणि च भूतानि मां तु वेद न कश्चन ॥
iast: vedāhaṁ samatītāni vartamānāni cārjuna · bhaviṣyāṇi ca bhūtāni māṁ tu veda na kaścana
meaning: I know all beings, past, present and future, Arjuna. But no one knows me.
lifeNote: You do not have to control the future. Something wiser already holds it.
actions: Let go of one worry about the future today.
Focus on today's task, not tomorrow's result.
Trust that you are known even when unseen.

iast: icchādveṣasamutthena dvandvamohena bhārata · sarvabhūtāni saṁmohaṁ sarge yānti parantapa
meaning: Through the delusion of opposites that arises from desire and aversion, all beings fall into confusion at birth, Arjuna.
lifeNote: Like and dislike blur our vision from the start. Seeing this is the first step out.
actions: Notice one strong like or dislike today and question it.
Try something you thought you disliked.
Listen to a view you usually reject.

iast: yeṣāṁ tvantagataṁ pāpaṁ janānāṁ puṇyakarmaṇām · te dvandvamohanirmuktā bhajante māṁ dṛḍhavratāḥ
meaning: But people of good deeds whose wrongdoing has ended are freed from the delusion of opposites and worship me, firm in their vows.
lifeNote: Good actions clear the mind, and a clear mind finds steady devotion.
words: free from the delusion of opposites
actions: Do one good deed today without reward.
Keep one vow firmly this week.
Undo one small wrong you have done.

sanskrit: ते ब्रह्म तद्विदुः कृत्स्नमध्यात्मं कर्म चाखिलम् ॥
iast: jarāmaraṇamokṣāya māmāśritya yatanti ye · te brahma tadviduḥ kṛtsnamadhyātmaṁ karma cākhilam
meaning: Those who take refuge in me and strive for freedom from old age and death know Brahman, the whole of the self and all of action.
lifeNote: Facing ageing and death honestly can open the door to deep understanding.
words: for freedom from old age and death
actions: Spend time with an elder and listen to their story.
Reflect on what you want your life to mean.
Make peace with one fear about ageing.

sanskrit: साधिभूताधिदैवं मां साधियज्ञं च ये विदुः ।
iast: sādhibhūtādhidaivaṁ māṁ sādhiyajñaṁ ca ye viduḥ · prayāṇakāle'pi ca māṁ te viduryuktacetasaḥ
meaning: Those who know me as underlying the material, the divine and sacrifice, with steady minds, know me even at the time of death.
lifeNote: Steady awareness built in life stays with you at the end.
words: with the material and divine aspects
actions: Practise a few minutes of awareness daily.
Think about what you would want in your final moments.
Comfort someone who is grieving with presence.

sanskrit: किं तद्ब्रह्म किमध्यात्मं किं कर्म पुरुषोत्तम ।
iast: kiṁ tadbrahma kimadhyātmaṁ kiṁ karma puruṣottama · adhibhūtaṁ ca kiṁ proktamadhidaivaṁ kimucyate
meaning: Arjuna said: Krishna, what is Brahman? What is the self? What is action? What is called the material realm, and what the divine realm?
lifeNote: Big questions deserve to be asked plainly. Curiosity is the beginning of wisdom.
actions: Write down your biggest life question.
Ask a teacher one 'what is' question.
Read about one spiritual term you don't understand.

iast: adhiyajñaḥ kathaṁ ko'tra dehe'sminmadhusūdana · prayāṇakāle ca kathaṁ jñeyo'si niyatātmabhiḥ
meaning: Who is the lord of sacrifice here in this body, and how? And how are you to be known at the time of death by those who are self-controlled?
lifeNote: Arjuna even asks how to face death well. No question is too heavy for the Gita.
actions: Talk openly about death with someone you trust.
Reflect on how you want to live, knowing life is short.
Note one fear and one hope about the end of life.

iast: akṣaraṁ brahma paramaṁ svabhāvo'dhyātmamucyate · bhūtabhāvodbhavakaro visargaḥ karmasaṁjñitaḥ
meaning: Krishna said: Brahman is the supreme and imperishable. One's own essential nature is called the self. The creative act that brings beings into existence is called action.
lifeNote: Your deepest nature is unchanging. Your actions are how life keeps creating.
actions: Do one creative thing today.
Reflect on what in you never changes.
See your work as part of life's creating.

iast: adhibhūtaṁ kṣaro bhāvaḥ puruṣaścādhidaivatam · adhiyajño'hamevātra dehe dehabhṛtāṁ vara
meaning: The material realm is perishable existence. The divine realm is the cosmic person. And I myself, here in the body, am the lord of sacrifice, O best of the embodied.
lifeNote: The divine is not far away; it lives within your own body.
actions: Treat your body as a temple today.
Before eating, remember who it nourishes.
Sit quietly and feel the presence within.

sanskrit: यः प्रयाति स मद्भावं याति नास्त्यत्र संशयः ॥
iast: antakāle ca māmeva smaranmuktvā kalevaram · yaḥ prayāti sa madbhāvaṁ yāti nāstyatra saṁśayaḥ
meaning: Whoever leaves the body at the end remembering me alone reaches my being. There is no doubt about this.
lifeNote: What we hold in mind at the end grows from what we practise every day.
actions: End each day remembering what matters most.
Choose a name or prayer you will keep close.
Visit or call a dying or elderly relative.

sanskrit: यं यं वापि स्मरन्भावं त्यजत्यन्ते कलेवरम् ।
iast: yaṁ yaṁ vāpi smaranbhāvaṁ tyajatyante kalevaram · taṁ tamevaiti kaunteya sadā tadbhāvabhāvitaḥ
meaning: Whatever state one remembers on leaving the body at the end, that is the state one reaches, Arjuna, having always been absorbed in it.
lifeNote: You become what you dwell on. Choose your daily thoughts carefully.
actions: Notice what you think about most today.
Replace one negative loop with a good thought.
Fill your mind with something uplifting before sleep.

iast: tasmātsarveṣu kāleṣu māmanusmara yudhya ca · mayyarpitamanobuddhirmāmevaiṣyasyasaṁśayam
meaning: So remember me at all times, and fight. With mind and intellect offered to me, you will surely come to me.
lifeNote: Remember what is highest, and do your work. Both together, all the time.
actions: Set a reminder to pause and remember God during work.
Do today's hardest task with a short prayer.
Keep devotion and duty side by side.

iast: abhyāsayogayuktena cetasā nānyagāminā · paramaṁ puruṣaṁ divyaṁ yāti pārthānucintayan
meaning: With a mind trained by practice and not wandering elsewhere, meditating constantly, one reaches the supreme divine person, Arjuna.
lifeNote: Practice trains the mind to stay where you put it.
words: trained by the yoga of practice
actions: Practise focus on one thing for ten minutes.
Return gently each time your mind wanders.
Keep a practice log for one week.

iast: kaviṁ purāṇamanuśāsitāram · aṇoraṇīyāṁsamanusmaredyaḥ · sarvasya dhātāramacintyarūpam · ādityavarṇaṁ tamasaḥ parastāt
meaning: One should remember the all-knowing, ancient ruler, subtler than an atom, the sustainer of all, of unthinkable form, radiant like the sun and beyond all darkness.
lifeNote: Hold in mind something greater than your problems: subtle, bright and beyond darkness.
actions: Picture a bright sun when your mind feels dark.
Remember how vast the universe is when worries feel huge.
Read this verse aloud slowly.

iast: prayāṇakāle manasā'calena · bhaktyā yukto yogabalena caiva · bhruvormadhye prāṇamāveśya samyak · sa taṁ paraṁ puruṣamupaiti divyam
meaning: At the time of death, with an unmoving mind full of devotion, fixing the life breath between the eyebrows by the power of yoga, one reaches that supreme divine person.
lifeNote: Steady mind and loving heart, built over a lifetime, carry you at the end.
actions: Practise focusing gently between the eyebrows for a minute.
Pair breath practice with a loving prayer.
Make devotion a daily habit, not an emergency tool.

iast: yadakṣaraṁ vedavido vadanti · viśanti yadyatayo vītarāgāḥ · yadicchanto brahmacaryaṁ caranti · tatte padaṁ saṁgraheṇa pravakṣye
meaning: I will briefly explain the goal that knowers of the Vedas call imperishable, that ascetics free from attachment enter, and for which people practise self-restraint.
lifeNote: Many paths of discipline aim at one goal. Knowing the goal makes the discipline meaningful.
actions: Remind yourself why you keep a discipline.
Write the goal behind one of your habits.
Respect people who live simply for a higher aim.

sanskrit: सर्वद्वाराणि संयम्य मनो हृदि निरुध्य च ।
iast: sarvadvārāṇi saṁyamya mano hṛdi nirudhya ca · mūrdhnyādhāyātmanaḥ prāṇamāsthito yogadhāraṇām
meaning: Controlling all the gates of the body, holding the mind in the heart and placing the life breath in the head, established in yogic concentration...
lifeNote: Close the doors of distraction and settle into your heart.
actions: Close your eyes and rest attention in your heart for two minutes.
Shut off screens and sounds for a short sitting.
Notice how calm follows when senses rest.

sanskrit: यः प्रयाति त्यजन्देहं स याति परमां गतिम् ॥
iast: omityekākṣaraṁ brahma vyāharanmāmanusmaran · yaḥ prayāti tyajandehaṁ sa yāti paramāṁ gatim
meaning: ...uttering Om, the single syllable that is Brahman, and remembering me, whoever departs leaving the body reaches the supreme goal.
lifeNote: A single sacred sound can gather the whole mind into one point.
actions: Chant Om slowly three times morning and night.
Use Om to steady yourself before a hard task.
Teach a child to chant Om.

sanskrit: अनन्यचेताः सततं यो मां स्मरति नित्यशः ।
iast: ananyacetāḥ satataṁ yo māṁ smarati nityaśaḥ · tasyāhaṁ sulabhaḥ pārtha nityayuktasya yoginaḥ
meaning: For the ever-devoted yogi who remembers me constantly with an undivided mind, I am easy to reach, Arjuna.
lifeNote: Constant love makes the divine feel close and easy, not distant.
actions: Remember God briefly every hour today.
Keep a small reminder on your desk.
Speak to the divine like a close friend.

iast: māmupetya punarjanma duḥkhālayamaśāśvatam · nāpnuvanti mahātmānaḥ saṁsiddhiṁ paramāṁ gatāḥ
meaning: Having reached me, great souls do not take rebirth in this temporary home of sorrow. They have reached the highest perfection.
lifeNote: This world is beautiful and also full of sorrow. There is a peace beyond its ups and downs.
actions: Accept one sorrow as part of this passing world.
Look for peace that doesn't depend on circumstances.
Read about a saint who found lasting peace.

sanskrit: मामुपेत्य तु कौन्तेय पुनर्जन्म न विद्यते ॥
iast: ābrahmabhuvanāllokāḥ punarāvartino'rjuna · māmupetya tu kaunteya punarjanma na vidyate
meaning: All worlds, up to the realm of Brahma, are subject to return, Arjuna. But on reaching me there is no rebirth.
lifeNote: Even the highest worldly success is temporary. Aim beyond it.
words: up to the realm of Brahma
actions: Remember that even big achievements fade.
Invest in something lasting today.
Hold success loosely.

iast: sahasrayugaparyantamaharyadbrahmaṇo viduḥ · rātriṁ yugasahasrāntāṁ te'horātravido janāḥ
meaning: Those who know that a day of Brahma lasts a thousand ages, and a night a thousand ages too, truly know day and night.
lifeNote: On a cosmic clock our worries are tiny. Perspective brings calm.
actions: Look at the stars and feel the size of time.
Ask whether today's worry will matter in a year.
Read one fact about the age of the universe.

iast: avyaktādvyaktayaḥ sarvāḥ prabhavantyaharāgame · rātryāgame pralīyante tatraivāvyaktasaṁjñake
meaning: At the coming of Brahma's day all manifest things arise from the unmanifest. At the coming of night they dissolve back into it.
lifeNote: Life moves in cycles of appearing and disappearing. Nothing is truly lost.
actions: Notice the cycle of day and night with awareness.
Accept the end of one season in your life.
Plant a seed and watch the cycle of growth.

sanskrit: भूतग्रामः स एवायं भूत्वा भूत्वा प्रलीयते ।
iast: bhūtagrāmaḥ sa evāyaṁ bhūtvā bhūtvā pralīyate · rātryāgame'vaśaḥ pārtha prabhavatyaharāgame
meaning: This same multitude of beings arises again and again and helplessly dissolves at nightfall, Arjuna, and arises again at daybreak.
lifeNote: Cycles repeat. Use each new 'day' to grow, not just to repeat.
actions: Treat tomorrow as a fresh start.
Break one repeating cycle in your habits.
Reflect each night on what to do differently.

sanskrit: यः स सर्वेषु भूतेषु नश्यत्सु न विनश्यति ॥
iast: parastasmāttu bhāvo'nyo'vyakto'vyaktātsanātanaḥ · yaḥ sa sarveṣu bhūteṣu naśyatsu na vinaśyati
meaning: But beyond this unmanifest there is another, eternal unmanifest existence that does not perish when all beings perish.
lifeNote: Something in you does not end when everything else changes.
actions: Remember a loved one who has passed, with peace.
Reflect on what in you is unchanging.
Hold onto hope in a time of loss.

sanskrit: यं प्राप्य न निवर्तन्ते तद्धाम परमं मम ॥
iast: avyakto'kṣara ityuktastamāhuḥ paramāṁ gatim · yaṁ prāpya na nivartante taddhāma paramaṁ mama
meaning: That unmanifest is called the imperishable; they call it the highest goal. Those who reach it do not return. That is my supreme abode.
lifeNote: There is a home beyond change. Knowing it brings quiet courage.
actions: Picture your 'true home' when you feel lost.
Sit in silence and rest in what does not change.
Comfort someone with the idea of a lasting home.

sanskrit: पुरुषः स परः पार्थ भक्त्या लभ्यस्त्वनन्यया ।
iast: puruṣaḥ sa paraḥ pārtha bhaktyā labhyastvananyayā · yasyāntaḥsthāni bhūtāni yena sarvamidaṁ tatam
meaning: That supreme person, in whom all beings dwell and by whom all this is pervaded, is reached by undivided devotion, Arjuna.
lifeNote: Love is the simplest path to what holds everything together.
actions: Offer one act today with wholehearted love.
Pray without asking for anything.
See others as living within the same divine.

sanskrit: प्रयाता यान्ति तं कालं वक्ष्यामि भरतर्षभ ॥
iast: yatra kāle tvanāvṛttimāvṛttiṁ caiva yoginaḥ · prayātā yānti taṁ kālaṁ vakṣyāmi bharatarṣabha
meaning: Now I will tell you, Arjuna, the times at which yogis depart and do not return, and the times at which they do return.
lifeNote: The Gita speaks of paths after death symbolically: light and darkness, clarity and confusion.
actions: Reflect on what 'light' and 'darkness' mean in your choices.
Read a commentary on this passage.
Ask an elder what this verse means to them.

sanskrit: तत्र प्रयाता गच्छन्ति ब्रह्म ब्रह्मविदो जनाः ॥
iast: agnirjyotirahaḥ śuklaḥ ṣaṇmāsā uttarāyaṇam · tatra prayātā gacchanti brahma brahmavido janāḥ
meaning: Fire, light, day, the bright fortnight, the six months of the sun's northern course: departing then, knowers of Brahman go to Brahman.
lifeNote: Light stands for clarity and awareness. Live in the light and you leave in the light.
actions: Choose one 'bright' action today: honest, kind, clear.
Watch a sunrise and set a clear intention.
Bring more light (clarity) to one confusing area.

iast: dhūmo rātristathā kṛṣṇaḥ ṣaṇmāsā dakṣiṇāyanam · tatra cāndramasaṁ jyotiryogī prāpya nivartate
meaning: Smoke, night, the dark fortnight, the six months of the southern course: departing then, the yogi reaches the light of the moon and returns.
lifeNote: Clouded awareness keeps us circling. Clear the smoke a little each day.
actions: Identify one 'smoky' area of confusion in your life.
Spend ten minutes clearing one confusion.
Avoid decisions made in a cloud of anger.

sanskrit: शुक्लकृष्णे गती ह्येते जगतः शाश्वते मते ।
iast: śuklakṛṣṇe gatī hyete jagataḥ śāśvate mate · ekayā yātyanāvṛttimanyayā''vartate punaḥ
meaning: These two paths, the bright and the dark, are considered eternal. By one, one goes and does not return; by the other, one returns again.
lifeNote: Two roads are always open: clarity and confusion. Choose daily.
actions: At each choice today ask: bright or dark?
Choose the honest option in one small matter.
Reflect at night on which path you took.

sanskrit: नैते सृती पार्थ जानन्योगी मुह्यति कश्चन ।
iast: naite sṛtī pārtha jānanyogī muhyati kaścana · tasmātsarveṣu kāleṣu yogayukto bhavārjuna
meaning: Knowing these two paths, no yogi is deluded, Arjuna. So be steady in yoga at all times.
lifeNote: When you know the paths, you won't be confused. Stay steady.
actions: Keep a short daily practice no matter what.
Remember your path when tempted to drift.
Stay steady through one distracting day.

iast: vedeṣu yajñeṣu tapaḥsu caiva · dāneṣu yatpuṇyaphalaṁ pradiṣṭam · atyeti tatsarvamidaṁ viditvā · yogī paraṁ sthānamupaiti cādyam
meaning: The yogi who knows this goes beyond all the merit declared for study of the Vedas, sacrifice, austerity and charity, and reaches the supreme, primal abode.
lifeNote: Understanding goes further than any amount of ritual or merit-collecting.
actions: Look for meaning behind your good deeds.
Choose understanding over counting merits.
Read this chapter again in one sitting.

iast: idaṁ tu te guhyatamaṁ pravakṣyāmyanasūyave · jñānaṁ vijñānasahitaṁ yajjñātvā mokṣyase'śubhāt
meaning: Krishna said: Because you are free of envy, I will tell you this most secret knowledge, together with its realisation. Knowing it, you will be freed from all that is harmful.
lifeNote: An open, non-envious heart is ready for deep truths.
actions: Let go of one envious thought today.
Approach a lesson with openness, not judgement.
Celebrate someone else's gift sincerely.

iast: rājavidyā rājaguhyaṁ pavitramidamuttamam · pratyakṣāvagamaṁ dharmyaṁ susukhaṁ kartumavyayam
meaning: This is the king of knowledge, the king of secrets, supremely purifying. It can be directly experienced, is in line with dharma, is easy to practise and lasts for ever.
lifeNote: The deepest truth is not complicated; it can be lived and felt directly.
actions: Try one spiritual practice and notice its effect.
Keep faith simple and practical today.
Share one easy practice with a friend.

iast: aśraddadhānāḥ puruṣā dharmasyāsya parantapa · aprāpya māṁ nivartante mṛtyusaṁsāravartmani
meaning: People without faith in this dharma do not reach me, Arjuna. They return to the path of death and rebirth.
lifeNote: Faith keeps you moving forward; without it, we circle back to the same troubles.
words: to the path of death and rebirth
actions: Notice one cycle you keep repeating.
Trust one good practice long enough to see results.
Ask what you truly have faith in.

iast: mayā tatamidaṁ sarvaṁ jagadavyaktamūrtinā · matsthāni sarvabhūtāni na cāhaṁ teṣvavasthitaḥ
meaning: This whole world is pervaded by me in my unmanifest form. All beings rest in me, but I do not rest in them.
lifeNote: Everything is held by something larger. You are held too.
actions: When anxious, remember you are held by something larger.
Look at the sky and feel how vast it is.
Breathe and feel supported for one minute.

sanskrit: न च मत्स्थानि भूतानि पश्य मे योगमैश्वरम् ।
iast: na ca matsthāni bhūtāni paśya me yogamaiśvaram · bhūtabhṛnna ca bhūtastho mamātmā bhūtabhāvanaḥ
meaning: And yet beings do not rest in me: see my divine mystery! My self sustains all beings and brings them forth, yet does not dwell in them.
lifeNote: Some truths are paradoxes. Let them deepen your wonder rather than frustrate you.
actions: Sit with one paradox in your life without forcing an answer.
Let wonder replace confusion for a moment.
Read this verse slowly twice.

iast: yathā''kāśasthito nityaṁ vāyuḥ sarvatrago mahān · tathā sarvāṇi bhūtāni matsthānītyupadhāraya
meaning: As the mighty wind moving everywhere always rests in space, understand that all beings rest in me in the same way.
lifeNote: Like wind in the sky, you move freely and are still held.
actions: Feel the wind on your face and remember this verse.
Let your busy day move within a calm inner sky.
Take a mindful walk outside.

iast: sarvabhūtāni kaunteya prakṛtiṁ yānti māmikām · kalpakṣaye punastāni kalpādau visṛjāmyaham
meaning: At the end of a cosmic cycle all beings return into my nature, Arjuna. At the beginning of the next cycle I send them forth again.
lifeNote: Endings make room for new beginnings.
words: at the end of a cycle
at the beginning of a cycle
actions: Treat one ending as space for something new.
Write what you'd like to start after a loss.
Notice the cycle of seasons around you.

iast: prakṛtiṁ svāmavaṣṭabhya visṛjāmi punaḥ punaḥ · bhūtagrāmamimaṁ kṛtsnamavaśaṁ prakṛtervaśāt
meaning: Taking hold of my own nature, I send forth this whole multitude of beings again and again, helpless under the force of nature.
lifeNote: We are shaped by nature's forces. Knowing this makes us humble and gentle.
actions: Be patient with someone acting from habit.
Notice how much of your day is driven by nature and habit.
Respect the forces of nature around you.

sanskrit: न च मां तानि कर्माणि निबध्नन्ति धनञ्जय ।
iast: na ca māṁ tāni karmāṇi nibadhnanti dhanañjaya · udāsīnavadāsīnamasaktaṁ teṣu karmasu
meaning: These actions do not bind me, Arjuna. I sit as if neutral, unattached to them.
lifeNote: You can be fully involved and still not be entangled.
actions: Care deeply without trying to control outcomes.
Do your part in a family matter, then step back.
Notice entanglement and loosen it.

iast: mayā'dhyakṣeṇa prakṛtiḥ sūyate sacarācaram · hetunā'nena kaunteya jagadviparivartate
meaning: Under my oversight, nature brings forth all moving and unmoving things. Because of this, Arjuna, the world keeps turning.
lifeNote: Order runs beneath all the change around you.
actions: Notice one natural pattern: sunrise, tides, seasons.
Trust that life has an order beyond your control.
Do your part and let the world turn.

iast: avajānanti māṁ mūḍhā mānuṣīṁ tanumāśritam · paraṁ bhāvamajānanto mama bhūtamaheśvaram
meaning: The deluded disregard me when I take a human form, not knowing my higher nature as the great lord of all beings.
lifeNote: Greatness can look ordinary. Don't overlook it in plain clothes.
actions: Look for greatness in an ordinary person today.
Avoid judging people by appearance.
Thank someone whose quiet help you overlooked.

iast: moghāśā moghakarmāṇo moghajñānā vicetasaḥ · rākṣasīmāsurīṁ caiva prakṛtiṁ mohinīṁ śritāḥ
meaning: Their hopes, actions and knowledge are in vain; they are senseless, having taken on a fiendish, demonic and deluding nature.
lifeNote: Effort without the right direction ends up empty. Check your direction.
actions: Ask whether a current effort is pointed at something good.
Drop one goal that feeds only ego.
Seek honest feedback on your direction.

iast: mahātmānastu māṁ pārtha daivīṁ prakṛtimāśritāḥ · bhajantyananyamanaso jñātvā bhūtādimavyayam
meaning: But great souls, Arjuna, taking refuge in the divine nature, worship me with undivided minds, knowing me as the imperishable origin of all beings.
lifeNote: Kindness, patience and focus are the divine nature in you. Lean on them.
actions: Practise one divine quality today: patience, kindness, honesty.
Worship with your whole mind for five minutes.
Spend time with people of good character.

iast: satataṁ kīrtayanto māṁ yatantaśca dṛḍhavratāḥ · namasyantaśca māṁ bhaktyā nityayuktā upāsate
meaning: Always singing my glories, striving with firm vows and bowing to me with devotion, they worship me, ever steadfast.
lifeNote: Singing, effort and humility together keep love alive.
actions: Sing a bhajan or prayer today.
Bow in gratitude before sleeping.
Keep one spiritual vow firmly.

iast: jñānayajñena cāpyanye yajanto māmupāsate · ekatvena pṛthaktvena bahudhā viśvatomukham
meaning: Others worship me through the sacrifice of knowledge: as the one, as distinct, and in many forms, as the one whose face is everywhere.
lifeNote: Thinking deeply about truth is also a form of worship.
actions: Study one spiritual idea carefully today.
Respect people who seek through questions.
Notice the divine in many different faces.

iast: ahaṁ kraturahaṁ yajñaḥ svadhā'hamahamauṣadham · maṁtro'hamahamevājyamahamagnirahaṁ hutam
meaning: I am the ritual, I am the sacrifice, the offering to the ancestors and the healing herb. I am the mantra, the ghee, the fire and the act of offering.
lifeNote: Every part of worship, even the herb and the fire, is sacred.
actions: Light a lamp with full attention today.
Thank the plants that feed and heal you.
See each part of your daily routine as sacred.

sanskrit: वेद्यं पवित्रमोंकार ऋक् साम यजुरेव च ॥
iast: pitā'hamasya jagato mātā dhātā pitāmahaḥ · vedyaṁ pavitramoṁkāra ṛk sāma yajureva ca
meaning: I am the father of this world, its mother, sustainer and grandfather. I am what is to be known, the purifier, the syllable Om, and the Rig, Sama and Yajur Vedas.
lifeNote: The divine can be loved as mother, father and elder. You are family.
actions: Call your parent or grandparent today.
Pray to the divine as you would talk to a parent.
Chant Om once with care.

sanskrit: गतिर्भर्ता प्रभुः साक्षी निवासः शरणं सुहृत् ।
iast: gatirbhartā prabhuḥ sākṣī nivāsaḥ śaraṇaṁ suhṛt · prabhavaḥ pralayaḥ sthānaṁ nidhānaṁ bījamavyayam
meaning: I am the goal, the supporter, the lord, the witness, the home, the refuge and the friend. I am the origin, the dissolution, the foundation, the resting place and the imperishable seed.
lifeNote: You always have a refuge and a friend. You are never without shelter.
actions: In a hard moment, remember you have a refuge.
Be a refuge for someone who needs it.
Write down people and places that feel like home.

iast: tapāmyahamahaṁ varṣaṁ nigṛhṇāmyutsṛjāmi ca · amṛtaṁ caiva mṛtyuśca sadasaccāhamarjuna
meaning: I give heat; I hold back and send forth the rain. I am immortality and death, being and non-being, Arjuna.
lifeNote: Rain and drought, life and death: all come from one source. Even hard seasons have their place.
actions: Notice the rain or heat today and give thanks.
Accept a hard season as part of life's whole.
Comfort someone facing a loss.

iast: traividyā māṁ somapāḥ pūtapāpā · yajñairiṣṭvā svargatiṁ prārthayante · te puṇyamāsādya surendralokam · aśnanti divyāndivi devabhogān
meaning: Those who know the three Vedas, drink soma and are cleansed of sin worship me with sacrifices and pray for heaven. Reaching Indra's holy world, they enjoy the divine pleasures of the gods.
lifeNote: Rewards like heaven are real but temporary. Aim beyond rewards.
actions: Notice when you do good only for a reward.
Do one good act without expecting anything.
Ask what you want beyond rewards.

iast: te taṁ bhuktvā svargalokaṁ viśālaṁ · kṣīṇe puṇye martyalokaṁ viśanti · evaṁ trayīdharmamanuprapannā · gatāgataṁ kāmakāmā labhante
meaning: Having enjoyed that vast heaven, when their merit is spent they enter the mortal world again. Following Vedic rites for the sake of desires, they keep coming and going.
lifeNote: Pleasure-seeking keeps you on a merry-go-round. Step off now and then.
actions: Notice a reward cycle you keep repeating.
Choose meaning over pleasure in one decision.
Rest without seeking entertainment for an hour.

iast: ananyāścintayanto māṁ ye janāḥ paryupāsate · teṣāṁ nityābhiyuktānāṁ yogakṣemaṁ vahāmyaham
meaning: For those who worship me, thinking of nothing else and ever devoted, I carry what they need and protect what they have.
lifeNote: When you give your heart fully, you are cared for. You do not carry everything alone.
actions: Hand over one worry about money or security in prayer.
Do your duty and trust for the rest.
Help someone in need as a channel of this care.

iast: ye'pyanyadevatā bhaktā yajante śraddhayā'nvitāḥ · te'pi māmeva kaunteya yajantyavidhipūrvakam
meaning: Even devotees who worship other gods with faith are really worshipping me alone, Arjuna, though not in the proper way.
lifeNote: All sincere worship reaches the same source. Respect it.
actions: Respect someone else's form of worship.
Notice the shared sincerity in different faiths.
Avoid arguing about the 'right' god.

sanskrit: अहं हि सर्वयज्ञानां भोक्ता च प्रभुरेव च ।
iast: ahaṁ hi sarvayajñānāṁ bhoktā ca prabhureva ca · na tu māmabhijānanti tattvenātaścyavanti te
meaning: I am the receiver and the lord of all sacrifices. But they do not know me in truth, and so they fall.
lifeNote: Know who your effort really goes to. That gives it lasting value.
actions: Dedicate one effort today consciously.
Reflect on whom your work truly serves.
Offer gratitude before beginning work.

sanskrit: भूतानि यान्ति भूतेज्या यान्ति मद्याजिनोऽपि माम् ॥
iast: yānti devavratā devān pitṛnyānti pitṛvratāḥ · bhūtāni yānti bhūtejyā yānti madyājino'pi mām
meaning: Worshippers of gods go to the gods, worshippers of ancestors go to the ancestors, worshippers of spirits go to the spirits, and my worshippers come to me.
lifeNote: You become like what you devote yourself to. Choose wisely.
actions: Ask what you are really devoted to.
Spend time on what you want to become.
Choose role models carefully.

sanskrit: पत्रं पुष्पं फलं तोयं यो मे भक्त्या प्रयच्छति ।
iast: patraṁ puṣpaṁ phalaṁ toyaṁ yo me bhaktyā prayacchati · tadahaṁ bhaktyupahṛtamaśnāmi prayatātmanaḥ
meaning: Whoever offers me with love a leaf, a flower, a fruit or a little water, I accept that loving offering from the pure-hearted.
lifeNote: The size of the gift doesn't matter; the love in it does.
actions: Offer a flower or a glass of water with love today.
Give a small, heartfelt gift to someone.
Teach a child to offer a leaf with a prayer.

iast: yatkaroṣi yadaśnāsi yajjuhoṣi dadāsi yat · yattapasyasi kaunteya tatkuruṣva madarpaṇam
meaning: Whatever you do, whatever you eat, whatever you offer, whatever you give, whatever discipline you practise, Arjuna, do it as an offering to me.
lifeNote: Every ordinary act can be an offering. Life itself becomes worship.
actions: Offer your work today with a short prayer.
Eat one meal as an offering.
Give something today as an offering, not a favour.

iast: śubhāśubhaphalairevaṁ mokṣyase karmabandhanaiḥ · saṁnyāsayogayuktātmā vimukto māmupaiṣyasi
meaning: This way you will be freed from the bonds of action and their good and bad results. With your mind set on renunciation, liberated, you will come to me.
lifeNote: Offering frees you from carrying the weight of every result.
actions: Let go of one result you are anxious about.
Offer both your successes and failures tonight.
Feel the relief of not owning every outcome.

sanskrit: समोऽहं सर्वभूतेषु न मे द्वेष्योऽस्ति न प्रियः ।
ये भजन्ति तु मां भक्त्या मयि ते तेषु चाप्यहम् ॥
iast: samo'haṁ sarvabhūteṣu na me dveṣyo'sti na priyaḥ · ye bhajanti tu māṁ bhaktyā mayi te teṣu cāpyaham
meaning: I am the same to all beings; no one is hateful or especially dear to me. But those who worship me with devotion are in me, and I am in them.
lifeNote: Love is offered equally to all. Devotion is how you receive it.
actions: Treat everyone fairly today, without favourites.
Open your heart in prayer and receive.
Notice you are loved without needing to earn it.

sanskrit: साधुरेव स मन्तव्यः सम्यग्व्यवसितो हि सः ॥
iast: api cetsudurācāro bhajate māmananyabhāk · sādhureva sa mantavyaḥ samyagvyavasito hi saḥ
meaning: Even if a person of very bad conduct worships me with undivided devotion, he should be considered good, for he has resolved rightly.
lifeNote: Your past doesn't decide your future. A sincere turn changes everything.
actions: Make one sincere fresh start today.
Don't define someone by their past mistakes.
Write a resolution and keep it.

sanskrit: कौन्तेय प्रतिजानीहि न मे भक्तः प्रणश्यति ॥
iast: kṣipraṁ bhavati dharmātmā śaśvacchāntiṁ nigacchati · kaunteya pratijānīhi na me bhaktaḥ praṇaśyati
meaning: He quickly becomes righteous and attains lasting peace. Declare it boldly, Arjuna: my devotee never perishes.
lifeNote: One of the Gita's great promises: sincere love is never lost.
actions: Repeat 'my devotee never perishes' when afraid.
Encourage someone who feels it's too late to change.
Keep a short daily devotion.

sanskrit: मां हि पार्थ व्यपाश्रित्य येऽपि स्युः पापयोनयः ।
स्त्रियो वैश्यास्तथा शूद्रास्तेऽपि यान्ति परां गतिम् ॥
iast: māṁ hi pārtha vyapāśritya ye'pi syuḥ pāpayonayaḥ · striyo vaiśyāstathā śūdrāste'pi yānti parāṁ gatim
meaning: Anyone who takes refuge in me, Arjuna, whatever their birth, women, merchants and workers alike, reaches the supreme goal.
lifeNote: The door is open to everyone. No birth, gender or job keeps you out.
actions: Challenge one belief that excludes people.
Welcome someone into a group they're left out of.
Remember your path is open regardless of background.

iast: kiṁ punarbrāhmaṇāḥ puṇyā bhaktā rājarṣayastathā · anityamasukhaṁ lokamimaṁ prāpya bhajasva mām
meaning: How much more then holy priests and devoted saintly kings! Having come into this temporary, joyless world, worship me.
lifeNote: This life is short and imperfect. Use it for what matters most.
actions: Spend time today on what matters most to you.
Don't postpone devotion for a 'better time'.
Make one choice that reflects your deepest values.

sanskrit: मन्मना भव मद्भक्तो मद्याजी मां नमस्कुरु ।
iast: manmanā bhava madbhakto madyājī māṁ namaskuru · māmevaiṣyasi yuktvaivamātmānaṁ matparāyaṇaḥ
meaning: Fix your mind on me, be devoted to me, worship me and bow to me. Uniting yourself with me as your goal, you will surely come to me.
lifeNote: Mind, heart, action and humility pointed one way: that is the whole path in one line.
actions: Begin your day with this verse.
Bow once in gratitude before bed.
Keep your mind on what you love for one minute.

sanskrit: भूय एव महाबाहो शृणु मे परमं वचः ।
iast: bhūya eva mahābāho śṛṇu me paramaṁ vacaḥ · yatte'haṁ prīyamāṇāya vakṣyāmi hitakāmyayā
meaning: Krishna said: Listen again, Arjuna, to my supreme word. Because you are dear to me, I will speak for your good.
lifeNote: Good teachers speak out of care. Listen when someone speaks for your good.
actions: Listen fully to advice given with care.
Speak today only to help, not to impress.
Thank someone who wished you well.

sanskrit: न मे विदुः सुरगणाः प्रभवं न महर्षयः ।
iast: na me viduḥ suragaṇāḥ prabhavaṁ na maharṣayaḥ · ahamādirhi devānāṁ maharṣīṇāṁ ca sarvaśaḥ
meaning: Neither the gods nor the great sages know my origin, for I am the source of the gods and the great sages in every way.
lifeNote: Some things are beyond full understanding. Humility is wise.
actions: Admit one thing you don't fully understand.
Approach big questions with humility.
Read about the vastness of the cosmos.

iast: yo māmajamanādiṁ ca vetti lokamaheśvaram · asammūḍhaḥ sa martyeṣu sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate
meaning: One who knows me as unborn, without beginning and the great lord of the worlds is undeluded among mortals and freed from all wrongs.
lifeNote: Knowing what is eternal clears confusion about what is passing.
actions: Reflect on what in life has no beginning or end.
Let go of one passing worry.
Seek clarity before making a big choice.

sanskrit: सुखं दुःखं भवोऽभावो भयं चाभयमेव च ॥
iast: buddhirjñānamasaṁmohaḥ kṣamā satyaṁ damaḥ śamaḥ · sukhaṁ duḥkhaṁ bhavo'bhāvo bhayaṁ cābhayameva ca
meaning: Intelligence, knowledge, clarity, forgiveness, truth, self-control and calm; pleasure and pain, birth and death, fear and fearlessness...
lifeNote: All our qualities, the bright and the hard, come from one source.
actions: Practise forgiveness in one small matter today.
Tell the truth in a situation where it's hard.
Notice fear and fearlessness both rising in you.

sanskrit: भवन्ति भावा भूतानां मत्त एव पृथग्विधाः ॥
iast: ahiṁsā samatā tuṣṭistapo dānaṁ yaśo'yaśaḥ · bhavanti bhāvā bhūtānāṁ matta eva pṛthagvidhāḥ
meaning: ...non-violence, equanimity, contentment, discipline, charity, fame and infamy: these various qualities of beings arise from me alone.
lifeNote: Kindness, contentment and generosity are divine gifts. Use them.
actions: Avoid harsh words for one whole day.
Give something to charity this week.
Notice contentment in a simple moment.

sanskrit: मद्भावा मानसा जाता येषां लोक इमाः प्रजाः ॥
iast: maharṣayaḥ sapta pūrve catvāro manavastathā · madbhāvā mānasā jātā yeṣāṁ loka imāḥ prajāḥ
meaning: The seven great sages of old and the four Manus were born from my mind and share my nature. From them came all the creatures of the world.
lifeNote: Every family line traces back to wise ancestors. Honour your roots.
actions: Learn the name of an ancestor you didn't know.
Thank elders who passed on good values.
Share a family story with a younger relative.

sanskrit: एतां विभूतिं योगं च मम यो वेत्ति तत्त्वतः ।
iast: etāṁ vibhūtiṁ yogaṁ ca mama yo vetti tattvataḥ · so'vikampena yogena yujyate nātra saṁśayaḥ
meaning: One who truly knows my glory and power is united with me in unwavering yoga. There is no doubt about this.
lifeNote: Seeing the divine in the world's glory steadies faith.
actions: Notice one glorious thing in nature today.
Let wonder strengthen your faith.
Keep a 'glory' journal for a week.

sanskrit: अहं सर्वस्य प्रभवो मत्तः सर्वं प्रवर्तते ।
इति मत्वा भजन्ते मां बुधा भावसमन्विताः ॥
iast: ahaṁ sarvasya prabhavo mattaḥ sarvaṁ pravartate · iti matvā bhajante māṁ budhā bhāvasamanvitāḥ
meaning: I am the origin of all; everything proceeds from me. Understanding this, the wise worship me with deep feeling.
lifeNote: Knowing where everything comes from fills worship with real feeling.
actions: Pray with feeling, not just words.
Remember the source before a meal.
Feel gratitude for one thing you usually ignore.

sanskrit: कथयन्तश्च मां नित्यं तुष्यन्ति च रमन्ति च ॥
iast: maccittā madgataprāṇā bodhayantaḥ parasparam · kathayantaśca māṁ nityaṁ tuṣyanti ca ramanti ca
meaning: With minds on me and lives given to me, enlightening one another and always speaking of me, they are content and full of delight.
lifeNote: Good company that talks about what matters brings deep joy.
actions: Talk about something meaningful with a friend today.
Join or start a small study group.
Share a story from the Gita with a child.

sanskrit: ददामि बुद्धियोगं तं येन मामुपयान्ति ते ॥
iast: teṣāṁ satatayuktānāṁ bhajatāṁ prītipūrvakam · dadāmi buddhiyogaṁ taṁ yena māmupayānti te
meaning: To those who are ever devoted and worship me with love, I give the understanding by which they come to me.
lifeNote: Love opens the door to understanding. Wisdom is a gift as well as an effort.
actions: Study something you love and notice how easily it sinks in.
Pray for understanding before studying.
Approach learning with affection, not fear.

iast: teṣāmevānukampārthamahamajñānajaṁ tamaḥ · nāśayāmyātmabhāvastho jñānadīpena bhāsvatā
meaning: Out of compassion for them, dwelling in their hearts, I destroy the darkness born of ignorance with the shining lamp of knowledge.
lifeNote: When you feel lost, a light can be lit inside you. Ask for it.
actions: Light a lamp and pray for clarity tonight.
Be a 'lamp' for someone confused.
Write down one thing that recently cleared your confusion.

sanskrit: परं ब्रह्म परं धाम पवित्रं परमं भवान् ।
iast: paraṁ brahma paraṁ dhāma pavitraṁ paramaṁ bhavān · puruṣaṁ śāśvataṁ divyamādidevamajaṁ vibhum
meaning: Arjuna said: You are the supreme Brahman, the supreme abode, the supreme purifier, the eternal divine person, the first god, unborn and all-pervading.
lifeNote: Arjuna responds with praise. Gratitude and wonder are natural responses to truth.
actions: Write a few lines of praise for something you admire.
Express thanks out loud today.
Sing a hymn of praise.

sanskrit: असितो देवलो व्यासः स्वयं चैव ब्रवीषि मे ॥
iast: āhustvāmṛṣayaḥ sarve devarṣirnāradastathā · asito devalo vyāsaḥ svayaṁ caiva bravīṣi me
meaning: All the sages declare this of you: the divine sage Narada, Asita, Devala and Vyasa. And now you yourself tell me.
lifeNote: When many wise voices agree, and your own experience confirms it, trust grows.
actions: Check one belief against several trusted sources.
Read what different sages say on one topic.
Notice when your own experience confirms a teaching.

sanskrit: न हि ते भगवन् व्यक्तिं विदुर्देवा न दानवाः ॥
iast: sarvametadṛtaṁ manye yanmāṁ vadasi keśava · na hi te bhagavan vyaktiṁ vidurdevā na dānavāḥ
meaning: I accept as true all that you tell me, Krishna. Neither the gods nor the demons know your manifestation, Lord.
lifeNote: Trust can grow beyond what you can prove. Honest faith is a choice too.
actions: Trust a teacher's word long enough to test it.
Accept a truth you can't fully explain yet.
Be honest about where your faith stands.

iast: svayamevātmanā'tmānaṁ vettha tvaṁ puruṣottama · bhūtabhāvana bhūteśa devadeva jagatpate
meaning: You alone know yourself by yourself, supreme person, source and lord of beings, god of gods, lord of the world.
lifeNote: Some things can only be known from the inside. Respect mystery.
actions: Spend a quiet moment getting to know yourself.
Respect that others know their own hearts best.
Ask before assuming what someone feels.

iast: vaktumarhasyaśeṣeṇa divyā hyātmavibhūtayaḥ · yābhirvibhūtibhirlokānimāṁstvaṁ vyāpya tiṣṭhasi
meaning: Please describe fully your divine glories, by which you pervade these worlds and remain in them.
lifeNote: Asking 'where can I see you?' is a beautiful prayer.
actions: Ask today: where can I see the divine?
Look for goodness in your surroundings.
Keep a list of 'divine moments' this week.

sanskrit: केषु केषु च भावेषु चिन्त्योऽसि भगवन्मया ॥
iast: kathaṁ vidyāmahaṁ yogiṁstvāṁ sadā paricintayan · keṣu keṣu ca bhāveṣu cintyo'si bhagavanmayā
meaning: How may I know you, great yogi, as I meditate on you always? In what forms should I think of you, Lord?
lifeNote: Having something concrete to focus on makes meditation easier.
actions: Choose one image or symbol to focus on in prayer.
Ask a teacher how they meditate.
Try meditating on a natural object like the sun.

sanskrit: भूयः कथय तृप्तिर्हि शृण्वतो नास्ति मेऽमृतम् ॥
iast: vistareṇātmano yogaṁ vibhūtiṁ ca janārdana · bhūyaḥ kathaya tṛptirhi śṛṇvato nāsti me'mṛtam
meaning: Tell me again in detail of your power and glory, Krishna, for I am never satisfied hearing your nectar-like words.
lifeNote: Some words feed the soul; you never tire of them.
actions: Reread a favourite verse today.
Listen to a talk that nourishes you.
Share an uplifting quote with a friend.

iast: hanta te kathayiṣyāmi divyā hyātmavibhūtayaḥ · prādhānyataḥ kuruśreṣṭha nāstyanto vistarasya me
meaning: Krishna said: Yes, I will tell you my divine glories, but only the chief ones, Arjuna, for there is no end to their extent.
lifeNote: The divine is endless. Any list is just a starting point.
actions: Notice how endless beauty is in nature.
Start a list of everyday wonders.
Let one example open your eyes to many.

sanskrit: अहमादिश्च मध्यं च भूतानामन्त एव च ॥
iast: ahamātmā guḍākeśa sarvabhūtāśayasthitaḥ · ahamādiśca madhyaṁ ca bhūtānāmanta eva ca
meaning: I am the self, Arjuna, dwelling in the heart of all beings. I am the beginning, the middle and the end of all beings.
lifeNote: The divine lives in every heart, including yours and those you struggle with.
words: dwelling in the heart of all beings
actions: Remember the divine lives in someone you dislike.
Place a hand on your heart and feel the presence.
Treat every stage of life as sacred.

iast: ādityānāmahaṁ viṣṇurjyotiṣāṁ raviraṁśumān · marīcirmarutāmasmi nakṣatrāṇāmahaṁ śaśī
meaning: Of the Adityas I am Vishnu; of lights, the radiant sun. Of the Maruts I am Marichi; among the stars, I am the moon.
lifeNote: The best in every group points to the divine.
actions: Watch the sun or moon today with this verse in mind.
Notice the brightest quality in each friend.
Look for the best in each group you're part of.

iast: vedānāṁ sāmavedo'smi devānāmasmi vāsavaḥ · indriyāṇāṁ manaścāsmi bhūtānāmasmi cetanā
meaning: Of the Vedas I am the Sama Veda; of the gods, Indra; of the senses, the mind; and in beings I am consciousness.
lifeNote: Your awareness itself is sacred. Guard it well.
actions: Notice your awareness itself for a minute.
Listen to sacred music (like Sama chants).
Protect your mind from junk content today.

iast: rudrāṇāṁ śaṅkaraścāsmi vitteśo yakṣarakṣasām · vasūnāṁ pāvakaścāsmi meruḥ śikhariṇāmaham
meaning: Of the Rudras I am Shankara; of yakshas and rakshasas, Kubera, lord of wealth. Of the Vasus I am fire, and of mountains, Meru.
lifeNote: Strength, wealth and height are all expressions of one power.
actions: Use your strengths to lift others.
Treat money as a trust, not an identity.
Climb a hill or look at mountains and feel small.

sanskrit: पुरोधसां च मुख्यं मां विद्धि पार्थ बृहस्पतिम् ।
iast: purodhasāṁ ca mukhyaṁ māṁ viddhi pārtha bṛhaspatim · senānīnāmahaṁ skandaḥ sarasāmasmi sāgaraḥ
meaning: Of priests, know me as the chief, Brihaspati. Of generals I am Skanda; of bodies of water, I am the ocean.
lifeNote: Wisdom, courage and depth: each is a face of the divine.
actions: Be brave in one small situation today.
Look at the sea or a large lake and reflect.
Learn from a wise teacher this week.

iast: maharṣīṇāṁ bhṛgurahaṁ girāmasmyekamakṣaram · yajñānāṁ japayajño'smi sthāvarāṇāṁ himālayaḥ
meaning: Of great sages I am Bhrigu; of words, the single syllable Om. Of sacrifices I am silent repetition of a mantra; of immovable things, the Himalaya.
lifeNote: Simple japa, repeating a sacred name, is called the highest sacrifice.
actions: Repeat a sacred name 108 times today.
Use japa to calm yourself in a stressful moment.
Look at a picture of the Himalaya and feel steady.

iast: aśvatthaḥ sarvavṛkṣāṇāṁ devarṣīṇāṁ ca nāradaḥ · gandharvāṇāṁ citrarathaḥ siddhānāṁ kapilo muniḥ
meaning: Of all trees I am the peepal; of divine sages, Narada; of gandharvas, Chitraratha; of the perfected, the sage Kapila.
lifeNote: Sacred trees, sages and musicians all reflect the divine.
actions: Sit under a tree for a few minutes today.
Water a plant with care.
Tell a child the story of Narada.

iast: uccaiḥśravasamaśvānāṁ viddhi māmamṛtodbhavam · airāvataṁ gajendrāṇāṁ narāṇāṁ ca narādhipam
meaning: Of horses, know me as Uchchaihshravas, born from the churning of the nectar; of lordly elephants, Airavata; and among people, the king.
lifeNote: Excellence in any form, even in animals, can remind you of the divine.
actions: Admire an animal's grace today.
Lead with fairness if you're in charge of others.
Read the story of the churning of the ocean.

iast: āyudhānāmahaṁ vajraṁ dhenūnāmasmi kāmadhuk · prajanaścāsmi kandarpaḥ sarpāṇāmasmi vāsukiḥ
meaning: Of weapons I am the thunderbolt; of cows, the wish-fulfilling Kamadhenu. I am Kandarpa, the power of procreation, and of serpents, Vasuki.
lifeNote: Even creative and protective energies are sacred when used rightly.
actions: Use your power to protect someone today.
Respect the gift of family and children.
Care for a cow or animal shelter in some way.

iast: anantaścāsmi nāgānāṁ varuṇo yādasāmaham · pitṛṇāmaryamā cāsmi yamaḥ saṁyamatāmaham
meaning: Of nagas I am Ananta; of water beings, Varuna. Of ancestors I am Aryama, and of those who keep order, Yama.
lifeNote: Discipline and order, like Yama's justice, are also divine.
actions: Keep one rule you set for yourself today.
Remember your ancestors with a short prayer.
Respect fair rules even when inconvenient.

iast: prahlādaścāsmi daityānāṁ kālaḥ kalayatāmaham · mṛgāṇāṁ ca mṛgendro'haṁ vainateyaśca pakṣiṇām
meaning: Of the daityas I am Prahlada; of reckoners, time. Of beasts I am the lion, and of birds, Garuda.
lifeNote: Prahlada, born among demons, shows that goodness can bloom anywhere.
actions: Tell a child the story of Prahlada.
Stay true to your values in a difficult place.
Use your time today as something sacred.

iast: pavanaḥ pavatāmasmi rāmaḥ śastrabhṛtāmaham · jhaṣāṇāṁ makaraścāsmi srotasāmasmi jāhnavī
meaning: Of purifiers I am the wind; of warriors, Rama. Of water creatures I am the makara, and of rivers, the Ganga.
lifeNote: Rama shows how strength serves righteousness.
actions: Read a short story from the Ramayana.
Take a breath of fresh air and feel cleansed.
Use your strength for a good cause today.

iast: sargāṇāmādirantaśca madhyaṁ caivāhamarjuna · adhyātmavidyā vidyānāṁ vādaḥ pravadatāmaham
meaning: Of creations I am the beginning, the middle and the end, Arjuna. Of sciences I am the knowledge of the self; of those who debate, I am honest reasoning.
lifeNote: Honest discussion, seeking truth not victory, is sacred.
actions: In a debate today, aim for truth, not winning.
Study self-knowledge alongside your subjects.
Listen to an opposing view fairly.

iast: akṣarāṇāmakāro'smi dvandvaḥ sāmāsikasya ca · ahamevākṣayaḥ kālo dhātā'haṁ viśvatomukhaḥ
meaning: Of letters I am 'A'; of compounds, the dual compound. I alone am endless time, and the sustainer who faces everywhere.
lifeNote: The divine is even in the first letter you learnt. Learning is sacred.
actions: Teach a child their first letters with care.
Treat your study as something sacred.
Use your time today wisely.

sanskrit: कीर्तिः श्रीर्वाक्च नारीणां स्मृतिर्मेधा धृतिः क्षमा ॥
iast: mṛtyuḥ sarvaharaścāhamudbhavaśca bhaviṣyatām · kīrtiḥ śrīrvākca nārīṇāṁ smṛtirmedhā dhṛtiḥ kṣamā
meaning: I am all-devouring death and the origin of all that is to come. Among feminine qualities I am fame, prosperity, speech, memory, intelligence, steadfastness and forgiveness.
lifeNote: Memory, steadfastness and forgiveness are divine strengths; cultivate them.
actions: Practise forgiveness in one relationship.
Use a memory technique while studying.
Speak gently and truthfully today.

iast: bṛhatsāma tathā sāmnāṁ gāyatrī chandasāmaham · māsānāṁ mārgaśīrṣo'hamṛtūnāṁ kusumākaraḥ
meaning: Of Sama hymns I am the Brihat Sama; of metres, the Gayatri. Of months I am Margashirsha, and of seasons, flower-bearing spring.
lifeNote: Beauty in poetry and seasons is a window to the divine.
actions: Chant the Gayatri mantra once today.
Enjoy flowers or fresh leaves outside.
Notice the beauty of the current season.

iast: dyūtaṁ chalayatāmasmi tejastejasvināmaham · jayo'smi vyavasāyo'smi sattvaṁ sattvavatāmaham
meaning: Of cheats I am gambling; I am the splendour of the splendid. I am victory, I am determination, and I am the goodness of the good.
lifeNote: Determination and goodness lead to true victory.
actions: Stay determined on one goal today.
Avoid shortcuts that feel like cheating.
Celebrate a win earned honestly.

iast: vṛṣṇīnāṁ vāsudevo'smi pāṇḍavānāṁ dhanaṁjayaḥ · munīnāmapyahaṁ vyāsaḥ kavīnāmuśanā kaviḥ
meaning: Of the Vrishnis I am Vasudeva; of the Pandavas, Arjuna. Of sages I am Vyasa, and of poets, the poet Ushana.
lifeNote: Krishna even names Arjuna himself. The divine shines in the one listening.
actions: Recognise one divine quality in yourself.
Read something by Vyasa or about him.
Thank a friend for being who they are.

iast: daṇḍo damayatāmasmi nītirasmi jigīṣatām · maunaṁ caivāsmi guhyānāṁ jñānaṁ jñānavatāmaham
meaning: Of rulers I am the rod of justice; of those seeking victory, wise policy. Of secrets I am silence, and of the wise, knowledge.
lifeNote: Silence keeps the deepest secrets; wise strategy wins fairly.
actions: Keep a confidence someone trusted you with.
Plan wisely before acting on a goal.
Practise ten minutes of silence today.

sanskrit: न तदस्ति विना यत्स्यान्मया भूतं चराचरम् ॥
iast: yaccāpi sarvabhūtānāṁ bījaṁ tadahamarjuna · na tadasti vinā yatsyānmayā bhūtaṁ carācaram
meaning: I am the seed of all beings, Arjuna. Nothing, moving or unmoving, can exist without me.
lifeNote: Everything that exists shares one seed. You are part of everything.
actions: Plant a seed and remember this verse.
Treat all life with respect today.
Feel connected to everything for a moment.

iast: nānto'sti mama divyānāṁ vibhūtīnāṁ paraṁtapa · eṣa tūddeśataḥ prokto vibhūtervistaro mayā
meaning: There is no end to my divine glories, Arjuna. What I have told you is only a brief sketch of their extent.
lifeNote: Whatever you've seen of beauty and goodness is only a glimpse.
actions: Stay curious about life's wonders.
Notice one new wonder each day this week.
Remind yourself there is always more to learn.

iast: yadyadvibhūtimatsattvaṁ śrīmadūrjitameva vā · tattadevāvagaccha tvaṁ mama tejoṁ'śasaṁbhavam
meaning: Whatever is glorious, prosperous or powerful, know that it springs from a mere spark of my splendour.
lifeNote: When you see greatness anywhere, see the divine spark in it.
words: born of a spark of my splendour
actions: When you admire someone, recognise the divine spark.
Use your talent as a spark of something greater.
Avoid envy by remembering the source of all gifts.

iast: athavā bahunaitena kiṁ jñātena tavārjuna · viṣṭabhyāhamidaṁ kṛtsnamekāṁśena sthito jagat
meaning: But what use is all this detail to you, Arjuna? I support this entire world with a single fraction of myself.
lifeNote: The whole universe is a small part of the divine. Your worries are smaller still.
actions: When overwhelmed, remember how vast reality is.
Let one detail go and focus on the big picture.
Rest in trust for a few minutes.

iast: madanugrahāya paramaṁ guhyamadhyātmasaṁjñitam · yattvayoktaṁ vacastena moho'yaṁ vigato mama
meaning: Arjuna said: Out of kindness to me you have spoken this supreme secret about the self. Through your words my confusion is gone.
lifeNote: Kind words of truth can dissolve confusion. Thank those who speak them.
actions: Thank someone whose words once cleared your confusion.
Speak one kind, clarifying word to someone today.
Write down a confusion that has cleared.

sanskrit: भवाप्ययौ हि भूतानां श्रुतौ विस्तरशो मया ।
iast: bhavāpyayau hi bhūtānāṁ śrutau vistaraśo mayā · tvattaḥ kamalapatrākṣa māhātmyamapi cāvyayam
meaning: I have heard from you in detail about the origin and dissolution of beings, lotus-eyed Krishna, and about your imperishable greatness.
lifeNote: After listening deeply, we long to see for ourselves.
actions: Summarise something you've learnt in your own words.
Move from hearing to experiencing one teaching.
Ask a follow-up question to a teacher.

iast: evametadyathāttha tvamātmānaṁ parameśvara · draṣṭumicchāmi te rūpamaiśvaraṁ puruṣottama
meaning: It is just as you describe yourself, supreme lord. Yet I wish to see your divine form, supreme person.
lifeNote: Faith grows into a wish for direct experience. That longing is healthy.
actions: Notice where you want to experience, not just believe.
Sit in prayer asking to 'see' more clearly.
Visit a place that inspires awe.

sanskrit: मन्यसे यदि तच्छक्यं मया द्रष्टुमिति प्रभो ।
iast: manyase yadi tacchakyaṁ mayā draṣṭumiti prabho · yogeśvara tato me tvaṁ darśayā'tmānamavyayam
meaning: If you think I am able to see it, Lord, master of yoga, then show me your imperishable self.
lifeNote: Arjuna asks humbly: 'if you think I'm ready.' Humility opens doors.
actions: Ask for something humbly today.
Accept a teacher's judgement of your readiness.
Prepare yourself before asking for more.

sanskrit: पश्य मे पार्थ रूपाणि शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः ।
iast: paśya me pārtha rūpāṇi śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ · nānāvidhāni divyāni nānāvarṇākṛtīni ca
meaning: Krishna said: Behold my forms, Arjuna, by hundreds and thousands: divine, of many kinds, of many colours and shapes.
lifeNote: The divine shows itself in endless variety. Diversity is sacred.
actions: Appreciate the variety of people around you.
Notice the many colours in nature today.
Draw or colour something with a child.

iast: paśyādityānvasūnrudrānaśvinau marutastathā · bahūnyadṛṣṭapūrvāṇi paśyā'ścaryāṇi bhārata
meaning: Behold the Adityas, Vasus, Rudras, the two Ashvins and the Maruts. Behold many wonders never seen before, Arjuna.
lifeNote: Life still holds wonders you have never seen. Stay open.
actions: Do one thing you've never done before.
Look closely at something you pass daily.
Keep a wonder journal for a week.

iast: ihaikasthaṁ jagatkṛtsnaṁ paśyādya sacarācaram · mama dehe guḍākeśa yaccānyaddraṣṭumicchasi
meaning: Behold today the whole world, moving and unmoving, gathered in one place in my body, Arjuna, and whatever else you wish to see.
lifeNote: Everything is connected in one whole. Seeing that changes how you treat the world.
actions: Notice how your actions affect the wider world.
Make one eco-friendly choice today.
See your community as one body.

sanskrit: न तु मां शक्यसे द्रष्टुमनेनैव स्वचक्षुषा ।
दिव्यं ददामि ते चक्षुः पश्य मे योगमैश्वरम् ॥
iast: na tu māṁ śakyase draṣṭumanenaiva svacakṣuṣā · divyaṁ dadāmi te cakṣuḥ paśya me yogamaiśvaram
meaning: But you cannot see me with these eyes of yours. I give you a divine eye: behold my divine power.
lifeNote: Some things need new eyes. Ask for the vision to see deeper.
actions: Look at a familiar problem through someone else's eyes.
Pray for the 'eye' to see what matters.
Learn a new perspective this week.

iast: evamuktvā tato rājanmahāyogeśvaro hariḥ · darśayāmāsa pārthāya paramaṁ rūpamaiśvaram
meaning: Sanjaya said: Having spoken thus, O king, Hari, the great lord of yoga, showed Arjuna his supreme divine form.
lifeNote: Sanjaya tells the blind king what he sees. Sharing a vision is a gift.
actions: Describe something beautiful to someone who can't see it.
Share an inspiring story at dinner.
Read this chapter aloud with family.

iast: anekavaktranayanamanekādbhutadarśanam · anekadivyābharaṇaṁ divyānekodyatāyudham
meaning: With countless mouths and eyes, countless wondrous sights, countless divine ornaments and many divine weapons raised...
lifeNote: The cosmic form is overwhelming on purpose: reality is bigger than our categories.
actions: Look at a photo of a galaxy and feel the scale.
Let wonder humble you today.
Draw what 'endless' means to you.

iast: divyamālyāmbaradharaṁ divyagandhānulepanam · sarvāścaryamayaṁ devamanantaṁ viśvatomukham
meaning: ...wearing divine garlands and garments, anointed with divine fragrances, full of every wonder: the infinite god facing in every direction.
lifeNote: Beauty and wonder are signs of the divine. Let them move you.
actions: Wear a fresh garland or flower at prayer time.
Enjoy a fragrance mindfully today.
Notice one wonder in each direction you turn.

sanskrit: यदि भाः सदृशी सा स्याद्भासस्तस्य महात्मनः ॥
iast: divi sūryasahasrasya bhavedyugapadutthitā · yadi bhāḥ sadṛśī sā syādbhāsastasya mahātmanaḥ
meaning: If the light of a thousand suns were to blaze forth in the sky at once, it might resemble the splendour of that great being.
lifeNote: Some experiences are beyond words. Try to describe them anyway, as the Gita does.
actions: Watch the sun rise and imagine a thousand suns.
Write about a moment that took your breath away.
Share this verse with a friend.

iast: tatraikasthaṁ jagatkṛtsnaṁ pravibhaktamanekadhā · apaśyaddevadevasya śarīre pāṇḍavastadā
meaning: There, in the body of the god of gods, Arjuna then saw the entire world, with all its many divisions, gathered in one place.
lifeNote: Behind all divisions is one whole. Look for unity under difference.
actions: Find common ground with someone very different.
See your family's differences as one whole.
Reflect on one thing all humans share.

iast: tataḥ sa vismayāviṣṭo hṛṣṭaromā dhanañjayaḥ · praṇamya śirasā devaṁ kṛtāñjalirabhāṣata
meaning: Then Arjuna, filled with wonder and with his hair standing on end, bowed his head to the god and spoke with joined palms.
lifeNote: Awe naturally leads to humility. Let yourself bow.
actions: Bow with joined palms at least once today.
Let wonder replace pride for a moment.
Greet elders with folded hands.

iast: paśyāmi devāṁstava deva dehe · sarvāṁstathā bhūtaviśeṣasaṅghān · brahmāṇamīśaṁ kamalāsanastham · ṛṣīṁśca sarvānuragāṁśca divyān
meaning: Arjuna said: I see in your body, O God, all the gods and hosts of beings: Brahma, the lord seated on the lotus, all the sages and the divine serpents.
lifeNote: Everything sacred fits within one presence. You need not choose sides.
actions: Honour different traditions as parts of one whole.
Picture all you hold sacred in one place.
Respect the beliefs of your friends.

iast: anekabāhūdaravaktranetraṁ · paśyāmi tvāṁ sarvato'nantarūpam · nāntaṁ na madhyaṁ na punastavādiṁ · paśyāmi viśveśvara viśvarūpa
meaning: I see you everywhere, of infinite form, with countless arms, bellies, mouths and eyes. I see no end, no middle and no beginning to you, lord of the universe.
lifeNote: Some realities have no edges. Rest in that without needing to grasp it.
words: with many arms, bellies, mouths and eyes
actions: Look at the open sky and feel 'no end'.
Let go of the need to understand everything.
Rest in silence for a few minutes.

iast: kirīṭinaṁ gadinaṁ cakriṇaṁ ca · tejorāśiṁ sarvatodīptimantam · paśyāmi tvāṁ durnirīkṣyaṁ samantā · ddīptānalārkadyutimaprameyam
meaning: I see you crowned, with mace and discus, a mass of light shining everywhere, hard to look at, blazing on all sides like fire and the sun, immeasurable.
lifeNote: Truth can be dazzling. It's fine to be overwhelmed at first.
actions: Notice when truth feels too bright, and stay.
Take a small step towards a big realisation.
Light a lamp and gaze softly.

iast: tvamakṣaraṁ paramaṁ veditavyaṁ · tvamasya viśvasya paraṁ nidhānam · tvamavyayaḥ śāśvatadharmagoptā · sanātanastvaṁ puruṣo mato me
meaning: You are the imperishable, the supreme to be known, the final refuge of this universe. You are the unchanging protector of eternal dharma, the eternal person.
lifeNote: There is a protector of what is right. Trust it when you stand for good.
actions: Stand for what is right in one small matter.
Trust that goodness is protected.
Take refuge in prayer when afraid.

iast: anādimadhyāntamanantavīryam · anantabāhuṁ śaśisūryanetram · paśyāmi tvāṁ dīptahutāśavaktram · svatejasā viśvamidaṁ tapantam
meaning: I see you without beginning, middle or end, of infinite power and countless arms, with the sun and moon as your eyes and blazing fire for a mouth, heating the universe with your radiance.
lifeNote: Sun and moon as eyes: the divine watches over day and night.
words: with moon and sun as eyes
actions: Greet the sun in the morning and moon at night.
Feel watched over with love, not fear.
Read this verse at sunrise.

iast: dyāvāpṛthivyoridamantaraṁ hi · vyāptaṁ tvayaikena diśaśca sarvāḥ · dṛṣṭvā'dbhutaṁ rūpamugraṁ tavedaṁ · lokatrayaṁ pravyathitaṁ mahātman
meaning: The space between heaven and earth and all the directions are filled by you alone. Seeing this wondrous and terrible form of yours, the three worlds tremble, great one.
lifeNote: The divine is both beautiful and fearsome. Reality includes both.
actions: Accept that life includes both beauty and fear.
Face one fearsome fact with calm.
Stand in an open space and feel its size.

iast: amī hi tvāṁ surasaṅghā viśanti · kecidbhītāḥ prāñjalayo gṛṇanti · svastītyuktvā maharṣisiddhasaṅghāḥ · stuvanti tvāṁ stutibhiḥ puṣkalābhiḥ
meaning: Hosts of gods enter into you; some, afraid, praise you with joined palms. Great sages and perfected ones say 'may all be well' and praise you with abundant hymns.
lifeNote: Even in fear, praising and wishing well is a beautiful response.
actions: Say 'may all be well' when you feel afraid.
Sing a hymn when anxious.
Wish well to everyone before sleep.

iast: rudrādityā vasavo ye ca sādhyā · viśve'śvinau marutaścoṣmapāśca · gandharvayakṣāsurasiddhasaṅghā · vīkṣante tvāṁ vismitāścaiva sarve
meaning: The Rudras, Adityas, Vasus, Sadhyas, Vishvadevas, the Ashvins, Maruts, the ancestors, and hosts of gandharvas, yakshas, asuras and siddhas all gaze at you in amazement.
lifeNote: All beings, high and low, share the same wonder before the divine.
actions: Share a moment of wonder with someone today.
Look at the night sky together with family.
Feel kinship with all beings.

iast: rūpaṁ mahatte bahuvaktranetraṁ · mahābāho bahubāhūrupādam · bahūdaraṁ bahudaṁṣṭrākarālaṁ · dṛṣṭvā lokāḥ pravyathitāstathā'ham
meaning: Seeing your great form, mighty one, with many mouths and eyes, arms, thighs and feet, many bellies and terrible with many tusks, the worlds tremble, and so do I.
lifeNote: Arjuna admits he is shaking. Admitting fear is honest and brave.
words: with many arms, thighs and feet
actions: Admit one fear honestly to a trusted friend.
Breathe slowly when you feel overwhelmed.
Be gentle with someone who is afraid.

sanskrit: धृतिं न विन्दामि शमं च विष्णो ॥
iast: nabhaḥspṛśaṁ dīptamanekavarṇaṁ · vyāttānanaṁ dīptaviśālanetram · dṛṣṭvā hi tvāṁ pravyathitāntarātmā · dhṛtiṁ na vindāmi śamaṁ ca viṣṇo
meaning: Seeing you touching the sky, blazing in many colours, with gaping mouths and huge fiery eyes, I am shaken to the core. I find no courage and no peace, Vishnu.
lifeNote: Sometimes reality overwhelms you. It's okay to say 'I can't find my footing.'
actions: Name it when you feel overwhelmed.
Reach out to someone instead of hiding.
Ground yourself: feel your feet on the floor.

sanskrit: दिशो न जाने न लभे च शर्म
iast: daṁṣṭrākarālāni ca te mukhāni · dṛṣṭvaiva kālānalasannibhāni · diśo na jāne na labhe ca śarma · prasīda deveśa jagannivāsa
meaning: Seeing your mouths, terrible with tusks and like the fire at the end of time, I lose all sense of direction and find no peace. Be gracious, lord of gods, refuge of the world.
lifeNote: When lost, the simplest prayer is 'be gracious to me'.
actions: Pray simply: 'be gracious' when lost.
Ask for help without shame.
Comfort a frightened child with calm words.

iast: amī ca tvāṁ dhṛtarāṣṭrasya putrāḥ · sarve sahaivāvanipālasaṅghaiḥ · bhīṣmo droṇaḥ sūtaputrastathā'sau · sahāsmadīyairapi yodhamukhyaiḥ
meaning: And all these sons of Dhritarashtra, with hosts of kings, Bhishma, Drona and Karna, together with our own chief warriors too...
lifeNote: Arjuna sees the outcome of the war already within Krishna. Time reveals what is already in motion.
actions: Reflect on a consequence already in motion in your life.
Make peace with people before conflicts grow.
Pray for those on both sides of a conflict.

iast: vaktrāṇi te tvaramāṇā viśanti · daṁṣṭrākarālāni bhayānakāni · kecidvilagnā daśanāntareṣu · saṁdṛśyante cūrṇitairuttamāṅgaiḥ
meaning: ...rush into your fearsome mouths, terrible with tusks. Some are seen caught between your teeth, their heads crushed.
lifeNote: Time consumes all. Seeing this clearly can make us kinder and less proud.
actions: Let go of one grudge; life is short.
Treat today as precious.
Say a kind word you've been putting off.

iast: yathā nadīnāṁ bahavo'mbuvegāḥ · samudramevābhimukhāḥ dravanti · tathā tavāmī naralokavīrā · viśanti vaktrāṇyabhivijvalanti
meaning: As the many currents of rivers flow towards the ocean, so these heroes of the human world enter your blazing mouths.
lifeNote: All rivers end in the sea. All lives return to the same source.
actions: Watch flowing water and reflect on this verse.
Accept the natural course of life and death.
Honour a hero who has passed.

iast: yathā pradīptaṁ jvalanaṁ pataṅgā · viśanti nāśāya samṛddhavegāḥ · tathaiva nāśāya viśanti lokā · stavāpi vaktrāṇi samṛddhavegāḥ
meaning: As moths rush at great speed into a blazing fire to their destruction, so the worlds rush at great speed into your mouths to their destruction.
lifeNote: Like moths to a flame, we rush towards what harms us. Notice where you do this.
actions: Name one 'flame' you rush towards that harms you.
Slow down before a risky impulse.
Choose safety over thrill in one decision.

iast: lelihyase grasamānaḥ samantā · llokānsamagrānvadanairjvaladbhiḥ · tejobhirāpūrya jagatsamagraṁ · bhāsastavogrāḥ pratapanti viṣṇo
meaning: Devouring all the worlds on every side with your flaming mouths, you lick your lips. Your fierce rays fill the whole world with radiance and scorch it, Vishnu.
lifeNote: Time is relentless. Use it well while you have it.
actions: Do the important thing first today.
Stop wasting time on one habit.
Spend time with someone you love.

iast: ākhyāhi me ko bhavānugrarūpo · namo'stu te devavara prasīda · vijñātumicchāmi bhavantamādyaṁ · na hi prajānāmi tava pravṛttim
meaning: Tell me who you are in this fierce form. Salutations to you, best of gods; be gracious. I wish to know you, the primal one, for I do not understand your purpose.
lifeNote: Even in fear, Arjuna asks to understand. Curiosity is a form of courage.
actions: Ask 'what is this for?' about one hard situation.
Bow before you question.
Seek understanding instead of panicking.

iast: kālo'smi lokakṣayakṛtpravṛddho · lokānsamāhartumiha pravṛttaḥ · ṛte'pi tvāṁ na bhaviṣyanti sarve · ye'vasthitāḥ pratyanīkeṣu yodhāḥ
meaning: Krishna said: I am time, the mighty destroyer of worlds, here to bring the worlds to an end. Even without you, none of the warriors arrayed in the opposing armies will survive.
lifeNote: Time moves with or without you. Your choice is how you play your part.
actions: Focus on your part, not on controlling outcomes.
Accept what time will change regardless.
Act today instead of waiting.

iast: tasmāttvamuttiṣṭha yaśo labhasva · jitvā śatrūn bhuṅkṣva rājyaṁ samṛddham · mayaivaite nihatāḥ pūrvameva · nimittamātraṁ bhava savyasācin
meaning: So stand up and win glory. Conquer your enemies and enjoy a prosperous kingdom. They are already slain by me; be merely the instrument, Arjuna.
lifeNote: You are an instrument, not the whole story. That frees you to act without ego.
actions: Do your task as an instrument, not the owner.
Stand up and start one hard task today.
Let go of the pressure to control everything.

sanskrit: द्रोणं च भीष्मं च जयद्रथं च
iast: droṇaṁ ca bhīṣmaṁ ca jayadrathaṁ ca · karṇaṁ tathā'nyānapi yodhavīrān · mayā hatāṁstvaṁ jahi mā vyathiṣṭhā · yudhyasva jetāsi raṇe sapatnān
meaning: Drona, Bhishma, Jayadratha, Karna and the other heroic warriors are already slain by me. Slay them; do not be distressed. Fight, and you will conquer your enemies in battle.
lifeNote: Do not be paralysed by distress. Do your duty with courage.
actions: Do one hard duty despite feeling upset.
Tell yourself: do not be distressed, act.
Face a fear with a clear plan.

iast: etacchrutvā vacanaṁ keśavasya · kṛtāñjalirvepamānaḥ kirīṭī · namaskṛtvā bhūya evāha kṛṣṇaṁ · sagadgadaṁ bhītabhītaḥ praṇamya
meaning: Sanjaya said: Hearing Krishna's words, Arjuna, trembling, with joined palms, bowed again and spoke to Krishna in a choked voice, very frightened.
lifeNote: Even great warriors tremble. Fear and devotion can coexist.
actions: Allow yourself to feel fear without shame.
Pray even when your voice shakes.
Support someone who is visibly afraid.

iast: sthāne hṛṣīkeśa tava prakīrtyā · jagat prahṛṣyatyanurajyate ca · rakṣāṁsi bhītāni diśo dravanti · sarve namasyanti ca siddhasaṅghāḥ
meaning: Arjuna said: Rightly, Krishna, the world rejoices and delights in your praise. Demons flee in fear in all directions, and hosts of the perfected bow to you.
lifeNote: Praise of the good brings joy and drives away fear and darkness.
actions: Sing or listen to devotional music today.
Praise goodness when you see it.
Use prayer to drive away fear.

iast: kasmācca te na nameranmahātman · garīyase brahmaṇo'pyādikartre · ananta deveśa jagannivāsa · tvamakṣaraṁ sadasattatparaṁ yat
meaning: And why should they not bow to you, great one, greater even than Brahma, the first creator? Infinite one, lord of gods, refuge of the world: you are the imperishable, being and non-being, and what lies beyond both.
lifeNote: When you see what deserves honour, honouring it comes naturally.
actions: Bow to something greater than yourself today.
Honour a person who deserves it.
Reflect on what lies beyond 'is' and 'is not'.

sanskrit: वेत्तासि वेद्यं च परं च धाम
iast: tvamādidevaḥ puruṣaḥ purāṇa · stvamasya viśvasya paraṁ nidhānam · vettāsi vedyaṁ ca paraṁ ca dhāma · tvayā tataṁ viśvamanantarūpa
meaning: You are the first god, the ancient person, the supreme refuge of this universe. You are the knower and the known, and the supreme abode. The universe is pervaded by you, infinite form.
lifeNote: You can rest in what is both the knower and the known.
actions: Notice the 'knower' behind your thoughts.
Take refuge in prayer today.
Reflect on what holds the universe together.

iast: vāyuryamo'gnirvaruṇaḥ śaśāṅkaḥ · prajāpatistvaṁ prapitāmahaśca · namo namaste'stu sahasrakṛtvaḥ · punaśca bhūyo'pi namo namaste
meaning: You are Vayu, Yama, Agni, Varuna and the moon; you are Prajapati and the great-grandfather of all. Salutations to you a thousand times, and again and again salutations to you!
lifeNote: Gratitude can overflow; let it.
actions: Say 'thank you' more than once to someone today.
Offer salutations to the elements: wind, fire, water.
Write a list of a hundred things you're grateful for.

iast: namaḥ purastādatha pṛṣṭhataste · namo'stu te sarvata eva sarva · anantavīryāmitavikramastvaṁ · sarvaṁ samāpnoṣi tato'si sarvaḥ
meaning: Salutations to you in front and behind, salutations on every side, O All! Infinite in strength and boundless in might, you pervade everything; therefore you are everything.
lifeNote: Bowing in every direction reminds you the sacred is everywhere.
actions: Bow to the four directions at sunrise.
Feel surrounded by the divine wherever you are.
Be respectful in every space you enter.

sanskrit: हे कृष्ण हे यादव हे सखेति ।
iast: sakheti matvā prasabhaṁ yaduktaṁ · he kṛṣṇa he yādava he sakheti · ajānatā mahimānaṁ tavedaṁ · mayā pramādātpraṇayena vāpi
meaning: Thinking of you as a friend, I carelessly called you 'Krishna', 'Yadava', 'friend', not knowing your greatness, out of carelessness or affection.
lifeNote: Familiarity can make us careless with people we love. Apologise when you notice it.
actions: Apologise for one careless word to a loved one.
Show respect to a close friend today.
Notice where familiarity makes you casual.

iast: yaccāvahāsārthamasatkṛto'si · vihāraśayyāsanabhojaneṣu · eko'thavāpyacyuta tatsamakṣaṁ · tatkṣāmaye tvāmahamaprameyam
meaning: And if I ever disrespected you in jest, while playing, resting, sitting or eating, alone or in front of others, Krishna, I ask your forgiveness, immeasurable one.
lifeNote: Asking forgiveness for small slights keeps relationships healthy.
words: while playing, resting, sitting or eating
actions: Ask forgiveness for a joke that hurt someone.
Avoid teasing that crosses a line.
Forgive someone who joked at your expense.

iast: pitāsi lokasya carācarasya · tvamasya pūjyaśca gururgarīyān · na tvatsamo'styabhyadhikaḥ kuto'nyo · lokatraye'pyapratimaprabhāva
meaning: You are the father of the world, of all that moves and does not move. You are to be worshipped; you are the greatest teacher. There is no one equal to you in the three worlds, let alone greater, one of matchless power.
lifeNote: The divine is father and teacher. Honour your earthly teachers too.
actions: Thank a teacher who shaped you.
Pray to the divine as your guru before studying.
Honour your father or a father-figure today.

iast: tasmātpraṇamya praṇidhāya kāyaṁ · prasādaye tvāmahamīśamīḍyam · piteva putrasya sakheva sakhyuḥ · priyaḥ priyāyārhasi deva soḍhum
meaning: So I bow down and prostrate my body, seeking your grace, adorable lord. As a father forgives his son, a friend his friend and a lover the beloved, please forgive me, God.
lifeNote: Love forgives easily: like a parent, a friend, a partner.
actions: Forgive someone the way a parent would.
Ask forgiveness from someone close.
Prostrate in prayer once this week.

iast: adṛṣṭapūrvaṁ hṛṣito'smi dṛṣṭvā · bhayena ca pravyathitaṁ mano me · tadeva me darśaya deva rūpaṁ · prasīda deveśa jagannivāsa
meaning: I am thrilled to have seen what was never seen before, yet my mind is shaken with fear. Show me that familiar form of yours, lord of gods; be gracious, refuge of the world.
lifeNote: After overwhelming experiences, we need gentleness and the familiar. That's okay.
actions: After a big experience, return to a simple routine.
Seek comfort in something familiar.
Rest after an emotionally heavy day.

iast: kirīṭinaṁ gadinaṁ cakrahastam · icchāmi tvāṁ draṣṭumahaṁ tathaiva · tenaiva rūpeṇa caturbhujena · sahasrabāho bhava viśvamūrte
meaning: I want to see you as before, crowned, with mace and discus in hand. Thousand-armed one, universal form, take on that four-armed form again.
lifeNote: We relate best to the divine in a form we can love.
actions: Keep a picture or murti you feel close to.
Pray to the form of God you love most.
Respect how others picture the divine.

iast: mayā prasannena tavārjunedaṁ · rūpaṁ paraṁ darśitamātmayogāt · tejomayaṁ viśvamanantamādyaṁ · yanme tvadanyena na dṛṣṭapūrvam
meaning: Krishna said: Pleased with you, Arjuna, I have shown you by my own power this supreme form, radiant, universal, infinite and primal, which no one but you has seen before.
lifeNote: Grace is given, not grabbed. Be open to receive it.
actions: Notice a gift you didn't earn and give thanks.
Be open to grace in an ordinary moment.
Share a blessing you received.

iast: na vedayajñādhyayanairna dānai · rna ca kriyābhirna tapobhirugraiḥ · evaṁrūpaḥ śakya ahaṁ nṛloke · draṣṭuṁ tvadanyena kurupravīra
meaning: Not by the Vedas, sacrifice, study, charity, rituals or severe austerities can I be seen in this form in the human world by anyone but you, hero of the Kurus.
lifeNote: Effort alone can't earn every gift. Some come through love and grace.
actions: Do your practices with love, not as a deal.
Accept that some things can't be forced.
Notice grace where effort had little to do with it.

sanskrit: मा ते व्यथा मा च विमूढभावो
iast: mā te vyathā mā ca vimūḍhabhāvo · dṛṣṭvā rūpaṁ ghoramīdṛṅmamedam · vyapetabhīḥ prītamanāḥ punastvaṁ · tadeva me rūpamidaṁ prapaśya
meaning: Do not be afraid or bewildered at seeing this terrible form of mine. Free from fear and glad at heart, behold again my familiar form.
lifeNote: After the storm comes comfort. Fear can give way to gladness.
actions: Say 'do not be afraid' to yourself in a hard moment.
Comfort someone after a scare.
Notice gladness returning after fear.

iast: ityarjunaṁ vāsudevastathoktvā · svakaṁ rūpaṁ darśayāmāsa bhūyaḥ · āśvāsayāmāsa ca bhītamenaṁ · bhūtvā punaḥ saumyavapurmahātmā
meaning: Sanjaya said: Having spoken thus to Arjuna, Krishna showed his own form again. Taking his gentle form once more, the great one comforted the frightened Arjuna.
lifeNote: Strength that can also be gentle is the best kind.
actions: Comfort someone frightened with gentleness.
Use a soft voice when someone is scared.
Be strong and gentle at the same time today.

sanskrit: दृष्ट्वेदं मानुषं रूपं तव सौम्यं जनार्दन ।
iast: dṛṣṭvedaṁ mānuṣaṁ rūpaṁ tava saumyaṁ janārdana · idānīmasmi saṁvṛttaḥ sacetāḥ prakṛtiṁ gataḥ
meaning: Arjuna said: Seeing this gentle human form of yours, Krishna, I am now composed and have returned to my normal self.
lifeNote: After a shake-up, returning to calm is part of the journey.
actions: Take time to return to calm after a shock.
Do something familiar to ground yourself.
Thank someone who helped you settle.

iast: sudurdarśamidaṁ rūpaṁ dṛṣṭavānasi yanmama · devā apyasya rūpasya nityaṁ darśanakāṅkṣiṇaḥ
meaning: Krishna said: This form of mine that you have seen is very hard to see. Even the gods always long to see it.
lifeNote: Value rare moments of insight; even the great long for them.
