actions: Write down a rare moment of insight you had.
Cherish a deep conversation.
Revisit a place where you felt close to the divine.

sanskrit: नाहं वेदैर्न तपसा न दानेन न चेज्यया ।
शक्य एवंविधो द्रष्टुं दृष्टवानसि मां यथा ॥
iast: nāhaṁ vedairna tapasā na dānena na cejyayā · śakya evaṁvidho draṣṭuṁ dṛṣṭavānasi māṁ yathā
meaning: Not by the Vedas, nor by austerity, charity or ritual worship can I be seen as you have seen me.
lifeNote: Rituals and effort are good, but love is what truly opens the door.
actions: Bring love to one ritual you do mechanically.
Value relationship over routine in faith.
Pray from the heart, not from habit.

sanskrit: ज्ञातुं द्रष्टुं च तत्त्वेन प्रवेष्टुं च परंतप ॥
iast: bhaktyā tvananyayā śakyamahamevaṁvidho'rjuna · jñātuṁ draṣṭuṁ ca tattvena praveṣṭuṁ ca paraṁtapa
meaning: But by undivided devotion, Arjuna, I can be known like this, seen in truth and even entered into.
lifeNote: Wholehearted love is the key: to know, to see and to become one.
actions: Give your full heart to one thing today.
Spend five minutes in wholehearted prayer.
Love someone without holding back.

sanskrit: निर्वैरः सर्वभूतेषु यः स मामेति पाण्डव ॥
iast: matkarmakṛnmatparamo madbhaktaḥ saṅgavarjitaḥ · nirvairaḥ sarvabhūteṣu yaḥ sa māmeti pāṇḍava
meaning: One who does my work, holds me as the highest, is devoted to me, free from attachment and without enmity towards any being, comes to me, Arjuna.
lifeNote: The whole path in one line: work, devotion, detachment and no enmity.
actions: Let go of one enmity today.
Do your work as service.
Memorise this verse as a summary of the path.

iast: evaṁ satatayuktā ye bhaktāstvāṁ paryupāsate · ye cāpyakṣaramavyaktaṁ teṣāṁ ke yogavittamāḥ
meaning: Arjuna said: Some devotees worship you with constant devotion; others worship the imperishable, unmanifest. Which of them know yoga best?
lifeNote: Should you pray to a form or meditate on the formless? Arjuna asks a question many people share.
actions: Notice whether you feel closer to a form or to silence.
Respect friends whose way of worship differs.
Ask an elder how they pray.

sanskrit: मय्यावेश्य मनो ये मां नित्ययुक्ता उपासते ।
iast: mayyāveśya mano ye māṁ nityayuktā upāsate · śraddhayā parayopetāste me yuktatamā matāḥ
meaning: Krishna said: Those who fix their minds on me and worship me with constant devotion and supreme faith, I consider the most united with me.
lifeNote: Loving devotion with full faith is the most direct path.
actions: Keep your mind on the divine during one task today.
Pray with full trust tonight.
Choose a form of God you feel close to.

iast: ye tvakṣaramanirdeśyamavyaktaṁ paryupāsate · sarvatragamacintyaṁ ca kūṭasthamacalaṁ dhruvam
meaning: But those who worship the imperishable, indefinable and unmanifest, the all-pervading, unthinkable, unchanging, immovable and eternal...
lifeNote: Meditating on the formless is also a real path, though a demanding one.
actions: Try five minutes of silent meditation without an image.
Notice what in you never changes.
Respect people who meditate on the formless.

iast: saṁniyamyendriyagrāmaṁ sarvatra samabuddhayaḥ · te prāpnuvanti māmeva sarvabhūtahite ratāḥ
meaning: ...restraining all the senses, even-minded everywhere and devoted to the welfare of all beings, they too reach me.
lifeNote: Whatever your path, caring for all beings is part of it.
words: in the welfare of all beings
actions: Do one act for the welfare of others today.
Stay even-minded in one tense moment.
Restrain one sense habit this week.

iast: kleśo'dhikatarasteṣāmavyaktāsaktacetasām · avyaktā hi gatirduḥkhaṁ dehavadbhiravāpyate
meaning: The difficulty is greater for those whose minds are set on the unmanifest, for the unmanifest goal is hard for embodied beings to reach.
lifeNote: It's natural to need something to hold on to. Choose a path that suits you.
words: whose minds are set on the unmanifest
actions: Pick a practice that fits your nature.
Don't feel guilty for needing a concrete form.
Be patient with a hard spiritual practice.

sanskrit: ये तु सर्वाणि कर्माणि मयि संन्यस्य मत्पराः ।
iast: ye tu sarvāṇi karmāṇi mayi saṁnyasya matparāḥ · ananyenaiva yogena māṁ dhyāyanta upāsate
meaning: But those who offer all their actions to me, regard me as supreme, and worship me meditating with undivided devotion...
lifeNote: Offering every action turns a busy life into prayer.
actions: Offer your work today with a short prayer.
Meditate on the divine for five minutes.
Keep your heart on one goal.

iast: teṣāmahaṁ samuddhartā mṛtyusaṁsārasāgarāt · bhavāmi nacirātpārtha mayyāveśitacetasām
meaning: ...for them, whose minds are fixed on me, I soon become the one who lifts them out of the ocean of death and rebirth, Arjuna.
lifeNote: You are not alone in deep waters; help reaches those who hold on in love.
words: from the ocean of death and rebirth
actions: In a hard time, remember you will be lifted.
Reach out a hand to someone 'drowning'.
Hold on to your practice in difficult weeks.

sanskrit: मय्येव मन आधत्स्व मयि बुद्धिं निवेशय ।
निवसिष्यसि मय्येव अत ऊर्ध्वं न संशयः ॥
iast: mayyeva mana ādhatsva mayi buddhiṁ niveśaya · nivasiṣyasi mayyeva ata ūrdhvaṁ na saṁśayaḥ
meaning: Fix your mind on me alone and place your understanding in me. You will then live in me; there is no doubt.
lifeNote: Heart and head together: that is how you abide in what you love.
actions: Think and feel about one teaching today.
Fix your mind on one sacred thought.
Let your decisions reflect your love.

sanskrit: अथ चित्तं समाधातुं न शक्नोषि मयि स्थिरम् ।
iast: atha cittaṁ samādhātuṁ na śaknoṣi mayi sthiram · abhyāsayogena tato māmicchāptuṁ dhanañjaya
meaning: If you cannot fix your mind steadily on me, then seek to reach me through the yoga of practice, Arjuna.
lifeNote: If you can't do it naturally, practise. Practice makes devotion steady.
actions: Set a daily time for practice, however short.
Repeat a small habit until it becomes easy.
Don't quit when focus is hard; practise.

iast: abhyāse'pyasamartho'si matkarmaparamo bhava · madarthamapi karmāṇi kurvan siddhimavāpsyasi
meaning: If you are unable even to practise, then devote yourself to work for my sake. Doing actions for me, you will attain perfection.
lifeNote: If you can't meditate, serve. Work done for the divine is a full path.
actions: Do your work today as service to God.
Volunteer for an hour this week.
Dedicate a household chore as an offering.

iast: athaitadapyaśakto'si kartuṁ madyogamāśritaḥ · sarvakarmaphalatyāgaṁ tataḥ kuru yatātmavān
meaning: If you cannot do even this, then take refuge in me, be self-controlled, and give up the fruit of all your actions.
lifeNote: At the very least, let go of clinging to results. That alone brings peace.
words: giving up the fruit of all actions
actions: Do your best today and let the result go.
Stop checking for results after you submit.
Practise self-control in one habit.

iast: śreyo hi jñānamabhyāsājjñānāddhyānaṁ viśiṣyate · dhyānātkarmaphalatyāgastyāgācchāntiranantaram
meaning: Knowledge is better than mere practice; meditation is better than knowledge; giving up the fruit of action is better than meditation. From such giving up, peace follows at once.
lifeNote: Letting go of results brings immediate peace. Try it today.
words: giving up the fruit of action
actions: Let go of one result right now and feel the relief.
Meditate for five minutes.
Study the meaning behind a practice.

sanskrit: अद्वेष्टा सर्वभूतानां मैत्रः करुण एव च ।
iast: adveṣṭā sarvabhūtānāṁ maitraḥ karuṇa eva ca · nirmamo nirahaṅkāraḥ samaduḥkhasukhaḥ kṣamī
meaning: One who has no hatred for any being, is friendly and compassionate, free from possessiveness and ego, even in pain and pleasure, and forgiving...
lifeNote: This is the portrait of a loving person. Try one quality at a time.
actions: Be friendly to someone you usually ignore.
Forgive one small hurt today.
Drop 'mine' in one argument.

iast: santuṣṭaḥ satataṁ yogī yatātmā dṛḍhaniścayaḥ · mayyarpitamanobuddhiryo madbhaktaḥ sa me priyaḥ
meaning: ...always content, self-controlled, firm in resolve, with mind and intellect offered to me: such a devotee is dear to me.
lifeNote: Contentment and firm resolve together make a strong, peaceful person.
actions: Practise contentment with what you have today.
Make one firm resolution and keep it.
Offer your thoughts to God before sleep.

sanskrit: हर्षामर्षभयोद्वेगैर्मुक्तो यः स च मे प्रियः ॥
iast: yasmānnodvijate loko lokānnodvijate ca yaḥ · harṣāmarṣabhayodvegairmukto yaḥ sa ca me priyaḥ
meaning: One who does not disturb the world and is not disturbed by it, who is free from elation, anger, fear and anxiety, is dear to me.
lifeNote: Don't disturb others, and don't let them disturb you. That's real peace.
words: from elation, anger, fear and anxiety
actions: Avoid creating drama for anyone today.
Let one irritating remark pass without reacting.
Calm your anxiety with slow breathing.

sanskrit: सर्वारम्भपरित्यागी यो मद्भक्तः स मे प्रियः ॥
iast: anapekṣaḥ śucirdakṣa udāsīno gatavyathaḥ · sarvārambhaparityāgī yo madbhaktaḥ sa me priyaḥ
meaning: One who expects nothing, is pure, skilful, unconcerned, free from distress, and gives up all selfish undertakings: such a devotee is dear to me.
lifeNote: Skilful work without expectations is a sign of maturity.
actions: Do one task skilfully without expecting thanks.
Keep your space and mind clean today.
Let go of a distress you've been carrying.

sanskrit: यो न हृष्यति न द्वेष्टि न शोचति न काङ्क्षति ।
iast: yo na hṛṣyati na dveṣṭi na śocati na kāṅkṣati · śubhāśubhaparityāgī bhaktimānyaḥ sa me priyaḥ
meaning: One who neither rejoices nor hates, neither grieves nor craves, who has given up both good and bad, and is full of devotion, is dear to me.
lifeNote: Steady through ups and downs, with love at the centre.
actions: Respond to today's good and bad news with the same calm.
Notice a craving and let it pass.
Keep devotion steady through mood changes.

sanskrit: समः शत्रौ च मित्रे च तथा मानापमानयोः ।
iast: samaḥ śatrau ca mitre ca tathā mānāpamānayoḥ · śītoṣṇasukhaduḥkheṣu samaḥ saṅgavivarjitaḥ
meaning: One who is the same to enemy and friend, in honour and dishonour, in cold and heat, pleasure and pain, and free from attachment...
lifeNote: Equanimity is strength, not coldness.
words: in cold and heat, pleasure and pain
actions: Treat a rival with the same courtesy as a friend.
Stay calm whether praised or criticised.
Accept today's weather without complaint.

iast: tulyanindāstutirmaunī santuṣṭo yenakenacit · aniketaḥ sthiramatirbhaktimānme priyo naraḥ
meaning: ...who is the same in blame and praise, quiet, content with whatever comes, not attached to a home, steady-minded and devoted: such a person is dear to me.
lifeNote: Speak less, want less, and stay steady. That makes a heart dear to God.
actions: Spend one hour speaking only when needed.
Be content with what today brings.
Don't defend yourself against one criticism.

iast: ye tu dharmyāmṛtamidaṁ yathoktaṁ paryupāsate · śraddadhānā matparamā bhaktāste'tīva me priyāḥ
meaning: But those who follow this nectar of dharma as I have taught it, with faith and with me as their highest goal, are very dear to me.
lifeNote: Living these qualities with faith makes you deeply loved.
actions: Pick one quality from this chapter to practise this week.
Read chapter 12 again slowly.
Share one verse from this chapter with a friend.

sanskrit: प्रकृतिं पुरुषं चैव क्षेत्रं क्षेत्रज्ञमेव च ।
iast: prakṛtiṁ puruṣaṁ caiva kṣetraṁ kṣetrajñameva ca · etadveditumicchāmi jñānaṁ jñeyaṁ ca keśava
meaning: Arjuna said: Krishna, I wish to know about nature and spirit, the field and the knower of the field, knowledge and what is to be known.
lifeNote: What am I, and what do I know? Good questions to start any inner journey.
actions: Write down 'who am I?' and answer for five minutes.
Notice the difference between your body and your awareness.
Ask a teacher about the 'field and the knower'.

sanskrit: एतद्यो वेत्ति तं प्राहुः क्षेत्रज्ञ इति तद्विदः ॥
iast: idaṁ śarīraṁ kaunteya kṣetramityabhidhīyate · etadyo vetti taṁ prāhuḥ kṣetrajña iti tadvidaḥ
meaning: Krishna said: This body is called the field, Arjuna. The one who knows it is called the knower of the field by those who understand.
lifeNote: Your body is a field; you are the one who knows it. That small distance brings calm.
actions: When in pain, notice: 'I am aware of this pain.'
Look after your body as a field you tend.
Watch your body's sensations for two minutes.

sanskrit: क्षेत्रज्ञं चापि मां विद्धि सर्वक्षेत्रेषु भारत ।
iast: kṣetrajñaṁ cāpi māṁ viddhi sarvakṣetreṣu bhārata · kṣetrakṣetrajñayorjñānaṁ yattajjñānaṁ mataṁ mama
meaning: Know me as the knower in all fields, Arjuna. Knowledge of the field and its knower is, in my view, true knowledge.
lifeNote: The same awareness looks out through every pair of eyes.
words: of the field and its knower
actions: Look into someone's eyes and remember this verse.
Treat others' awareness as precious as yours.
Reflect on what true knowledge means.

sanskrit: तत्क्षेत्रं यच्च यादृक् च यद्विकारि यतश्च यत् ।
स च यो यत्प्रभावश्च तत्समासेन मे शृणु ॥
iast: tatkṣetraṁ yacca yādṛk ca yadvikāri yataśca yat · sa ca yo yatprabhāvaśca tatsamāsena me śṛṇu
meaning: Hear from me briefly what the field is, what it is like, how it changes, where it comes from, and who the knower is and what powers he has.
lifeNote: A clear, short explanation is a gift. Listen well.
actions: Summarise a topic in five lines.
Listen to a short lesson with full attention.
Ask 'what, how, why' about one idea.

iast: ṛṣibhirbahudhā gītaṁ chandobhirvividhaiḥ pṛthak · brahmasūtrapadaiścaiva hetumadbhirviniścitaiḥ
meaning: This has been sung by sages in many ways, in various hymns, and set out in the reasoned, conclusive words of the Brahma Sutras.
lifeNote: Truth has been tested by many minds over centuries. You stand on their shoulders.
actions: Read a short passage from an Upanishad.
Compare two teachers on the same topic.
Respect tradition while asking questions.

iast: mahābhūtānyahaṅkāro buddhiravyaktameva ca · indriyāṇi daśaikaṁ ca pañca cendriyagocarāḥ
meaning: The great elements, ego, intellect and the unmanifest; the ten senses and the mind; and the five objects of the senses...
lifeNote: Your body-mind has many parts. Knowing them helps you manage them.
actions: Name the five senses and notice each for a minute.
Notice your ego reacting in one conversation.
Draw a simple map of 'what I am made of'.

iast: icchā dveṣaḥ sukhaṁ duḥkhaṁ saṅghātaścetanādhṛtiḥ · etatkṣetraṁ samāsena savikāramudāhṛtam
meaning: ...desire, aversion, pleasure, pain, the body, awareness and steadfastness: this, in brief, is the field with all its changes.
lifeNote: Even your desires and moods belong to the 'field'. You can observe them.
actions: Observe one desire without acting on it.
Notice pleasure and pain as passing states.
Practise steadiness in one small difficulty.

iast: amānitvamadambhitvamahiṁsā kṣāntirārjavam · ācāryopāsanaṁ śaucaṁ sthairyamātmavinigrahaḥ
meaning: Humility, lack of pretence, non-violence, patience, honesty, service to the teacher, cleanliness, steadiness and self-control...
lifeNote: Real knowledge shows up as character: humility, patience and honesty.
actions: Be humble about one success today.
Practise patience in a queue or traffic.
Help a teacher in some small way.

iast: indriyārtheṣu vairāgyamanahaṅkāra eva ca · janmamṛtyujarāvyādhiduḥkhadoṣānudarśanam
meaning: ...dispassion towards sense objects, absence of ego, and clearly seeing the pain and flaws in birth, death, old age and illness...
lifeNote: Seeing life's hard facts clearly makes you wiser and kinder.
words: seeing the pain of birth, death, old age and illness
actions: Visit someone who is ill or elderly.
Reflect on ageing without fear.
Reduce one indulgence this week.

iast: asaktiranabhiṣvaṅgaḥ putradāragṛhādiṣu · nityaṁ ca samacittatvamiṣṭāniṣṭopapattiṣu
meaning: ...non-attachment, not clinging to children, spouse, home and the like, and constant even-mindedness in wanted and unwanted events...
lifeNote: Love your family deeply but without clinging; it makes love healthier.
words: to children, spouse, home and the like
actions: Give a family member space to make their own choice.
Stay calm when plans at home change.
Love without trying to control.

iast: mayi cānanyayogena bhaktiravyabhicāriṇī · viviktadeśasevitvamaratirjanasaṁsadi
meaning: ...unwavering devotion to me through undivided yoga, a liking for quiet places and a distaste for crowds...
lifeNote: Quiet time is not antisocial; it feeds the soul.
actions: Spend twenty minutes in a quiet place today.
Skip one noisy gathering if it drains you.
Keep devotion steady through the week.

iast: adhyātmajñānanityatvaṁ tattvajñānārthadarśanam · etajjñānamiti proktamajñānaṁ yadato'nyathā
meaning: ...constancy in self-knowledge and keeping in view the goal of true knowledge. This is called knowledge; whatever is contrary to it is ignorance.
lifeNote: Knowledge is a way of living, not just a set of facts.
words: seeing the goal of true knowledge
actions: Check whether what you know is changing how you live.
Spend time daily on self-reflection.
Keep your life's goal in view this week.

iast: jñeyaṁ yattatpravakṣyāmi yajjñātvā'mṛtamaśnute · anādimatparaṁ brahma na sattannāsaducyate
meaning: I will describe what is to be known, knowing which one attains immortality: the beginningless supreme Brahman, which is said to be neither being nor non-being.
lifeNote: Some truths are beyond 'is' and 'isn't'. Let them stretch your mind.
actions: Sit with a question that has no simple answer.
Read this verse slowly three times.
Notice the limits of words.

iast: sarvataḥ pāṇipādaṁ tatsarvato'kṣiśiromukham · sarvataḥ śrutimalloke sarvamāvṛtya tiṣṭhati
meaning: With hands and feet everywhere, eyes, heads and mouths everywhere, and ears everywhere in the world, it exists enveloping all.
lifeNote: The divine works through every hand. Yours too.
actions: Use your hands today to help someone.
See helpers around you as the divine at work.
Listen as if the whole world were listening.

iast: sarvendriyaguṇābhāsaṁ sarvendriyavivarjitam · asaktaṁ sarvabhṛccaiva nirguṇaṁ guṇabhoktṛ ca
meaning: It shines through all the senses, yet is without senses; unattached, yet sustaining all; beyond the qualities, yet experiencing them.
lifeNote: Paradox is a sign you're near something deep.
actions: Notice awareness shining through your senses.
Sit with one paradox today.
Write your own 'both/and' statement about life.

iast: bahirantaśca bhūtānāmacaraṁ carameva ca · sūkṣmatvāttadavijñeyaṁ dūrasthaṁ cāntike ca tat
meaning: It is outside and inside all beings, unmoving and moving. Being subtle, it cannot be known by the senses. It is far away and also near.
lifeNote: What you seek is both far and very near. Look within too.
actions: Look for the divine within yourself today.
Notice how near and far can be the same.
Sit still and feel the presence inside.

sanskrit: अविभक्तं च भूतेषु विभक्तमिव च स्थितम् ।
भूतभर्तृ च तज्ज्ञेयं ग्रसिष्णु प्रभविष्णु च ॥
iast: avibhaktaṁ ca bhūteṣu vibhaktamiva ca sthitam · bhūtabhartṛ ca tajjñeyaṁ grasiṣṇu prabhaviṣṇu ca
meaning: Undivided, it seems divided among beings. Know it as the sustainer of beings, their devourer and their creator.
lifeNote: We look separate, but we share one life.
actions: Treat someone as part of the same life as you.
Notice the unity behind a family quarrel.
Reflect on creation, sustenance and endings.

sanskrit: ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं ज्ञानगम्यं हृदि सर्वस्य विष्ठितम् ॥
iast: jyotiṣāmapi tajjyotistamasaḥ paramucyate · jñānaṁ jñeyaṁ jñānagamyaṁ hṛdi sarvasya viṣṭhitam
meaning: It is the light of all lights, said to be beyond darkness. It is knowledge, the known and the goal of knowledge, dwelling in the heart of all.
lifeNote: The light you seek already lives in your heart.
actions: Place your hand on your heart and sit quietly.
Light a lamp and remember this verse.
Be a light for someone in a dark time.

sanskrit: इति क्षेत्रं तथा ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं चोक्तं समासतः ।
iast: iti kṣetraṁ tathā jñānaṁ jñeyaṁ coktaṁ samāsataḥ · madbhakta etadvijñāya madbhāvāyopapadyate
meaning: Thus the field, knowledge and the known have been briefly described. Understanding this, my devotee becomes fit to reach my state.
lifeNote: Understanding prepares the heart for union.
actions: Review what you learnt this week.
Combine study with devotion.
Share a summary with a friend.

iast: prakṛtiṁ puruṣaṁ caiva viddhyanādī ubhāvapi · vikārāṁśca guṇāṁścaiva viddhi prakṛtisaṁbhavān
meaning: Know that nature and spirit are both without beginning. Know too that all changes and qualities are born of nature.
lifeNote: Changes come from nature; you, the spirit, are the witness.
actions: Watch a mood change and remember you are the witness.
Accept changes in your body calmly.
Notice what in you stays the same.

iast: kāryakāraṇakartṛtve hetuḥ prakṛtirucyate · puruṣaḥ sukhaduḥkhānāṁ bhoktṛtve heturucyate
meaning: Nature is said to be the cause of the body, the senses and action. Spirit is said to be the cause of experiencing pleasure and pain.
lifeNote: Nature does; spirit experiences. Know which is which.
words: in producing effects, means and agency
actions: Notice how much of your day 'just happens'.
Watch your reactions to pleasure and pain.
Reflect on who is experiencing your life.

iast: puruṣaḥ prakṛtistho hi bhuṅkte prakṛtijānguṇān · kāraṇaṁ guṇasaṅgo'sya sadasadyonijanmasu
meaning: Seated in nature, the spirit experiences the qualities born of nature. Attachment to these qualities is the cause of its births in good and bad wombs.
lifeNote: Attachment shapes where life takes you. Loosen it gently.
words: of births in good and bad wombs
actions: Notice one attachment shaping your choices.
Loosen your grip on one preference today.
Reflect on what drives your big decisions.

iast: upadraṣṭā'numantā ca bhartā bhoktā maheśvaraḥ · paramātmeti cāpyukto dehe'sminpuruṣaḥ paraḥ
meaning: In this body the supreme spirit is called the witness, the permitter, the supporter, the experiencer, the great lord and the supreme self.
lifeNote: A silent witness lives within you. Turn to it when life is loud.
actions: Take one minute to just witness your thoughts.
Ask the 'inner witness' for guidance.
Notice calm beneath busy thoughts.

sanskrit: य एवं वेत्ति पुरुषं प्रकृतिं च गुणैः सह ।
iast: ya evaṁ vetti puruṣaṁ prakṛtiṁ ca guṇaiḥ saha · sarvathā vartamāno'pi na sa bhūyo'bhijāyate
meaning: One who knows spirit, nature and its qualities in this way is not born again, however he lives.
lifeNote: Understanding frees you, whatever your circumstances.
actions: Apply one teaching in an ordinary situation.
Remember your inner freedom in a hard place.
Reflect on how understanding has freed you before.

iast: dhyānenātmani paśyanti kecidātmānamātmanā · anye sāṁkhyena yogena karmayogena cāpare
meaning: Some see the self within themselves through meditation; others through the path of knowledge; and others through the yoga of action.
lifeNote: Different people find truth in different ways. All are valid.
actions: Notice which path fits you best: meditation, study or service.
Respect a friend's different path.
Try a path you usually skip for one day.

iast: anye tvevamajānantaḥ śrutvā'nyebhya upāsate · te'pi cātitarantyeva mṛtyuṁ śrutiparāyaṇāḥ
meaning: Others, not knowing this, worship by hearing from others. They too, devoted to what they hear, cross beyond death.
lifeNote: Even listening with faith to the wise is a path that works.
actions: Listen to a talk by a wise teacher this week.
Learn from elders' stories.
Value the simple faith of others.

iast: yāvatsañjāyate kiñcitsattvaṁ sthāvarajaṅgamam · kṣetrakṣetrajñasaṁyogāttadviddhi bharatarṣabha
meaning: Whatever being is born, moving or unmoving, know that it arises from the union of the field and its knower, Arjuna.
lifeNote: Every living thing is matter joined with awareness. Treat all life with respect.
words: from the union of field and knower
actions: Treat plants and animals with care today.
Reflect on the miracle of being alive.
Thank your body for carrying your awareness.

iast: samaṁ sarveṣu bhūteṣu tiṣṭhantaṁ parameśvaram · vinaśyatsvavinaśyantaṁ yaḥ paśyati sa paśyati
meaning: One who sees the supreme lord dwelling equally in all beings, the imperishable within the perishing, truly sees.
lifeNote: True sight sees the lasting within the passing, and the same in everyone.
actions: See the lasting in someone who is ageing.
Treat everyone as carrying the same divine.
Comfort grief by remembering what doesn't perish.

sanskrit: न हिनस्त्यात्मनाऽऽत्मानं ततो याति परां गतिम् ॥
iast: samaṁ paśyanhi sarvatra samavasthitamīśvaram · na hinastyātmanā''tmānaṁ tato yāti parāṁ gatim
meaning: Seeing the same lord equally present everywhere, one does not harm the self by the self, and so reaches the supreme goal.
lifeNote: When you see the divine in everyone, you stop hurting yourself and others.
actions: Avoid harsh self-talk today.
Refrain from hurting someone in anger.
See the divine in yourself and be kind to yourself.

iast: prakṛtyaiva ca karmāṇi kriyamāṇāni sarvaśaḥ · yaḥ paśyati tathā''tmānamakartāraṁ sa paśyati
meaning: One who sees that all actions are performed by nature alone, and that the self is not the doer, truly sees.
lifeNote: Much happens through you, not by you. Hold credit and blame lightly.
actions: Take less credit for one success today.
Take less blame for something beyond your control.
Watch your body work without 'you' pushing it.

sanskrit: तत एव च विस्तारं ब्रह्म सम्पद्यते तदा ॥
iast: yadā bhūtapṛthagbhāvamekasthamanupaśyati · tata eva ca vistāraṁ brahma sampadyate tadā
meaning: When one sees the separate existence of beings as resting in the one, and expanding from it alone, one then attains Brahman.
lifeNote: Many from one: that vision dissolves loneliness.
actions: See your community as branches of one tree.
Reach out to someone who feels separate.
Reflect on the unity behind diversity.

sanskrit: शरीरस्थोऽपि कौन्तेय न करोति न लिप्यते ॥
iast: anāditvānnirguṇatvātparamātmāyamavyayaḥ · śarīrastho'pi kaunteya na karoti na lipyate
meaning: Being without beginning and beyond the qualities, this imperishable supreme self, though dwelling in the body, Arjuna, neither acts nor is tainted.
lifeNote: Your deepest self stays clean, whatever happens to the body.
actions: Remember your untouched core during a hard day.
Forgive yourself, knowing your essence is pure.
Comfort someone who feels 'dirty' with shame.

iast: yathā sarvagataṁ saukṣmyādākāśaṁ nopalipyate · sarvatrāvasthito dehe tathā''tmā nopalipyate
meaning: As all-pervading space is not tainted because of its subtlety, so the self, present everywhere in the body, is not tainted.
lifeNote: Like the sky, you can hold storms without being stained by them.
actions: Picture yourself as the sky during a stormy feeling.
Let one insult pass through without sticking.
Look at the sky for a minute and breathe.

sanskrit: क्षेत्रं क्षेत्री तथा कृत्स्नं प्रकाशयति भारत ॥
iast: yathā prakāśayatyekaḥ kṛtsnaṁ lokamimaṁ raviḥ · kṣetraṁ kṣetrī tathā kṛtsnaṁ prakāśayati bhārata
meaning: As the one sun lights up this whole world, so the knower of the field lights up the whole field, Arjuna.
lifeNote: Your awareness lights up your whole life, like the sun lights the world.
actions: Watch the sunrise and remember this verse.
Bring bright awareness to one dull task.
Notice how attention 'lights up' what you look at.

sanskrit: भूतप्रकृतिमोक्षं च ये विदुर्यान्ति ते परम् ॥
iast: kṣetrakṣetrajñayorevamantaraṁ jñānacakṣuṣā · bhūtaprakṛtimokṣaṁ ca ye viduryānti te param
meaning: Those who see with the eye of knowledge the difference between the field and its knower, and the way to freedom from nature, reach the supreme.
lifeNote: Seeing clearly that you are more than body and mind is the start of freedom.
words: of the field and its knower
freedom from the nature of beings
actions: Practise watching your mind for five minutes.
Write: 'I am the one who knows my thoughts.'
Reread this chapter's key verses.

sanskrit: यज्ज्ञात्वा मुनयः सर्वे परां सिद्धिमितो गताः ॥
iast: paraṁ bhūyaḥ pravakṣyāmi jñānānāṁ jñānamuttamam · yajjñātvā munayaḥ sarve parāṁ siddhimito gatāḥ
meaning: Krishna said: I will declare again the supreme knowledge, the highest of all knowledge. Knowing it, all the sages have gone from here to supreme perfection.
lifeNote: Some knowledge changes everything. This chapter is about understanding your own moods and drives.
actions: Read this chapter with a notebook.
Commit to learning one deep idea well.
Share a key idea with a friend.

sanskrit: सर्गेऽपि नोपजायन्ते प्रलये न व्यथन्ति च ॥
iast: idaṁ jñānamupāśritya mama sādharmyamāgatāḥ · sarge'pi nopajāyante pralaye na vyathanti ca
meaning: Taking refuge in this knowledge, they have come to share my nature. They are not born at creation, nor troubled at dissolution.
lifeNote: Understanding can make you unshaken by beginnings and endings.
actions: Stay calm through one big change this week.
Reflect on what remains through all changes.
Take refuge in a teaching when life shifts.

iast: mama yonirmahadbrahma tasmin garbhaṁ dadhāmyaham · saṁbhavaḥ sarvabhūtānāṁ tato bhavati bhārata
meaning: Great nature is my womb; into it I place the seed. From that comes the birth of all beings, Arjuna.
lifeNote: Life comes from a union of matter and spirit. Every birth is sacred.
actions: Celebrate a new baby or birth in your circle.
Treat your own life as a sacred birth.
Tell a child they are a precious seed.

iast: sarvayoniṣu kaunteya mūrtayaḥ sambhavanti yāḥ · tāsāṁ brahma mahadyonirahaṁ bījapradaḥ pitā
meaning: Whatever forms are born in any womb, Arjuna, great nature is their womb and I am the seed-giving father.
lifeNote: All beings share one mother and one father. We are one family.
actions: Treat a stranger as a sibling today.
Care for an animal as family.
Teach a child that all living things are related.

iast: sattvaṁ rajastama iti guṇāḥ prakṛtisaṁbhavāḥ · nibadhnanti mahābāho dehe dehinamavyayam
meaning: Goodness, passion and inertia: these qualities born of nature bind the imperishable self to the body, Arjuna.
lifeNote: Clarity, restlessness and dullness: notice which one is in charge right now.
actions: Label your current state: calm, restless or dull.
Do one thing that brings out your calm side.
Notice how each state affects your choices.

iast: tatra sattvaṁ nirmalatvātprakāśakamanāmayam · sukhasaṅgena badhnāti jñānasaṅgena cānagha
meaning: Of these, goodness, being pure, gives light and health. Yet it binds through attachment to happiness and to knowledge, sinless Arjuna.
lifeNote: Even good qualities can trap you if you cling to feeling good or being right.
actions: Notice clinging to being 'the one who knows'.
Enjoy happiness without needing it to last.
Stay humble about your knowledge.

iast: rajo rāgātmakaṁ viddhi tṛṣṇāsaṅgasamudbhavam · tannibadhnāti kaunteya karmasaṅgena dehinam
meaning: Know passion as the nature of craving, born of thirst and attachment. It binds the embodied self through attachment to action, Arjuna.
lifeNote: Restless craving keeps you busy but rarely satisfied. Notice it.
actions: Notice busyness driven by craving.
Pause before taking on one more task.
Rest without guilt for an hour.

iast: tamastvajñānajaṁ viddhi mohanaṁ sarvadehinām · pramādālasyanidrābhistannibadhnāti bhārata
meaning: Know inertia as born of ignorance, deluding all embodied beings. It binds through carelessness, laziness and sleep, Arjuna.
lifeNote: Laziness and carelessness are not character flaws forever; they are a state you can shift.
actions: Do a five-minute task to break inertia.
Go to bed and wake on time.
Notice carelessness and slow down.

sanskrit: सत्त्वं सुखे सञ्जयति रजः कर्मणि भारत ।
iast: sattvaṁ sukhe sañjayati rajaḥ karmaṇi bhārata · jñānamāvṛtya tu tamaḥ pramāde sañjayatyuta
meaning: Goodness attaches one to happiness, passion to action, Arjuna. Inertia, covering knowledge, attaches one to carelessness.
lifeNote: Each mood pulls you somewhere. Know where it's pulling.
actions: Ask 'where is this mood pulling me?' once today.
Use a calm mood for important decisions.
Avoid big decisions when dull or agitated.

sanskrit: रजः सत्त्वं तमश्चैव तमः सत्त्वं रजस्तथा ॥
iast: rajastamaścābhibhūya sattvaṁ bhavati bhārata · rajaḥ sattvaṁ tamaścaiva tamaḥ sattvaṁ rajastathā
meaning: Goodness prevails by overpowering passion and inertia, Arjuna. Passion prevails by overpowering goodness and inertia, and inertia likewise by overpowering goodness and passion.
lifeNote: Moods compete in you all day. You can feed the one you want to win.
actions: Feed calm: a walk, silence, good food.
Starve restlessness by reducing screen time.
Notice which mood wins most often this week.

iast: sarvadvāreṣu dehe'sminprakāśa upajāyate · jñānaṁ yadā tadā vidyādvivṛddhaṁ sattvamityuta
meaning: When the light of knowledge shines through all the gates of the body, know that goodness has increased.
lifeNote: Clarity feels like light in your eyes, ears and mind. Notice when it comes.
actions: Notice when you feel clear and bright.
Study when your mind feels light.
Recreate the conditions of your clearest days.

iast: lobhaḥ pravṛttirārambhaḥ karmaṇāmaśamaḥ spṛhā · rajasyetāni jāyante vivṛddhe bharatarṣabha
meaning: Greed, constant activity, taking on actions, restlessness and longing arise when passion increases, Arjuna.
lifeNote: If you feel greedy and restless, passion is high. Slow down.
actions: Notice restlessness and take ten slow breaths.
Finish one task before starting another.
Skip one impulse purchase.

iast: aprakāśo'pravṛttiśca pramādo moha eva ca · tamasyetāni jāyante vivṛddhe kurunandana
meaning: Darkness, inactivity, carelessness and delusion arise when inertia increases, Arjuna.
lifeNote: Feeling foggy and stuck is a sign of inertia, not your true self. Move a little.
actions: When stuck, do one tiny physical task.
Open the curtains and let light in.
Talk to a friend when you feel foggy.

sanskrit: यदा सत्त्वे प्रवृद्धे तु प्रलयं याति देहभृत् ।
iast: yadā sattve pravṛddhe tu pralayaṁ yāti dehabhṛt · tadottamavidāṁ lokānamalānpratipadyate
meaning: When the embodied one meets death while goodness prevails, he reaches the pure worlds of those who know the highest.
lifeNote: The state you cultivate in life shapes your end.
words: of the knowers of the highest
actions: Cultivate calm and clarity daily.
Spend time with good, wise people.
End each day in a peaceful state.

iast: rajasi pralayaṁ gatvā karmasaṅgiṣu jāyate · tathā pralīnastamasi mūḍhayoniṣu jāyate
meaning: Dying in passion, one is born among those attached to action. Dying in inertia, one is born in deluded wombs.
lifeNote: Your habits now become your nature later. Choose them with care.
actions: Drop one restless habit this week.
Replace one lazy habit with a small good one.
Reflect on what you're becoming.

iast: karmaṇaḥ sukṛtasyāhuḥ sāttvikaṁ nirmalaṁ phalam · rajasastu phalaṁ duḥkhamajñānaṁ tamasaḥ phalam
meaning: The fruit of good action is said to be pure and full of goodness. The fruit of passion is pain, and the fruit of inertia is ignorance.
lifeNote: Look at the results: calm actions bring peace, frantic ones bring pain.
actions: Look at the results of how you worked last week.
Choose calm effort over frantic effort.
Notice pain that came from rushing.

sanskrit: सत्त्वात्सञ्जायते ज्ञानं रजसो लोभ एव च ।
iast: sattvātsañjāyate jñānaṁ rajaso lobha eva ca · pramādamohau tamaso bhavato'jñānameva ca
meaning: From goodness arises knowledge, from passion greed, and from inertia come carelessness, delusion and ignorance.
lifeNote: What you feed grows: calm feeds wisdom, greed feeds more greed.
actions: Study in a calm state to learn better.
Notice greed and pause.
Avoid deciding when foggy.

sanskrit: ऊर्ध्वं गच्छन्ति सत्त्वस्था मध्ये तिष्ठन्ति राजसाः ।
iast: ūrdhvaṁ gacchanti sattvasthā madhye tiṣṭhanti rājasāḥ · jaghanyaguṇavṛttisthā adho gacchanti tāmasāḥ
meaning: Those in goodness rise upward, those in passion stay in the middle, and those in the lowest quality, inertia, go downward.
lifeNote: Your inner state is a direction, not a fixed place. You can rise.
actions: Take one step 'upward' today: kinder, clearer, calmer.
Lift yourself out of a slump with a walk.
Encourage a friend who feels stuck.

iast: nānyaṁ guṇebhyaḥ kartāraṁ yadā draṣṭānupaśyati · guṇebhyaśca paraṁ vetti madbhāvaṁ so'dhigacchati
meaning: When the seer sees no doer other than the qualities, and knows what is beyond them, he attains my nature.
lifeNote: Seeing that moods do the acting lets you step back and be free.
actions: Watch a mood act without joining in.
Say 'that's just restlessness' when it rises.
Rest in what is beyond moods for a minute.

iast: guṇānetānatītya trīndehī dehasamudbhavān · janmamṛtyujarāduḥkhairvimukto'mṛtamaśnute
meaning: Going beyond these three qualities that arise from the body, the embodied self is freed from birth, death, old age and pain, and attains immortality.
lifeNote: Beyond moods lies a freedom that ageing and loss can't touch.
words: from birth, death, old age and pain
actions: Reflect on what in you doesn't age.
Comfort an elder with this idea.
Practise watching moods without being them.

iast: kairliṁgaistrīnguṇānetānatīto bhavati prabho · kimācāraḥ kathaṁ caitāṁstrīnguṇānativartate
meaning: Arjuna said: Lord, by what signs is one who has gone beyond the three qualities known? How does he behave, and how does he go beyond them?
lifeNote: Arjuna asks for practical signs. Good question to ask about any ideal.
actions: Ask 'what would this look like in daily life?'
Write three signs of a calm person.
Observe someone you admire for one day.

sanskrit: प्रकाशं च प्रवृत्तिं च मोहमेव च पाण्डव ।
न द्वेष्टि सम्प्रवृत्तानि न निवृत्तानि काङ्क्षति ॥
iast: prakāśaṁ ca pravṛttiṁ ca mohameva ca pāṇḍava · na dveṣṭi sampravṛttāni na nivṛttāni kāṅkṣati
meaning: Krishna said: One who does not hate light, activity or delusion when they arise, nor long for them when they cease, Arjuna...
lifeNote: Don't fight moods or chase them. Let them come and go.
actions: Let a low mood be without fighting it.
Don't chase a high mood when it fades.
Practise 'this too will pass' today.

iast: udāsīnavadāsīno guṇairyo na vicālyate · guṇā vartanta ityeva yo'vatiṣṭhati neṅgate
meaning: ...who sits as if indifferent, not disturbed by the qualities, knowing 'it is only the qualities at work', and stays firm without wavering...
lifeNote: Sit like a calm witness while moods move. You don't have to waver.
actions: When upset, say 'the qualities are acting'.
Sit still for five minutes, unmoved by thoughts.
Stay steady in one chaotic situation.

iast: samaduḥkhasukhaḥ svasthaḥ samaloṣṭāśmakāñcanaḥ · tulyapriyāpriyo dhīrastulyanindātmasaṁstutiḥ
meaning: ...who is the same in pain and pleasure, rests in the self, sees a clod, a stone and gold as equal, is the same towards the pleasant and unpleasant, steady, and the same in blame and praise...
lifeNote: Steadiness is freedom. Praise and blame lose their grip.
words: same to clod, stone and gold
actions: Respond to praise and blame the same way today.
Value a friend over a gift.
Rest in yourself when others judge you.

iast: mānāpamānayostulyastulyo mitrāripakṣayoḥ · sarvārambhaparityāgī guṇātītaḥ sa ucyate
meaning: ...the same in honour and dishonour, the same to friend and foe, giving up all selfish undertakings: such a person is said to have gone beyond the qualities.
lifeNote: Treating friend and foe alike is the mark of a free person.
actions: Be fair to someone who wronged you.
Accept an insult without retaliating.
Start a task for others, not for yourself.

iast: māṁ ca yo'vyabhicāreṇa bhaktiyogena sevate · sa guṇānsamatītyaitān brahmabhūyāya kalpate
meaning: One who serves me with unwavering devotion goes beyond these qualities and becomes fit to become one with Brahman.
lifeNote: Steady love lifts you beyond your moods.
actions: Keep a short devotional practice every day.
Serve someone as an act of devotion.
Let love guide you through a bad mood.

iast: brahmaṇo hi pratiṣṭhā'hamamṛtasyāvyayasya ca · śāśvatasya ca dharmasya sukhasyaikāntikasya ca
meaning: For I am the foundation of Brahman, of the immortal and imperishable, of eternal dharma and of absolute happiness.
lifeNote: Lasting happiness rests on something eternal. Build on that foundation.
actions: Ask what your happiness is built on.
Spend time on what lasts.
End this chapter with a prayer of thanks.

sanskrit: छन्दांसि यस्य पर्णानि यस्तं वेद स वेदवित् ॥
iast: ūrdhvamūlamadhaḥśākhamaśvatthaṁ prāhuravyayam · chandāṁsi yasya parṇāni yastaṁ veda sa vedavit
meaning: Krishna said: They speak of an imperishable ashvattha tree with its roots above and branches below, whose leaves are the Vedic hymns. One who knows it knows the Vedas.
lifeNote: Life is like an upside-down tree: its roots are in the divine. Look up to find your source.
actions: Draw the upside-down tree and label your 'roots'.
Reflect on where your life draws its strength.
Sit under a peepal tree if you can.

iast: adhaścordhvaṁ prasṛtāstasya śākhā · guṇapravṛddhā viṣayapravālāḥ · adhaśca mūlānyanusantatāni · karmānubandhīni manuṣyaloke
meaning: Its branches spread below and above, nourished by the qualities, with sense objects as buds. Its roots extend downward too, binding people to action in the human world.
lifeNote: Desires sprout like buds and tie us down. Notice the new buds before they grow.
actions: Notice one new desire 'budding' today.
Cut back one habit that keeps branching out.
Reflect on what ties you to restless action.

iast: na rūpamasyeha tathopalabhyate · nānto na cādirna ca saṁpratiṣṭhā · aśvatthamenaṁ suvirūḍhamūlam · asaṅgaśastreṇa dṛḍhena chittvā
meaning: Its real form is not seen here, nor its end, beginning or foundation. Cutting down this firmly rooted ashvattha with the strong axe of detachment...
lifeNote: Detachment is an axe: it cuts the roots of endless craving.
actions: Cut one unhealthy attachment cleanly this week.
Unfollow or mute one source of craving.
Practise saying 'I don't need this'.

iast: tataḥ padaṁ tatparimārgitavyaṁ · yasmingatā na nivartanti bhūyaḥ · tameva cādyaṁ puruṣaṁ prapadye · yataḥ pravṛttiḥ prasṛtā purāṇī
meaning: ...one should seek that goal from which, once reached, there is no return, saying: 'I take refuge in that primal person from whom this ancient flow of activity came forth.'
lifeNote: After cutting ties, turn towards the source and take refuge there.
actions: Say 'I take refuge' in a quiet moment.
Turn to prayer after letting something go.
Seek the goal that doesn't fade.

iast: nirmānamohā jitasaṅgadoṣā · adhyātmanityā vinivṛttakāmāḥ · dvandvairvimuktāḥ sukhaduḥkhasaṁjñaiḥ · gacchantyamūḍhāḥ padamavyayaṁ tat
meaning: Free from pride and delusion, having overcome attachment, always dwelling in the self, with desires stilled and freed from the opposites called pleasure and pain, the undeluded reach that imperishable goal.
lifeNote: Drop pride, calm desire, and the way becomes clear.
actions: Let go of pride in one conversation.
Spend ten minutes in self-reflection.
Stay even through one pleasant and one unpleasant event.

sanskrit: न तद्भासयते सूर्यो न शशाङ्को न पावकः ।
यद्गत्वा न निवर्तन्ते तद्धाम परमं मम ॥
iast: na tadbhāsayate sūryo na śaśāṅko na pāvakaḥ · yadgatvā na nivartante taddhāma paramaṁ mama
meaning: Neither the sun nor the moon nor fire lights that place. Those who reach it do not return; that is my supreme abode.
lifeNote: There is a light that needs no sun. It shines within.
actions: Close your eyes and look for inner light.
Remember a loved one as resting in that light.
Light a lamp and think of the light beyond it.

iast: mamaivāṁśo jīvaloke jīvabhūtaḥ sanātanaḥ · manaḥṣaṣṭhānīndriyāṇi prakṛtisthāni karṣati
meaning: An eternal part of me becomes the living soul in the world of beings. It draws to itself the five senses and the mind, the sixth, which rest in nature.
lifeNote: You are a part of the divine, eternal and precious.
actions: Remind yourself: I am an eternal part of the divine.
Treat others as eternal souls too.
Use your senses today with respect.

iast: śarīraṁ yadavāpnoti yaccāpyutkrāmatīśvaraḥ · gṛhītvaitāni saṁyāti vāyurgandhānivāśayāt
meaning: When the soul takes on a body and when it leaves one, it carries these along, as the wind carries scents from their source.
lifeNote: Like wind carrying fragrance, you carry your tendencies forward. Make them sweet.
actions: Cultivate one 'fragrant' habit you'd like to carry.
Reflect on what you'll leave behind.
Notice the wind carrying scents today.

sanskrit: श्रोत्रं चक्षुः स्पर्शनं च रसनं घ्राणमेव च ।
iast: śrotraṁ cakṣuḥ sparśanaṁ ca rasanaṁ ghrāṇameva ca · adhiṣṭhāya manaścāyaṁ viṣayānupasevate
meaning: Presiding over the ear, eye, touch, taste and smell, and over the mind, the soul enjoys the objects of the senses.
lifeNote: Your senses are instruments of the soul. Use them for good.
actions: Listen to something uplifting today.
Look at something beautiful on purpose.
Eat one meal slowly and taste it fully.

sanskrit: उत्क्रामन्तं स्थितं वापि भुञ्जानं वा गुणान्वितम् ।
iast: utkrāmantaṁ sthitaṁ vāpi bhuñjānaṁ vā guṇānvitam · vimūḍhā nānupaśyanti paśyanti jñānacakṣuṣaḥ
meaning: The deluded do not see the soul as it departs, stays or enjoys with the qualities. Those with the eye of knowledge see it.
lifeNote: Look past the body to the soul in people.
words: those with the eye of knowledge
actions: See the person, not just the body, in someone ill.
Look at a loved one and sense their soul.
Practise seeing with 'the eye of knowledge'.

iast: yatanto yoginaścainaṁ paśyantyātmanyavasthitam · yatanto'pyakṛtātmāno nainaṁ paśyantyacetasaḥ
meaning: Striving yogis see the soul established within themselves. But the impure and thoughtless do not see it, even when they strive.
lifeNote: Effort alone isn't enough; it must be joined with purity of heart.
actions: Clean up one motive before a big effort.
Strive with sincerity, not show.
Spend time in self-examination tonight.

iast: yadādityagataṁ tejo jagadbhāsayate'khilam · yaccandramasi yaccāgnau tattejo viddhi māmakam
meaning: The light in the sun that lights up the whole world, the light in the moon and in fire: know that light to be mine.
lifeNote: Every light you see reflects the divine light.
actions: Greet the sun with this verse.
Light a lamp at dusk with thanks.
Notice moonlight tonight.

sanskrit: पुष्णामि चौषधीः सर्वाः सोमो भूत्वा रसात्मकः ॥
iast: gāmāviśya ca bhūtāni dhārayāmyahamojasā · puṣṇāmi cauṣadhīḥ sarvāḥ somo bhūtvā rasātmakaḥ
meaning: Entering the earth, I sustain all beings with my energy. Becoming the moon, full of sap, I nourish all plants.
lifeNote: The earth holds you; the plants feed you. All is divine care.
actions: Thank the earth before a meal.
Water a plant and remember this verse.
Walk barefoot on grass for a minute.

iast: ahaṁ vaiśvānaro bhūtvā prāṇināṁ dehamāśritaḥ · prāṇāpānasamāyuktaḥ pacāmyannaṁ caturvidham
meaning: Becoming the digestive fire in the bodies of living beings and joined with the breaths, I digest the four kinds of food.
lifeNote: Even digestion is a divine process. Many recite this verse before eating.
actions: Recite this verse before a meal.
Eat at a calm pace today.
Thank your body for its quiet work.

iast: sarvasya cāhaṁ hṛdi sanniviṣṭo · mattaḥ smṛtirjñānamapohanaṁ ca · vedaiśca sarvairahameva vedyo · vedāntakṛdvedavideva cāham
meaning: I am seated in the heart of all. From me come memory, knowledge and their loss. I am what is to be known through all the Vedas; I am the author of Vedanta and the knower of the Vedas.
lifeNote: Memory and understanding are gifts from within. Ask the heart for help when studying.
actions: Pray for memory and clarity before an exam.
Place a hand on your heart when you forget something.
Revise with a calm heart.

sanskrit: द्वाविमौ पुरुषौ लोके क्षरश्चाक्षर एव च ।
iast: dvāvimau puruṣau loke kṣaraścākṣara eva ca · kṣaraḥ sarvāṇi bhūtāni kūṭastho'kṣara ucyate
meaning: There are two persons in this world: the perishable and the imperishable. All beings are the perishable; the unchanging is called the imperishable.
lifeNote: Something in you changes, and something does not. Know both.
actions: List what in your life changes and what doesn't.
Accept a change in your body calmly.
Rest in the unchanging for a minute.

iast: uttamaḥ puruṣastvanyaḥ paramātmetyudāhṛtaḥ · yo lokatrayamāviśya bibhartyavyaya īśvaraḥ
meaning: But there is another, the highest person, called the supreme self, the imperishable lord who enters the three worlds and sustains them.
lifeNote: Beyond change and changelessness is the one who holds both.
actions: Pray to the one who sustains all.
Feel held when you feel alone.
Read this verse slowly before sleep.

sanskrit: अतोऽस्मि लोके वेदे च प्रथितः पुरुषोत्तमः ॥
iast: yasmātkṣaramatīto'hamakṣarādapi cottamaḥ · ato'smi loke vede ca prathitaḥ puruṣottamaḥ
meaning: Since I am beyond the perishable and higher even than the imperishable, I am celebrated in the world and in the Veda as the supreme person.
lifeNote: Krishna is called Purushottama, the highest person. That's where the chapter's name comes from.
actions: Learn the meaning of 'Purushottama'.
Chant one of Krishna's names today.
Teach a child this name and its meaning.

iast: yo māmevamasammūḍho jānāti puruṣottamam · sa sarvavidbhajati māṁ sarvabhāvena bhārata
meaning: One who, free from delusion, knows me as the supreme person knows everything, and worships me with all his being, Arjuna.
lifeNote: True knowing turns into wholehearted love.
actions: Worship today with your whole heart.
Let study deepen your devotion.
Pray with full attention for five minutes.

iast: iti guhyatamaṁ śāstramidamuktaṁ mayā'nagha · etadbuddhvā buddhimānsyātkṛtakṛtyaśca bhārata
meaning: Thus I have told you this most secret teaching, sinless Arjuna. Understanding it, one becomes wise and has done all that needs to be done.
lifeNote: Understanding this chapter fully is said to complete your life's work. Read it often.
actions: Recite chapter 15 before meals this week.
Write the chapter's key idea in one line.
Share chapter 15 with your family.

iast: abhayaṁ sattvasaṁśuddhiḥ jñānayogavyavasthitiḥ · dānaṁ damaśca yajñaśca svādhyāyastapa ārjavam
meaning: Krishna said: Fearlessness, purity of heart, steadiness in knowledge and yoga, charity, self-control, sacrifice, study of scripture, discipline and straightforwardness...
lifeNote: This chapter lists divine qualities. Pick one and practise it.
actions: Do one thing today that requires a little courage.
Read a page of scripture.
Be straightforward in one conversation.

iast: ahiṁsā satyamakrodhastyāgaḥ śāntirapaiśunam · dayā bhūteṣvaloluptvaṁ mārdavaṁ hrīracāpalam
meaning: ...non-violence, truthfulness, freedom from anger, renunciation, peace, not slandering, compassion for all beings, freedom from greed, gentleness, modesty and steadiness...
lifeNote: Gentleness and truth together make a strong, kind person.
actions: Avoid gossip for a whole day.
Speak gently even when correcting someone.
Show compassion to an animal or person in need.

iast: tejaḥ kṣamā dhṛtiḥ śaucamadroho nātimānitā · bhavanti sampadaṁ daivīmabhijātasya bhārata
meaning: ...vigour, forgiveness, fortitude, purity, freedom from malice and from excessive pride: these are the wealth of one born to the divine nature, Arjuna.
lifeNote: Forgiveness and fortitude are true riches. Count them as your wealth.
actions: Forgive one person today, even silently.
Keep going through one hard task with fortitude.
Drop one prideful habit.

iast: dambho darpo'bhimānaśca krodhaḥ pāruṣyameva ca · ajñānaṁ cābhijātasya pārtha sampadamāsurīm
meaning: Hypocrisy, arrogance, conceit, anger, harshness and ignorance belong to one born to the demonic nature, Arjuna.
lifeNote: Arrogance and harshness are warning signs. Catch them in yourself first.
actions: Notice one moment of arrogance and correct it.
Soften one harsh word today.
Admit a mistake instead of defending it.

iast: daivī sampadvimokṣāya nibandhāyāsurī matā · mā śucaḥ sampadaṁ daivīmabhijāto'si pāṇḍava
meaning: The divine nature leads to liberation, the demonic to bondage. Do not grieve, Arjuna: you are born with the divine nature.
lifeNote: Krishna reassures Arjuna: you are good at heart. Believe it about yourself too.
actions: Remind yourself of your good qualities today.
Encourage someone who doubts their goodness.
Stop one self-critical loop.

sanskrit: द्वौ भूतसर्गौ लोकेऽस्मिन् दैव आसुर एव च ।
दैवो विस्तरशः प्रोक्त आसुरं पार्थ मे शृणु ॥
iast: dvau bhūtasargau loke'smin daiva āsura eva ca · daivo vistaraśaḥ prokta āsuraṁ pārtha me śṛṇu
meaning: There are two kinds of beings in this world: the divine and the demonic. The divine has been described in detail; now hear from me about the demonic, Arjuna.
lifeNote: Knowing what to avoid is as useful as knowing what to aim for.
actions: List three traits you want to avoid.
Notice one 'demonic' trait in media you consume.
Choose company that brings out your best.

sanskrit: प्रवृत्तिं च निवृत्तिं च जना न विदुरासुराः ।
न शौचं नापि चाचारो न सत्यं तेषु विद्यते ॥
iast: pravṛttiṁ ca nivṛttiṁ ca janā na vidurāsurāḥ · na śaucaṁ nāpi cācāro na satyaṁ teṣu vidyate
meaning: People of demonic nature do not know what to do and what to avoid. Neither purity, nor good conduct, nor truth is found in them.
lifeNote: Knowing when to act and when to stop is the beginning of character.
actions: Decide one thing to start and one to stop.
Keep one rule of good conduct today.
Tell the truth in a small matter.

iast: asatyamapratiṣṭhaṁ te jagadāhuranīśvaram · aparasparasambhūtaṁ kimanyatkāmahaitukam
meaning: They say the world is unreal, without foundation and without God, not born of any order. 'What else is it but desire?' they say.
lifeNote: A worldview that sees nothing beyond desire leads to emptiness.
actions: Reflect on what you believe the world is for.
Notice when you treat life as only about wants.
Read about a meaningful worldview.

iast: etāṁ dṛṣṭimavaṣṭabhya naṣṭātmāno'lpabuddhayaḥ · prabhavantyugrakarmāṇaḥ kṣayāya jagato'hitāḥ
meaning: Holding this view, these lost souls of little understanding rise up as enemies of the world, doing cruel deeds for its destruction.
lifeNote: Bad ideas lead to harmful actions. Guard what you believe.
actions: Question one cynical belief you hold.
Avoid content that glorifies cruelty.
Support something that heals the world.

iast: kāmamāśritya duṣpūraṁ dambhamānamadānvitāḥ · mohādgṛhītvāsadgrāhānpravartante'śucivratāḥ
meaning: Clinging to insatiable desire, full of hypocrisy, pride and arrogance, holding false ideas out of delusion, they act with impure resolves.
lifeNote: Insatiable desire is a bottomless pit. Notice when you're digging.
words: full of hypocrisy, pride and arrogance
actions: Notice one desire that's never satisfied.
Practise 'enough' in one area today.
Drop one hypocritical habit.

iast: cintāmaparimeyāṁ ca pralayāntāmupāśritāḥ · kāmopabhogaparamā etāvaditi niścitāḥ
meaning: Gripped by endless anxieties that end only with death, taking enjoyment of desires as the highest goal, they are convinced that this is all there is.
lifeNote: A life only for pleasure is full of anxiety. There is more.
words: with enjoyment as the highest goal
actions: Notice anxiety tied to wanting more.
Find one purpose beyond enjoyment.
Help someone today without benefit to you.

iast: āśāpāśaśatairbaddhāḥ kāmakrodhaparāyaṇāḥ · īhante kāmabhogārthamanyāyenārthasañcayān
meaning: Bound by hundreds of ropes of expectation, given over to desire and anger, they strive to pile up wealth by unjust means for their enjoyment.
lifeNote: Expectations can become ropes. Loosen a few.
words: by hundreds of ropes of hope
actions: Let go of one expectation about another person.
Earn honestly even if it's slower.
Notice anger tied to unmet desires.

iast: idamadya mayā labdhamimaṁ prāpsye manoratham · idamastīdamapi me bhaviṣyati punardhanam
meaning: 'This I have gained today; this desire I will fulfil next. This wealth is mine, and more will be mine too.'
lifeNote: The 'more, more' mindset never rests. Celebrate what is enough.
actions: Write down what is 'enough' for you.
Celebrate a gain without immediately wanting more.
Give away a portion of something you gained.

iast: asau mayā hataḥ śatrurhaniṣye cāparānapi · īśvaro'hamahaṁ bhogī siddho'haṁ balavānsukhī
meaning: 'That enemy has been slain by me, and I will slay others too. I am the lord, I am the enjoyer, I am successful, powerful and happy.'
lifeNote: Ego loves to say 'I, I, I'. Notice how often you do.
actions: Count how many times you say 'I' in a conversation.
Give credit to others for one success.
Let go of a rivalry.

iast: āḍhyo'bhijanavānasmi ko'nyo'sti sadṛśo mayā · yakṣye dāsyāmi modiṣya ityajñānavimohitāḥ
meaning: 'I am wealthy and well-born. Who else is equal to me? I will perform rituals, give charity and enjoy myself.' So they speak, deluded by ignorance.
lifeNote: Even charity can feed ego. Give quietly.
actions: Give something today without telling anyone.
Avoid comparing yourself to others for a day.
Notice pride in your background and soften it.

iast: anekacittavibhrāntā mohajālasamāvṛtāḥ · prasaktāḥ kāmabhogeṣu patanti narake'śucau
meaning: Bewildered by many thoughts, caught in a net of delusion and attached to sensual pleasures, they fall into a foul hell.
lifeNote: A scattered mind caught in pleasure ends up in suffering.
words: caught in a net of delusion
actions: Simplify your thoughts with a five-minute pause.
Notice a net of habits you're caught in.
Choose one pleasure to give up this week.

iast: ātmasambhāvitāḥ stabdhā dhanamānamadānvitāḥ · yajante nāmayajñaiste dambhenāvidhipūrvakam
meaning: Self-important, stubborn and intoxicated by wealth and pride, they perform sacrifices in name only, with hypocrisy and against the proper rules.
lifeNote: Worship for show is empty. Do it sincerely or not at all.
actions: Do one religious act sincerely, not for show.
Avoid posting about good deeds today.
Check your motive before a public ritual.

sanskrit: अहङ्कारं बलं दर्पं कामं क्रोधं च संश्रिताः ।
iast: ahaṅkāraṁ balaṁ darpaṁ kāmaṁ krodhaṁ ca saṁśritāḥ · māmātmaparadeheṣu pradviṣanto'bhyasūyakāḥ
meaning: Relying on ego, power, arrogance, desire and anger, these envious people hate me, who dwell in their own bodies and in others'.
lifeNote: Hating others is hating the divine in them, and in yourself.
words: in their own and others' bodies
actions: Notice envy and turn it into admiration.
Remember the divine in someone you resent.
Let go of one grudge this week.

iast: tānahaṁ dviṣataḥ krūrānsaṁsāreṣu narādhamān · kṣipāmyajasramaśubhānāsurīṣveva yoniṣu
meaning: These hateful, cruel, wicked people, the lowest of humans, I repeatedly cast into demonic wombs in the cycles of birth.
lifeNote: Cruelty breeds more cruelty. Break the cycle with kindness.
actions: Respond to cruelty without cruelty today.
Protect someone being bullied.
Notice cycles of harshness in your family and break one.

iast: asurīṁ yonimāpannā mūḍhā janmani janmani · māmaprāpyaiva kaunteya tato yāntyadhamāṁ gatim
meaning: Entering demonic wombs birth after birth, these deluded people never reach me, Arjuna, and sink to the lowest state.
lifeNote: Habits compound across time. It's never too early to change direction.
actions: Change one small habit today.
Reflect on where your habits will lead in ten years.
Ask for help changing a bad pattern.

iast: trividhaṁ narakasyedaṁ dvāraṁ nāśanamātmanaḥ · kāmaḥ krodhastathā lobhastasmādetattrayaṁ tyajet
meaning: There are three gates to hell that destroy the self: desire, anger and greed. So one should give up these three.
lifeNote: Lust, anger and greed: three doors to avoid. Watch them daily.
actions: Notice desire, anger and greed once each today.
Close one 'gate' this week with a firm rule.
Memorise this verse.

iast: etairvimuktaḥ kaunteya tamodvāraistribhirnaraḥ · ācaratyātmanaḥ śreyastato yāti parāṁ gatim
meaning: A person freed from these three gates of darkness, Arjuna, does what is good for the self and then reaches the supreme goal.
lifeNote: Free from desire, anger and greed, you naturally do what's good.
actions: After calming anger, do something kind.
Use freed-up energy for a good cause.
Celebrate a day without losing your temper.

sanskrit: न स सिद्धिमवाप्नोति न सुखं न परां गतिम् ॥
iast: yaḥ śāstravidhimutsṛjya vartate kāmakārataḥ · na sa siddhimavāpnoti na sukhaṁ na parāṁ gatim
meaning: One who discards the guidance of scripture and acts on the impulse of desire attains neither perfection, nor happiness, nor the supreme goal.
lifeNote: Acting on impulse alone rarely leads to happiness. Wise guidance helps.
actions: Check one impulse against wise guidance.
Read a teaching before a big choice.
Wait a day before acting on a strong urge.

iast: tasmācchāstraṁ pramāṇaṁ te kāryākāryavyavasthitau · jñātvā śāstravidhānoktaṁ karma kartumihārhasi
meaning: So let scripture be your guide in deciding what to do and what not to do. Knowing what it teaches, you should act here accordingly.
lifeNote: When unsure, lean on time-tested wisdom.
words: in deciding what to do and not do
actions: Look up what the Gita says about a current choice.
Ask an elder for guidance on a decision.
Write a rule from scripture you want to follow.

sanskrit: तेषां निष्ठा तु का कृष्ण सत्त्वमाहो रजस्तमः ॥
iast: ye śāstravidhimutsṛjya yajante śraddhayā'nvitāḥ · teṣāṁ niṣṭhā tu kā kṛṣṇa sattvamāho rajastamaḥ
meaning: Arjuna said: Krishna, what is the standing of those who set aside scriptural rules but worship with faith? Is it goodness, passion or inertia?
lifeNote: Faith without rules: is it enough? A fair question for many today.
actions: Reflect on whether your faith has structure.
Ask what your faith is really based on.
Respect sincere faith in others.

sanskrit: त्रिविधा भवति श्रद्धा देहिनां सा स्वभावजा ।
सात्त्विकी राजसी चैव तामसी चेति तां शृणु ॥
iast: trividhā bhavati śraddhā dehināṁ sā svabhāvajā · sāttvikī rājasī caiva tāmasī ceti tāṁ śṛṇu
meaning: Krishna said: The faith of embodied beings, born of their nature, is of three kinds: of goodness, of passion and of inertia. Hear about it.
lifeNote: Faith takes the colour of your nature. Clean the nature and faith grows clear.
actions: Notice the 'colour' of your faith today.
Do one thing to make your faith calmer.
Learn the three kinds of faith with a friend.

sanskrit: श्रद्धामयोऽयं पुरुषो यो यच्छ्रद्धः स एव सः ॥
iast: sattvānurūpā sarvasya śraddhā bhavati bhārata · śraddhāmayo'yaṁ puruṣo yo yacchraddhaḥ sa eva saḥ
meaning: Everyone's faith follows their nature, Arjuna. A person is made of faith: whatever one's faith is, that is what one is.
lifeNote: You are what you believe in. Choose your faith wisely.
actions: Write down what you truly believe in.
Check whether your actions match your faith.
Feed your faith with good company.

iast: yajante sāttvikā devānyakṣarakṣāṁsi rājasāḥ · pretānbhūtagaṇāṁścānye yajante tāmasā janāḥ
meaning: Those of goodness worship the gods; those of passion worship yakshas and rakshasas; and others, of inertia, worship ghosts and spirits.
lifeNote: What you worship shows your inner state.
actions: Notice what you spend most time 'worshipping'.
Shift one hour from idols of money to something higher.
Choose uplifting role models.

sanskrit: अशास्त्रविहितं घोरं तप्यन्ते ये तपो जनाः ।
iast: aśāstravihitaṁ ghoraṁ tapyante ye tapo janāḥ · dambhāhaṅkārasaṁyuktāḥ kāmarāgabalānvitāḥ
meaning: People who practise severe austerities not prescribed by scripture, with hypocrisy and ego, driven by desire, attachment and force...
lifeNote: Extreme self-punishment isn't spirituality. Be kind to your body.
words: driven by desire, attachment and force
actions: Avoid extreme fasting or punishing routines.
Choose gentle discipline over harsh.
Notice ego behind 'tough' practices.

iast: karṣayantaḥ śarīrasthaṁ bhūtagrāmamacetasaḥ · māṁ caivāntaḥśarīrasthaṁ tānviddhyāsuraniścayān
meaning: ...senselessly tormenting the elements of the body and me who dwell within it: know them to be of demonic resolve.
lifeNote: Harming your body harms the divine within. Care for it.
actions: Do one thing today to care for your body.
Rest when tired instead of pushing through.
Treat your body as a temple.

iast: āhārastvapi sarvasya trividho bhavati priyaḥ · yajñastapastathā dānaṁ teṣāṁ bhedamimaṁ śṛṇu
meaning: Even the food dear to each person is of three kinds, and so are sacrifice, austerity and charity. Hear how they differ.
lifeNote: Even your diet reflects your inner state.
actions: Notice which foods you crave when stressed.
Choose one fresh meal today.
Observe how food affects your mood.

sanskrit: रस्याः स्निग्धाः स्थिरा हृद्या आहाराः सात्त्विकप्रियाः ॥
iast: āyuḥsattvabalārogyasukhaprītivivardhanāḥ · rasyāḥ snigdhāḥ sthirā hṛdyā āhārāḥ sāttvikapriyāḥ
meaning: Foods that increase life, purity, strength, health, happiness and cheer, that are juicy, nourishing, sustaining and pleasing to the heart, are dear to those of goodness.
lifeNote: Fresh, wholesome food lifts body and mind.
words: increasing life, purity, strength, health, joy and cheer
actions: Eat fresh fruit or vegetables today.
Drink enough water before studying.
Cook a simple, wholesome meal.

iast: kaṭvamlalavaṇātyuṣṇatīkṣṇarūkṣavidāhinaḥ · āhārā rājasasyeṣṭā duḥkhaśokāmayapradāḥ
meaning: Foods that are bitter, sour, salty, very hot, pungent, dry and burning are liked by the passionate. They cause pain, grief and disease.
lifeNote: Too spicy, too salty, too much: these stir restlessness.
words: bitter, sour, salty, very hot, pungent, dry and burning
actions: Cut back on very spicy or salty food this week.
Notice how heavy spice affects sleep.
Balance a spicy meal with something cooling.

sanskrit: यातयामं गतरसं पूति पर्युषितं च यत् ।
iast: yātayāmaṁ gatarasaṁ pūti paryuṣitaṁ ca yat · ucchiṣṭamapi cāmedhyaṁ bhojanaṁ tāmasapriyam
meaning: Food that is stale, tasteless, putrid, left overnight, leftover and impure is dear to those of inertia.
lifeNote: Stale, processed food dulls the mind.
actions: Avoid stale or junk food before studying.
Eat freshly cooked food today.
Clear old food from your fridge.

iast: aphalākāṅkṣibhiryajño vidhidṛṣṭo ya ijyate · yaṣṭavyameveti manaḥ samādhāya sa sāttvikaḥ
meaning: Sacrifice performed as prescribed by those who seek no reward, with the mind resolved that 'it should simply be done', is of goodness.
lifeNote: Do good because it's right, not for the reward.
actions: Do one duty today simply because it should be done.
Skip the reward check after a good deed.
Offer your work without expecting thanks.

sanskrit: अभिसंधाय तु फलं दम्भार्थमपि चैव यत् ।
इज्यते भरतश्रेष्ठ तं यज्ञं विद्धि राजसम् ॥
iast: abhisaṁdhāya tu phalaṁ dambhārthamapi caiva yat · ijyate bharataśreṣṭha taṁ yajñaṁ viddhi rājasam
meaning: But sacrifice performed for a reward or for show, Arjuna, know that to be of passion.
lifeNote: Good deeds for show lose their goodness.
actions: Do one good deed without telling anyone.
Check your motive before a public act.
Avoid posting your charity online.

iast: vidhihīnamasṛṣṭānnaṁ mantrahīnamadakṣiṇam · śraddhāvirahitaṁ yajñaṁ tāmasaṁ paricakṣate
meaning: Sacrifice without rules, without sharing food, without mantras, without gifts to the priests and without faith is called of inertia.
lifeNote: Careless, faithless rituals are empty. Bring sincerity or skip it.
actions: Share food after a ritual or festival.
Bring faith and attention to one ritual.
Thank those who serve at your place of worship.

iast: devadvijaguruprājñapūjanaṁ śaucamārjavam · brahmacaryamahiṁsā ca śārīraṁ tapa ucyate
meaning: Honouring the gods, the twice-born, teachers and the wise; cleanliness, straightforwardness, self-restraint and non-violence: this is called austerity of the body.
lifeNote: Discipline of the body: respect, cleanliness, restraint, gentleness.
words: honouring gods, the twice-born, teachers and the wise
actions: Touch the feet of or bow to a teacher or elder.
Keep your body and room clean today.
Avoid hurting any living thing today.

sanskrit: अनुद्वेगकरं वाक्यं सत्यं प्रियहितं च यत् ।
iast: anudvegakaraṁ vākyaṁ satyaṁ priyahitaṁ ca yat · svādhyāyābhyasanaṁ caiva vāṅmayaṁ tapa ucyate
meaning: Speech that causes no distress, that is truthful, pleasant and beneficial, and the regular recitation of scripture: this is called austerity of speech.
lifeNote: Speak truth that is kind and helpful. That is discipline of the tongue.
actions: Before speaking, ask: true, kind, helpful?
Recite one verse aloud daily.
Avoid one hurtful remark today.

iast: manaḥprasādaḥ saumyatvaṁ maunamātmavinigrahaḥ · bhāvasaṁśuddhirityetattapo mānasamucyate
meaning: Serenity of mind, gentleness, silence, self-control and purity of intention: this is called austerity of the mind.
lifeNote: A calm, gentle, honest mind is the deepest discipline.
actions: Spend ten minutes in silence today.
Check your intention before acting.
Respond gently to a stressful message.

iast: śraddhayā parayā taptaṁ tapastattrividhaṁ naraiḥ · aphalākāṅkṣibhiryuktaiḥ sāttvikaṁ paricakṣate
meaning: This threefold austerity, practised with supreme faith by steadfast people who seek no reward, is called of goodness.
lifeNote: Discipline of body, speech and mind, done without wanting reward, is pure.
actions: Keep one discipline of body, speech and mind today.
Do it for its own sake.
Track your three disciplines for a week.

iast: satkāramānapūjārthaṁ tapo dambhena caiva yat · kriyate tadiha proktaṁ rājasaṁ calamadhruvam
meaning: Austerity done with hypocrisy to gain respect, honour and reverence is said here to be of passion: unstable and impermanent.
lifeNote: Discipline for applause doesn't last.
actions: Notice if you practise to impress others.
Keep one practice private.
Find your own reason for discipline.

iast: mūḍhagrāheṇātmano yatpīḍayā kriyate tapaḥ · parasyotsādanārthaṁ vā tattāmasamudāhṛtam
meaning: Austerity done out of foolish notions, by torturing oneself or to harm another, is declared to be of inertia.
lifeNote: Self-harm and harming others are never spiritual.
actions: Drop any routine that hurts you.
Never use 'discipline' to punish others.
Seek help if you feel the urge to self-harm.

sanskrit: देशे काले च पात्रे च तद्दानं सात्त्विकं स्मृतम् ॥
iast: dātavyamiti yaddānaṁ dīyate'nupakāriṇe · deśe kāle ca pātre ca taddānaṁ sāttvikaṁ smṛtam
meaning: A gift given because it ought to be given, to one who cannot repay, at the right place and time and to a worthy person, is held to be of goodness.
lifeNote: Give simply because it's right, to someone who can't pay you back.
actions: Give something to someone who can't return it.
Give at the right time, when it's needed.
Choose a worthy cause for your charity.

sanskrit: दीयते च परिक्लिष्टं तद्दानं राजसं स्मृतम् ॥
iast: yattu pratyupakārārthaṁ phalamuddiśya vā punaḥ · dīyate ca parikliṣṭaṁ taddānaṁ rājasaṁ smṛtam
meaning: But a gift given expecting something in return, or for a reward, or given reluctantly, is held to be of passion.
lifeNote: Giving with strings attached isn't true giving.
actions: Give one gift with no strings attached.
Notice reluctance when giving and give anyway.
Stop keeping score of favours.

iast: adeśakāle yaddānamapātrebhyaśca dīyate · asatkṛtamavajñātaṁ tattāmasamudāhṛtam
meaning: A gift given at the wrong place and time, to unworthy people, without respect or with contempt, is declared to be of inertia.
lifeNote: Give with respect. How you give matters as much as what.
words: at the wrong place and time
actions: Give with a smile and respect today.
Avoid giving in a way that humiliates.
Think before giving to make it useful.

iast: tatsaditi nirdeśo brahmaṇastrividhaḥ smṛtaḥ · brāhmaṇāstena vedāśca yajñāśca vihitāḥ purā
meaning: 'Om Tat Sat' is held to be the threefold name of Brahman. By it the knowers of Brahman, the Vedas and sacrifices were ordained of old.
lifeNote: Om Tat Sat: three words that dedicate any act to the highest.
actions: Say 'Om Tat Sat' before starting work.
Learn the meaning of each word.
End a task by offering it with these words.

iast: tasmādomityudāhṛtya yajñadānatapaḥkriyāḥ · pravartante vidhānoktāḥ satataṁ brahmavādinām
meaning: So the followers of Brahman always begin their prescribed acts of sacrifice, charity and austerity by uttering 'Om'.
lifeNote: Beginning with Om sets the right tone for any good act.
words: acts of sacrifice, charity and austerity
actions: Chant Om before studying or working.
Start your morning with Om.
Teach a child to begin tasks with Om.

iast: tadityanabhisandhāya phalaṁ yajñatapaḥkriyāḥ · dānakriyāśca vividhāḥ kriyante mokṣakāṅkṣibhiḥ
meaning: Uttering 'Tat', seekers of freedom perform various acts of sacrifice, austerity and charity without aiming at any reward.
lifeNote: 'Tat' means 'that': doing it for the highest, not for yourself.
actions: Do one act 'for That', not for you.
Let go of reward before starting.
Offer your charity silently.

sanskrit: प्रशस्ते कर्मणि तथा सच्छब्दः पार्थ युज्यते ॥
iast: sadbhāve sādhubhāve ca sadityetatprayujyate · praśaste karmaṇi tathā sacchabdaḥ pārtha yujyate
meaning: The word 'Sat' is used to mean reality and goodness, Arjuna. It is also used for praiseworthy action.
lifeNote: 'Sat' means truth and goodness. Let your actions be 'sat'.
actions: Do one praiseworthy act today.
Speak only what is true.
Notice goodness around you and name it.

sanskrit: यज्ञे तपसि दाने च स्थितिः सदिति चोच्यते ।
iast: yajñe tapasi dāne ca sthitiḥ saditi cocyate · karma caiva tadarthīyaṁ sadityevābhidhīyate
meaning: Steadfastness in sacrifice, austerity and charity is also called 'Sat', and so is any action done for that purpose.
lifeNote: Steady good practice is itself truth in action.
actions: Stay steady in one good practice this week.
Give regularly, even small amounts.
Keep a daily act of service.

sanskrit: अश्रद्धया हुतं दत्तं तपस्तप्तं कृतं च यत् ।
असदित्युच्यते पार्थ न च तत्प्रेत्य नो इह ॥
iast: aśraddhayā hutaṁ dattaṁ tapastaptaṁ kṛtaṁ ca yat · asadityucyate pārtha na ca tatpretya no iha
meaning: Whatever is offered, given, practised or done without faith is called 'Asat', Arjuna. It is of no value here or hereafter.
lifeNote: Faith gives action its value. Bring heart to what you do.
actions: Bring faith to one routine act today.
Skip a ritual you can't do sincerely, and reflect why.
Pray for deeper faith.

iast: saṁnyāsasya mahābāho tattvamicchāmi veditum · tyāgasya ca hṛṣīkeśa pṛthakkeśiniṣūdana
meaning: Arjuna said: Krishna, I wish to know the truth about renunciation and about relinquishment, and how they differ.
lifeNote: The last chapter begins with a request for clarity. Ask your own final questions.
actions: Write down your biggest remaining question about life.
Ask what 'letting go' means to you.
Read the summary of the Gita in chapter 18.

sanskrit: काम्यानां कर्मणां न्यासं संन्यासं कवयो विदुः ।
iast: kāmyānāṁ karmaṇāṁ nyāsaṁ saṁnyāsaṁ kavayo viduḥ · sarvakarmaphalatyāgaṁ prāhustyāgaṁ vicakṣaṇāḥ
meaning: Krishna said: The wise understand renunciation as giving up actions driven by desire. The discerning call giving up the fruit of all actions relinquishment.
lifeNote: Drop selfish actions, and drop clinging to results. Two kinds of letting go.
words: giving up the fruit of all actions
actions: Give up one desire-driven activity this week.
Do one duty and let go of its result.
Reflect on which kind of letting go you need.

iast: tyājyaṁ doṣavadityeke karma prāhurmanīṣiṇaḥ · yajñadānatapaḥkarma na tyājyamiti cāpare
meaning: Some thinkers say all action should be given up as faulty. Others say acts of sacrifice, charity and austerity should never be given up.
lifeNote: Wise people disagree. Listen to both sides before deciding.
words: acts of sacrifice, charity and austerity
actions: Hear both sides of one debate fully.
Don't drop good practices just because they're imperfect.
Keep one act of charity going.

sanskrit: निश्चयं शृणु मे तत्र त्यागे भरतसत्तम ।
iast: niścayaṁ śṛṇu me tatra tyāge bharatasattama · tyāgo hi puruṣavyāghra trividhaḥ saṁprakīrtitaḥ
meaning: Hear my conclusion on relinquishment, best of the Bharatas. Relinquishment is declared to be of three kinds, tiger among men.
lifeNote: Even letting go comes in kinds. Know which one you're practising.
actions: Notice the motive behind one thing you gave up.
Ask whether you let go out of wisdom, fear or laziness.
Listen to a teacher's final word on a topic.

iast: yajñadānatapaḥkarma na tyājyaṁ kāryameva tat · yajño dānaṁ tapaścaiva pāvanāni manīṣiṇām
meaning: Acts of sacrifice, charity and austerity should not be given up; they should be done. Sacrifice, charity and austerity purify even the wise.
lifeNote: Keep giving, serving and practising discipline. They keep you clean inside.
words: acts of sacrifice, charity and austerity
actions: Do one act of service today.
Give something this week.
Keep one discipline you've been neglecting.

sanskrit: एतान्यपि तु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा फलानि च ।
iast: etānyapi tu karmāṇi saṅgaṁ tyaktvā phalāni ca · kartavyānīti me pārtha niścitaṁ matamuttamam
meaning: But even these actions should be done without attachment and without desire for their results. This is my definite and best view, Arjuna.
lifeNote: Do good, and let go of how it turns out.
actions: Do one good deed and forget it.
Give without checking how it's used.
Serve without needing recognition.

iast: niyatasya tu saṁnyāsaḥ karmaṇo nopapadyate · mohāttasya parityāgastāmasaḥ parikīrtitaḥ
meaning: Giving up one's duty is not proper. Abandoning it out of delusion is declared to be of inertia.
lifeNote: Dropping your responsibilities out of confusion is not freedom.
actions: Take back one responsibility you've been avoiding.
Check whether your 'letting go' is really escape.
Do your duty even when confused.

sanskrit: स कृत्वा राजसं त्यागं नैव त्यागफलं लभेत् ॥
iast: duḥkhamityeva yatkarma kāyakleśabhayāttyajet · sa kṛtvā rājasaṁ tyāgaṁ naiva tyāgaphalaṁ labhet
meaning: One who gives up a duty because it is painful or out of fear of bodily discomfort practises relinquishment of passion and does not gain its fruit.
lifeNote: Quitting because it's hard isn't detachment; it's avoidance.
actions: Do one uncomfortable task you've avoided.
Notice when 'I'm letting go' means 'it's hard'.
Push through discomfort for one small goal.

sanskrit: सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा फलं चैव स त्यागः सात्त्विको मतः ॥
iast: kāryamityeva yatkarma niyataṁ kriyate'rjuna · saṅgaṁ tyaktvā phalaṁ caiva sa tyāgaḥ sāttviko mataḥ
meaning: When a prescribed duty is done simply because it ought to be done, giving up attachment and its fruit, that relinquishment is considered of goodness, Arjuna.
lifeNote: Do it because it's right, without clinging. That's the best kind of letting go.
actions: Do one duty today 'because it should be done'.
Release attachment to praise for it.
Notice how light work feels this way.

iast: na dveṣṭyakuśalaṁ karma kuśale nānuṣajjate · tyāgī sattvasamāviṣṭo medhāvī chinnasaṁśayaḥ
meaning: The relinquisher, filled with goodness, intelligent and free of doubt, neither hates disagreeable work nor clings to agreeable work.
lifeNote: Don't hate the boring tasks or cling to the fun ones. Do both well.
actions: Do a disliked task without complaining.
Don't over-indulge in a favourite task.
Treat all work as worth doing well.

sanskrit: न हि देहभृता शक्यं त्यक्तुं कर्माण्यशेषतः ।
iast: na hi dehabhṛtā śakyaṁ tyaktuṁ karmāṇyaśeṣataḥ · yastu karmaphalatyāgī sa tyāgītyabhidhīyate
meaning: It is impossible for an embodied being to give up action entirely. But one who gives up the fruit of action is called a true relinquisher.
lifeNote: You can't stop acting while you're alive. You can stop clinging.
words: gives up the fruit of action
actions: Accept that action is unavoidable today.
Let go of the result of one effort.
Stop waiting for a 'quiet time' to be spiritual.
