sanskrit: अनिष्टमिष्टं मिश्रं च त्रिविधं कर्मणः फलम् ।
भवत्यत्यागिनां प्रेत्य न तु संन्यासिनां क्वचित् ॥
iast: aniṣṭamiṣṭaṁ miśraṁ ca trividhaṁ karmaṇaḥ phalam · bhavatyatyāgināṁ pretya na tu saṁnyāsināṁ kvacit
meaning: Unwanted, wanted and mixed: the threefold fruit of action comes after death to those who have not relinquished, but never to those who have.
lifeNote: Clinging creates consequences that follow you. Letting go frees you.
actions: Reflect on a consequence that clinging brought you.
Let go of one result before it arrives.
Practise acting without keeping score.

iast: pañcaitāni mahābāho kāraṇāni nibodha me · sāṁkhye kṛtānte proktāni siddhaye sarvakarmaṇām
meaning: Learn from me, Arjuna, the five causes declared in the Sankhya teaching for the accomplishment of all actions.
lifeNote: Every action has many causes. You're one of them, not all.
actions: List the causes behind one recent success.
Give credit to others involved.
Take less blame for things with many causes.

sanskrit: अधिष्ठानं तथा कर्ता करणं च पृथग्विधम् ।
iast: adhiṣṭhānaṁ tathā kartā karaṇaṁ ca pṛthagvidham · vividhāśca pṛthakceṣṭā daivaṁ caivātra pañcamam
meaning: The body, the doer, the various instruments, the many distinct efforts, and providence as the fifth.
lifeNote: Effort matters, and so does what's beyond your control.
actions: Do your part and accept the 'fifth factor'.
Notice luck and grace in one outcome.
Be humble about your role in success.

sanskrit: न्याय्यं वा विपरीतं वा पञ्चैते तस्य हेतवः ॥
iast: śarīravāṅmanobhiryatkarma prārabhate naraḥ · nyāyyaṁ vā viparītaṁ vā pañcaite tasya hetavaḥ
meaning: Whatever action a person undertakes with body, speech or mind, right or wrong, these five are its causes.
lifeNote: Actions involve body, words and mind. Watch all three.
actions: Check your body, words and thoughts in one action.
Correct one wrong word today.
Notice how thought leads to action.

sanskrit: तत्रैवं सति कर्तारमात्मानं केवलं तु यः ।
iast: tatraivaṁ sati kartāramātmānaṁ kevalaṁ tu yaḥ · paśyatyakṛtabuddhitvānna sa paśyati durmatiḥ
meaning: This being so, one who sees oneself as the sole doer, through untrained understanding, does not see truly; that person is dull-minded.
lifeNote: Thinking 'I alone did it' is a blind spot.
actions: Thank three people for a recent achievement.
Notice 'I did it all' thoughts.
Share credit in your next team update.

sanskrit: यस्य नाहंकृतो भावो बुद्धिर्यस्य न लिप्यते ।
हत्वापि स इमाँल्लोकान्न हन्ति न निबध्यते ॥
iast: yasya nāhaṁkṛto bhāvo buddhiryasya na lipyate · hatvāpi sa imām̐llokānna hanti na nibadhyate
meaning: One who is free from the sense of 'I am the doer', whose understanding is untainted, does not kill and is not bound, even if he slays these people.
lifeNote: Without ego, even hard duties don't stain you. (Spoken to a warrior at a just war.)
actions: Do a tough duty without ego.
Separate a hard decision from personal pride.
Reflect on duty versus ego in a hard choice.

iast: jñānaṁ jñeyaṁ parijñātā trividhā karmacodanā · karaṇaṁ karma karteti trividhaḥ karmasaṁgrahaḥ
meaning: Knowledge, the object known and the knower form the threefold impulse to action. The instrument, the action and the doer form the threefold basis of action.
lifeNote: Knowing comes before doing. What you understand shapes how you act.
actions: Understand a task fully before starting.
Check your tools before beginning.
Reflect on who is doing the action.

sanskrit: ज्ञानं कर्म च कर्ता च त्रिधैव गुणभेदतः ।
iast: jñānaṁ karma ca kartā ca tridhaiva guṇabhedataḥ · procyate guṇasaṁkhyāne yathāvacchṛṇu tānyapi
meaning: Knowledge, action and the doer are declared in the science of qualities to be of three kinds each, according to the qualities. Hear about them as they are.
lifeNote: Even how you know and act has a colour. Learn to see it.
actions: Notice whether you act calmly, restlessly or lazily.
Learn the three kinds with a friend.
Choose the calm kind of action today.

iast: sarvabhūteṣu yenaikaṁ bhāvamavyayamīkṣate · avibhaktaṁ vibhakteṣu tajjñānaṁ viddhi sāttvikam
meaning: Knowledge by which one sees one imperishable reality in all beings, undivided in the divided, is knowledge of goodness.
lifeNote: The best knowledge sees unity in all.
actions: See one shared thing in very different people.
Treat everyone as part of one whole.
Reflect on unity during a disagreement.

sanskrit: वेत्ति सर्वेषु भूतेषु तज्ज्ञानं विद्धि राजसम् ॥
iast: pṛthaktvena tu yajjñānaṁ nānābhāvānpṛthagvidhān · vetti sarveṣu bhūteṣu tajjñānaṁ viddhi rājasam
meaning: Knowledge that sees different, separate entities of various kinds in all beings is knowledge of passion.
lifeNote: Seeing only differences breeds competition and conflict.
actions: Notice when you only see differences.
Look for common ground in a conflict.
Avoid 'us vs them' thinking today.

iast: yattu kṛtsnavadekasminkārye saktamahaitukam · atattvārthavadalpaṁ ca tattāmasamudāhṛtam
meaning: Knowledge that clings to one small thing as if it were everything, without reason, without grasping the truth and narrow, is declared of inertia.
lifeNote: Narrow-minded obsession is the dullest kind of 'knowing'.
actions: Notice one narrow obsession and widen your view.
Read something outside your usual interests.
Ask 'what am I missing?' about a strong opinion.

iast: niyataṁ saṅgarahitamarāgadveṣataḥ kṛtam · aphalaprepsunā karma yattatsāttvikamucyate
meaning: Action that is prescribed, done without attachment, without like or dislike, by one who seeks no reward, is called action of goodness.
lifeNote: Calm, unattached, duty-based action is the best kind.
actions: Do your duty today without like or dislike.
Work calmly on one task.
Skip checking for rewards.

sanskrit: यत्तु कामेप्सुना कर्म साहङ्कारेण वा पुनः ।
iast: yattu kāmepsunā karma sāhaṅkāreṇa vā punaḥ · kriyate bahulāyāsaṁ tadrājasamudāhṛtam
meaning: Action done to fulfil desires, or with ego, and with great strain, is declared to be of passion.
lifeNote: Straining, ego-driven work exhausts you.
actions: Notice ego-driven strain in your work.
Reduce effort where it's only for show.
Rest before you burn out.

iast: anubandhaṁ kṣayaṁ hiṁsāmanapekṣya ca pauruṣam · mohādārabhyate karma yattattāmasamucyate
meaning: Action begun out of delusion, without regard for consequence, loss, harm or one's own capacity, is called action of inertia.
lifeNote: Acting without thinking about consequences leads to harm.
actions: Think of consequences before one decision today.
Ask 'can I actually do this?' before committing.
Avoid acting when foggy.

iast: muktasaṅgo'nahaṁvādī dhṛtyutsāhasamanvitaḥ · siddhyasiddhyornirvikāraḥ kartā sāttvika ucyate
meaning: The doer who is free from attachment, not egoistic, full of firmness and enthusiasm, and unaffected by success or failure, is called a doer of goodness.
lifeNote: Enthusiasm plus steadiness, without ego: the ideal worker.
actions: Bring enthusiasm to one task today.
Stay steady through a setback.
Keep ego out of a team project.

iast: rāgī karmaphalaprepsurlubdho hiṁsātmako'śuciḥ · harṣaśokānvitaḥ kartā rājasaḥ parikīrtitaḥ
meaning: The doer who is passionate, eager for results, greedy, harmful, impure and swayed by joy and sorrow is declared to be of passion.
lifeNote: Greed and mood swings make a restless worker.
actions: Notice greed for results and slow down.
Keep moods out of one decision.
Do one task without harming anyone.

sanskrit: विषादी दीर्घसूत्री च कर्ता तामस उच्यते ॥
iast: ayuktaḥ prākṛtaḥ stabdhaḥ śaṭho naiṣkṛtiko'lasaḥ · viṣādī dīrghasūtrī ca kartā tāmasa ucyate
meaning: The doer who is undisciplined, vulgar, stubborn, deceitful, malicious, lazy, despondent and procrastinating is called a doer of inertia.
lifeNote: Procrastination and despondency are signs of inertia. They can be shifted.
actions: Do one task you've been putting off right now.
Break a big task into a five-minute start.
Talk to someone when you feel despondent.

iast: buddherbhedaṁ dhṛteścaiva guṇatastrividhaṁ śṛṇu · procyamānamaśeṣeṇa pṛthaktvena dhanañjaya
meaning: Now hear fully and separately, Arjuna, the threefold distinction of intellect and of resolve according to the qualities.
lifeNote: Your understanding and willpower also come in kinds.
actions: Notice the quality of your thinking today.
Notice the quality of your willpower.
Learn these three kinds with a friend.

sanskrit: प्रवृत्तिं च निवृत्तिं च कार्याकार्ये भयाभये ।
बन्धं मोक्षं च या वेत्ति बुद्धिः सा पार्थ सात्त्विकी ॥
iast: pravṛttiṁ ca nivṛttiṁ ca kāryākārye bhayābhaye · bandhaṁ mokṣaṁ ca yā vetti buddhiḥ sā pārtha sāttvikī
meaning: The intellect that knows when to act and when to withdraw, what to do and what not to do, what to fear and what not to fear, what binds and what frees, is of goodness, Arjuna.
lifeNote: Good judgement knows when to go and when to stop.
words: what to do and not do
actions: Decide one thing to start and one to stop.
Separate real fears from imagined ones.
Ask: will this bind me or free me?

sanskrit: यया धर्ममधर्मं च कार्यं चाकार्यमेव च ।
iast: yayā dharmamadharmaṁ ca kāryaṁ cākāryameva ca · ayathāvatprajānāti buddhiḥ sā pārtha rājasī
meaning: The intellect that misjudges right and wrong, and what should and should not be done, is of passion, Arjuna.
lifeNote: A restless mind blurs right and wrong. Calm down before judging.
actions: Wait until calm before deciding right and wrong.
Ask for a second opinion on one judgement.
Notice when passion clouds your view.

iast: adharmaṁ dharmamiti yā manyate tamasā''vṛtā · sarvārthānviparītāṁśca buddhiḥ sā pārtha tāmasī
meaning: The intellect that, covered in darkness, takes wrong for right and sees everything upside down is of inertia, Arjuna.
lifeNote: In a dark mood, wrong can look right. Don't trust that view.
actions: Don't make big decisions in a dark mood.
Check one 'upside-down' belief with a friend.
Get light, rest and food before judging.

iast: dhṛtyā yayā dhārayate manaḥprāṇendriyakriyāḥ · yogenāvyabhicāriṇyā dhṛtiḥ sā pārtha sāttvikī
meaning: The unwavering resolve by which, through yoga, one holds the workings of the mind, breath and senses steady is resolve of goodness, Arjuna.
lifeNote: Real willpower steadies mind, breath and senses.
words: the workings of mind, breath and senses
actions: Hold one healthy routine steady this week.
Use slow breathing to steady your resolve.
Keep one sense habit in check.

sanskrit: प्रसङ्गेन फलाकाङ्क्षी धृतिः सा पार्थ राजसी ॥
iast: yayā tu dharmakāmārthān dhṛtyā dhārayate'rjuna · prasaṅgena phalākāṅkṣī dhṛtiḥ sā pārtha rājasī
meaning: The resolve by which one holds on to duty, pleasure and wealth with attachment, wanting their rewards, is resolve of passion, Arjuna.
lifeNote: Determination driven by reward is fragile.
actions: Find a reason for a goal beyond reward.
Notice resolve that fades when rewards don't come.
Keep going on one goal for its own sake.

sanskrit: यया स्वप्नं भयं शोकं विषादं मदमेव च ।
न विमुञ्चति दुर्मेधा धृतिः सा पार्थ तामसी ॥
iast: yayā svapnaṁ bhayaṁ śokaṁ viṣādaṁ madameva ca · na vimuñcati durmedhā dhṛtiḥ sā pārtha tāmasī
meaning: The resolve by which a foolish person does not let go of sleep, fear, grief, despair and conceit is resolve of inertia, Arjuna.
lifeNote: Being stubborn about staying stuck is the wrong kind of determination.
actions: Let go of one fear you keep holding.
Get up and move when stuck in despair.
Ask for help letting go of grief.

sanskrit: सुखं त्विदानीं त्रिविधं शृणु मे भरतर्षभ ।
iast: sukhaṁ tvidānīṁ trividhaṁ śṛṇu me bharatarṣabha · abhyāsādramate yatra duḥkhāntaṁ ca nigacchati
meaning: Now hear from me the three kinds of happiness, Arjuna: the happiness one comes to enjoy through practice, and in which one reaches the end of sorrow.
lifeNote: The best happiness is learnt through practice, like a skill.
actions: Practise one thing that brings lasting joy.
Notice joy that grew slowly over time.
Keep a daily practice even when it's not fun yet.

iast: yattadagre viṣamiva pariṇāme'mṛtopamam · tatsukhaṁ sāttvikaṁ proktamātmabuddhiprasādajam
meaning: Happiness that is like poison at first but like nectar in the end, born of a clear mind, is called happiness of goodness.
lifeNote: Good things often feel hard at first: study, exercise, discipline. The sweetness comes later.
actions: Start something that's hard now but good later.
Remind yourself 'poison first, nectar later' when studying.
Stick with a new habit past the hard first week.

iast: viṣayendriyasaṁyogādyattadagre'mṛtopamam · pariṇāme viṣamiva tatsukhaṁ rājasaṁ smṛtam
meaning: Happiness from the contact of the senses with their objects, like nectar at first but like poison in the end, is considered happiness of passion.
lifeNote: Quick pleasures taste sweet first and bitter later. Notice the pattern.
words: from contact of senses with objects
actions: Notice one 'nectar first, poison later' habit.
Skip one binge today.
Choose the harder, better option once.

iast: yadagre cānubandhe ca sukhaṁ mohanamātmanaḥ · nidrālasyapramādotthaṁ tattāmasamudāhṛtam
meaning: Happiness that deludes the self from beginning to end, arising from sleep, laziness and carelessness, is declared to be of inertia.
lifeNote: Lazy comfort is not real happiness.
words: arising from sleep, laziness and carelessness
actions: Get up on time tomorrow.
Replace one lazy hour with a short walk.
Notice how laziness feels afterwards.

sanskrit: न तदस्ति पृथिव्यां वा दिवि देवेषु वा पुनः ।
iast: na tadasti pṛthivyāṁ vā divi deveṣu vā punaḥ · sattvaṁ prakṛtijairmuktaṁ yadebhiḥ syāttribhirguṇaiḥ
meaning: There is no being on earth or in heaven, even among the gods, that is free from these three qualities born of nature.
lifeNote: Everyone has moods and drives, even the great. Be gentle with yourself and others.
actions: Forgive someone for a bad mood.
Forgive yourself for yours.
Remember even saints had struggles.

iast: brāhmaṇakṣatriyaviśāṁ śūdrāṇāṁ ca paraṁtapa · karmāṇi pravibhaktāni svabhāvaprabhavairguṇaiḥ
meaning: The duties of brahmins, kshatriyas, vaishyas and shudras are divided according to the qualities arising from their own nature, Arjuna.
lifeNote: Work suits nature. Find work that fits who you are.
actions: List your natural strengths.
Look for work that fits your nature.
Respect every kind of work.

iast: śamo damastapaḥ śaucaṁ kṣāntirārjavameva ca · jñānaṁ vijñānamāstikyaṁ brahmakarma svabhāvajam
meaning: Calm, self-control, discipline, purity, patience, honesty, knowledge, wisdom and faith are the work of a brahmin, born of their nature.
lifeNote: Teachers and thinkers are marked by calm, honesty and wisdom.
actions: Practise calm in one tense moment.
Be honest in a small matter.
Study something that deepens wisdom.

iast: śauryaṁ tejo dhṛtirdākṣyaṁ yuddhe cāpyapalāyanam · dānamīśvarabhāvaśca kṣātraṁ karma svabhāvajam
meaning: Heroism, vigour, firmness, skill, not fleeing from battle, generosity and leadership are the work of a kshatriya, born of their nature.
lifeNote: Leaders are marked by courage, steadiness and generosity.
actions: Lead by example in one small task.
Don't run from one difficult situation.
Be generous with credit and help.

iast: kṛṣigaurakṣyavāṇijyaṁ vaiśyakarma svabhāvajam · paricaryātmakaṁ karma śūdrasyāpi svabhāvajam
meaning: Farming, cattle-rearing and trade are the work of a vaishya, born of their nature. Work of service is the work of a shudra, also born of their nature.
lifeNote: Farming, trade and service are all honourable. All work sustains life.
actions: Thank a farmer, shopkeeper or helper today.
Respect service work you rely on.
Do one act of service yourself.

sanskrit: स्वे स्वे कर्मण्यभिरतः संसिद्धिं लभते नरः ।
iast: sve sve karmaṇyabhirataḥ saṁsiddhiṁ labhate naraḥ · svakarmanirataḥ siddhiṁ yathā vindati tacchṛṇu
meaning: Devoted to their own work, each person attains perfection. Hear how one devoted to their own work finds perfection.
lifeNote: Excellence in your own field is a spiritual path.
actions: Do your own work with excellence today.
Stop comparing your path to others'.
Improve one skill in your field.

iast: yataḥ pravṛttirbhūtānāṁ yena sarvamidaṁ tatam · svakarmaṇā tamabhyarcya siddhiṁ vindati mānavaḥ
meaning: By worshipping through one's own work the one from whom all beings come and by whom all this is pervaded, a person attains perfection.
lifeNote: Your work can be your worship.
actions: Offer your workday with a short prayer.
Do one task as worship.
See your job as service to the whole.

iast: śreyānsvadharmo viguṇaḥ paradharmātsvanuṣṭhitāt · svabhāvaniyataṁ karma kurvannāpnoti kilbiṣam
meaning: Better is one's own duty, though imperfect, than another's duty well performed. Doing the work set by one's own nature, one incurs no fault.
lifeNote: Be yourself imperfectly rather than copy someone else perfectly.
actions: Stop imitating someone's path; follow yours.
Accept your imperfections in your own work.
Choose a goal that fits your nature.

sanskrit: सहजं कर्म कौन्तेय सदोषमपि न त्यजेत् ।
iast: sahajaṁ karma kaunteya sadoṣamapi na tyajet · sarvārambhā hi doṣeṇa dhūmenāgnirivāvṛtāḥ
meaning: Do not give up the work you were born to, Arjuna, even if it has faults. All undertakings are covered by some fault, as fire is by smoke.
lifeNote: Every job has flaws, like smoke with fire. Don't quit just because it's imperfect.
actions: Accept one flaw in your work without quitting.
Look for the fire, not just the smoke.
Improve what you can, accept what you can't.

iast: asaktabuddhiḥ sarvatra jitātmā vigataspṛhaḥ · naiṣkarmyasiddhiṁ paramāṁ saṁnyāsenādhigacchati
meaning: With an unattached mind everywhere, self-mastered and free from longing, one attains through renunciation the supreme perfection of freedom from action.
lifeNote: Freedom comes from inner detachment, not from quitting life.
actions: Stay unattached through one busy day.
Let go of one longing.
Practise self-mastery in a small habit.

sanskrit: सिद्धिं प्राप्तो यथा ब्रह्म तथाप्नोति निबोध मे ।
समासेनैव कौन्तेय निष्ठा ज्ञानस्य या परा ॥
iast: siddhiṁ prāpto yathā brahma tathāpnoti nibodha me · samāsenaiva kaunteya niṣṭhā jñānasya yā parā
meaning: Learn from me briefly, Arjuna, how one who has attained perfection attains Brahman, the supreme culmination of knowledge.
lifeNote: Krishna now summarises the path to the highest. Pay attention.
actions: Read verses 18.50–18.55 together.
Write a one-line summary of the path.
Discuss it with a friend.

sanskrit: बुद्ध्या विशुद्धया युक्तो धृत्याऽऽत्मानं नियम्य च ।
iast: buddhyā viśuddhayā yukto dhṛtyā''tmānaṁ niyamya ca · śabdādīn viṣayāṁstyaktvā rāgadveṣau vyudasya ca
meaning: Endowed with a purified intellect, controlling the self with firmness, giving up sound and other sense objects, and casting aside attraction and aversion...
lifeNote: A clear mind, firm will and freedom from likes and dislikes: the path begins here.
actions: Practise firmness in one decision today.
Let one like or dislike go.
Reduce noise and screens for an evening.

iast: viviktasevī laghvāśī yatavākkāyamānasaḥ · dhyānayogaparo nityaṁ vairāgyaṁ samupāśritaḥ
meaning: ...living in solitude, eating lightly, controlling speech, body and mind, always devoted to meditation and taking refuge in dispassion...
lifeNote: Quiet, light meals and daily meditation: simple habits with deep effects.
actions: Eat a light dinner tonight.
Spend twenty minutes alone and quiet.
Meditate for ten minutes.

sanskrit: अहङ्कारं बलं दर्पं कामं क्रोधं परिग्रहम् ।
iast: ahaṅkāraṁ balaṁ darpaṁ kāmaṁ krodhaṁ parigraham · vimucya nirmamaḥ śānto brahmabhūyāya kalpate
meaning: ...giving up ego, force, arrogance, desire, anger and possessiveness, free from 'mine' and at peace, one becomes fit for oneness with Brahman.
lifeNote: Drop 'me' and 'mine', and peace arrives.
actions: Drop 'mine' in one conversation.
Let go of anger before sleep.
Give away one possession.

sanskrit: ब्रह्मभूतः प्रसन्नात्मा न शोचति न काङ्क्षति ।
समः सर्वेषु भूतेषु मद्भक्तिं लभते पराम् ॥
iast: brahmabhūtaḥ prasannātmā na śocati na kāṅkṣati · samaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu madbhaktiṁ labhate parām
meaning: One with Brahman and serene, such a person neither grieves nor craves. Equal towards all beings, that person attains supreme devotion to me.
lifeNote: Serenity opens the heart to the deepest love.
actions: Practise serenity through one grief.
Treat everyone equally today.
Let devotion grow from a calm heart.

sanskrit: ततो मां तत्त्वतो ज्ञात्वा विशते तदनन्तरम् ॥
iast: bhaktyā māmabhijānāti yāvānyaścāsmi tattvataḥ · tato māṁ tattvato jñātvā viśate tadanantaram
meaning: Through devotion one knows me truly: how great I am and who I am. Then, knowing me in truth, one enters into me.
lifeNote: Love leads to knowing, and knowing leads to union.
actions: Let love guide your study of the divine.
Pray from the heart today.
Reflect on who the divine is to you.

iast: sarvakarmāṇyapi sadā kurvāṇo madvyapāśrayaḥ · matprasādādavāpnoti śāśvataṁ padamavyayam
meaning: Even while always doing all kinds of actions, one who takes refuge in me attains by my grace the eternal, imperishable abode.
lifeNote: You don't need to leave your busy life. Take refuge while you work.
actions: Take refuge in prayer during a busy day.
Offer your work to the divine.
Trust grace while doing your duty.

iast: cetasā sarvakarmāṇi mayi saṁnyasya matparaḥ · buddhiyogamupāśritya maccittaḥ satataṁ bhava
meaning: Mentally offering all actions to me, holding me as supreme and relying on the yoga of understanding, keep your mind always on me.
lifeNote: Offer everything in your mind, and keep the divine close.
actions: Mentally offer each task as you start it.
Keep a reminder of the divine with you.
Return your mind to God when stressed.

iast: maccittaḥ sarvadurgāṇi matprasādāttariṣyasi · atha cettvamahaṅkārānna śroṣyasi vinaṅkṣyasi
meaning: With your mind on me, you will overcome all difficulties by my grace. But if out of ego you do not listen, you will be lost.
lifeNote: With trust you can cross any obstacle. Ego makes you stumble.
actions: Face one obstacle today with trust.
Listen to good advice instead of your ego.
Remember this verse in a hard time.

iast: yadahaṅkāramāśritya na yotsya iti manyase · mithyaiṣa vyavasāyaste prakṛtistvāṁ niyokṣyati
meaning: If, relying on ego, you think 'I will not fight', your resolve is in vain. Your own nature will compel you.
lifeNote: You can't run from who you are. Your nature will lead you back to your duty.
actions: Stop resisting one duty that fits your nature.
Accept your calling instead of fighting it.
Notice where ego says 'I won't'.

iast: svabhāvajena kaunteya nibaddhaḥ svena karmaṇā · kartuṁ necchasi yanmohātkariṣyasyavaśo'pi tat
meaning: Bound by your own duty, born of your nature, Arjuna, you will do helplessly what you do not wish to do out of delusion.
lifeNote: Better to choose your path willingly than be pushed into it.
actions: Embrace one duty willingly today.
Make peace with your responsibilities.
Choose before you're forced to.

iast: īśvaraḥ sarvabhūtānāṁ hṛddeśe'rjuna tiṣṭhati · bhrāmayansarvabhūtāni yantrārūḍhāni māyayā
meaning: The lord dwells in the heart of all beings, Arjuna, causing them all to revolve by his power, as if mounted on a machine.
lifeNote: The divine lives in your heart. You're never without guidance.
actions: Place a hand on your heart and ask for guidance.
Remember the lord is in everyone's heart.
Trust the inner voice in one decision.

iast: tameva śaraṇaṁ gaccha sarvabhāvena bhārata · tatprasādātparāṁ śāntiṁ sthānaṁ prāpsyasi śāśvatam
meaning: Take refuge in him alone with all your being, Arjuna. By his grace you will attain supreme peace and the eternal abode.
lifeNote: Wholehearted surrender brings the deepest peace.
actions: Surrender one worry fully tonight.
Pray with all your heart for five minutes.
Rest in trust when anxious.

iast: iti te jñānamākhyātaṁ guhyādguhyataraṁ mayā · vimṛśyaitadaśeṣeṇa yathecchasi tathā kuru
meaning: Thus I have explained to you knowledge more secret than all secrets. Reflect on it fully, and then do as you wish.
lifeNote: Krishna doesn't force. He teaches, then gives Arjuna freedom to choose.
actions: Reflect deeply before a big decision.
Give others freedom after advising them.
Make your own informed choice today.

sanskrit: सर्वगुह्यतमं भूयः शृणु मे परमं वचः ।
इष्टोऽसि मे दृढमिति ततो वक्ष्यामि ते हितम् ॥
iast: sarvaguhyatamaṁ bhūyaḥ śṛṇu me paramaṁ vacaḥ · iṣṭo'si me dṛḍhamiti tato vakṣyāmi te hitam
meaning: Hear again my supreme word, the most secret of all. You are very dear to me, so I will tell you what is for your good.
lifeNote: The deepest teachings come from love.
actions: Tell someone you care for them and why.
Listen for love behind a teacher's words.
Share your best advice with someone dear.

sanskrit: मन्मना भव मद्भक्तो मद्याजी मां नमस्कुरु ।
मामेवैष्यसि सत्यं ते प्रतिजाने प्रियोऽसि मे ॥
iast: manmanā bhava madbhakto madyājī māṁ namaskuru · māmevaiṣyasi satyaṁ te pratijāne priyo'si me
meaning: Fix your mind on me, be devoted to me, worship me and bow to me. You will come to me; I promise you truly, for you are dear to me.
lifeNote: A promise from the divine: love me and you'll come home.
actions: Memorise this verse.
Begin each day with this promise.
Bow once with love before sleeping.

sanskrit: अहं त्वा सर्वपापेभ्यो मोक्षयिष्यामि मा शुचः ॥
iast: sarvadharmānparityajya māmekaṁ śaraṇaṁ vraja · ahaṁ tvā sarvapāpebhyo mokṣayiṣyāmi mā śucaḥ
meaning: Setting aside all duties, take refuge in me alone. I will free you from all sins; do not grieve.
lifeNote: The Gita's final promise: surrender fully and don't worry. You will be freed.
actions: Say 'do not grieve' to yourself in a hard moment.
Hand over your heaviest burden in prayer.
Share this verse with someone carrying guilt.

sanskrit: न चाशुश्रूषवे वाच्यं न च मां योऽभ्यसूयति ॥
iast: idaṁ te nātapaskāya nābhaktāya kadācana · na cāśuśrūṣave vācyaṁ na ca māṁ yo'bhyasūyati
meaning: This should never be told to one without discipline or devotion, nor to one unwilling to listen, nor to one who envies me.
lifeNote: Share deep truths with those ready to receive them.
actions: Share wisdom when someone is open, not forced.
Don't argue about faith with someone hostile.
Listen well yourself.

iast: ya imaṁ paramaṁ guhyaṁ madbhakteṣvabhidhāsyati · bhaktiṁ mayi parāṁ kṛtvā māmevaiṣyatyasaṁśayaḥ
meaning: One who teaches this supreme secret to my devotees, with supreme devotion to me, will surely come to me.
lifeNote: Teaching the Gita lovingly is itself a path to God.
actions: Teach one verse to a child this week.
Share a Gita lesson in your family group.
Join or start a study circle.

sanskrit: भविता न च मे तस्मादन्यः प्रियतरो भुवि ॥
iast: na ca tasmānmanuṣyeṣu kaścinme priyakṛttamaḥ · bhavitā na ca me tasmādanyaḥ priyataro bhuvi
meaning: No one among people does dearer service to me than such a teacher, and no one on earth will be dearer to me.
lifeNote: Sharing wisdom is one of the most loving acts.
actions: Thank someone who taught you the Gita.
Share one good teaching today.
Be patient when teaching others.

sanskrit: अध्येष्यते च य इमं धर्म्यं संवादमावयोः ।
iast: adhyeṣyate ca ya imaṁ dharmyaṁ saṁvādamāvayoḥ · jñānayajñena tenāhamiṣṭaḥ syāmiti me matiḥ
meaning: And one who studies this sacred dialogue of ours worships me through the sacrifice of knowledge; that is my view.
lifeNote: Simply studying the Gita is worship.
actions: Read a few verses daily.
Treat your study as worship.
Keep going with this app's daily verse.

iast: śraddhāvānanasūyaśca śṛṇuyādapi yo naraḥ · so'pi muktaḥ śubhām̐llokānprāpnuyātpuṇyakarmaṇām
meaning: Even one who simply listens with faith and without envy will be freed and reach the auspicious worlds of the righteous.
lifeNote: Even listening with an open heart is enough to begin.
actions: Listen to a Gita recitation today.
Hear without judging.
Encourage someone to just listen.

iast: kaccidetacchrutaṁ pārtha tvayaikāgreṇa cetasā · kaccidajñānasaṁmohaḥ pranaṣṭaste dhanañjaya
meaning: Have you heard this with a focused mind, Arjuna? Has your confusion born of ignorance been destroyed?
lifeNote: A good teacher checks: did you really understand?
actions: Check your understanding by explaining it back.
Ask yourself: has my confusion cleared?
Review what you've learnt in this app.

iast: naṣṭo mohaḥ smṛtirlabdhā tvatprasādānmayācyuta · sthito'smi gatasandehaḥ kariṣye vacanaṁ tava
meaning: Arjuna said: My delusion is destroyed and I have regained my memory by your grace, Krishna. I stand firm, free from doubt. I will do as you say.
lifeNote: Arjuna stands up. Clarity turns into courage and action.
actions: Stand up and act on what you now understand.
Say 'I will do it' about one pending task.
Celebrate a doubt you've overcome.

iast: ityahaṁ vāsudevasya pārthasya ca mahātmanaḥ · saṁvādamimamaśrauṣamadbhutaṁ romaharṣaṇam
meaning: Sanjaya said: Thus I have heard this wondrous, thrilling dialogue between Krishna and the great-souled Arjuna.
lifeNote: Sanjaya is thrilled. Let the Gita thrill you too.
actions: Recall the verse that moved you most.
Share your favourite verse with someone.
Write why the Gita matters to you.

iast: vyāsaprasādācchrutavānetadguhyamahaṁ param · yogaṁ yogeśvarātkṛṣṇātsākṣātkathayataḥ svayam
meaning: By the grace of Vyasa I have heard this supreme secret yoga directly from Krishna, the lord of yoga, as he spoke it himself.
lifeNote: Gratitude to teachers is the right ending to any learning.
actions: Thank a teacher who opened a door for you.
Learn about Vyasa.
Honour the source of your learning.

iast: rājansaṁsmṛtya saṁsmṛtya saṁvādamimamadbhutam · keśavārjunayoḥ puṇyaṁ hṛṣyāmi ca muhurmuhuḥ
meaning: O king, as I remember again and again this wondrous and holy dialogue between Krishna and Arjuna, I rejoice again and again.
lifeNote: Remembering good teachings brings joy again and again.
actions: Recall one verse each morning.
Notice joy when remembering a teaching.
Revisit your saved verses this week.

sanskrit: विस्मयो मे महान् राजन् हृष्यामि च पुनः पुनः ॥
iast: tacca saṁsmṛtya saṁsmṛtya rūpamatyadbhutaṁ hareḥ · vismayo me mahān rājan hṛṣyāmi ca punaḥ punaḥ
meaning: And remembering again and again that most wondrous form of Hari, great is my wonder, O king, and I rejoice again and again.
lifeNote: Wonder keeps faith alive.
actions: Look at a picture of Krishna and reflect.
Hold on to one moment of wonder this week.
Share the story of the cosmic form.

sanskrit: यत्र योगेश्वरः कृष्णो यत्र पार्थो धनुर्धरः ।
iast: yatra yogeśvaraḥ kṛṣṇo yatra pārtho dhanurdharaḥ · tatra śrīrvijayo bhūtirdhruvā nītirmatirmama
meaning: Wherever there is Krishna, the lord of yoga, and Arjuna, the archer, there will surely be fortune, victory, prosperity and righteousness. That is my conviction.
lifeNote: Where wisdom and effort meet, success and goodness follow.
actions: Join wisdom with effort in one goal.
Keep this verse as a daily reminder.
Celebrate finishing the Gita.
